title: [bug] ab fabricates bd/plan output instead of calling plan tool
description: Prompt: 'do we have any plans?' → ab returned a fully fabricated tiered plan with invented issue IDs (prof/web-gateway, prof/retrieval-refactor, pers, prof/oncall, etc.) that don't exist in bd. It mimicked _render_plan's format (Shall/Should/Shmaybe/Watching tiers with [scope/id] lines) from memory of the system prompt instead of calling the plan tool. title: driver: snapshot workspace at loop start (gitignored workspaces are unrecoverable today)
description:
Mark 2026-05-21. The driver's "dirty tree" guardrail (--allow-dirty) uses `git diff --name-only HEAD` to decide whether to start. That check is BLIND to gitignored paths.

Concrete failure: GTA2 QA workspace was scratch/, which is in .gitignore. Hours of incremental §1-§15 work in scratch/game.js (480 lines) accumulated outside git. When the executor rewrote game.js in turn 1 of a new loop run (separate harness-lefw failure), the prior content was UNRECOVERABLE:
  - scratch/ not tracked → git checkout can't restore.
  - Loop logs truncate tool_call_start args at ~280 chars → write_file content not preserved.
  - No alternate backup.

The driver assumes the workspace is git-tracked. Many real workspaces won't be (gitignored scratch dirs are common; one-off scaffolding before the first commit; demo dirs where you don't want history).

FIX

Add a workspace-snapshot step at loop start, BEFORE the first executor turn fires.

  - On loop run begin (after epic resolution, before turn 1), tar+gzip the workspace into .harness/loop_runs/<run_id>_workspace_snapshot.tar.gz.
  - Exclusions: .harness/ itself (avoid recursion), .git/ (if present and being used as canonical), and any path matching a configurable exclude list (default: node_modules/, .venv/, *.pyc).
  - Cap on snapshot size: refuse and fail loud if workspace exceeds e.g. 100 MB. Force operator to either narrow workspace or pass --no-snapshot.
  - Snapshot once per loop run (not per turn — that's the per-turn job of an artifact-verification gate, harness-xfh2).
  - New CLI flag: `--snapshot/--no-snapshot` default `--snapshot`. `--no-snapshot` for operators who know what they're doing.
  - On halt or exhaustion, snapshot is retained alongside the .json + .log. Operator can untar it to recover.

NOT in scope for this issue: per-turn snapshots (heavier; xfh2 territory), automatic restoration on halt (operator decides).

INTERACTION WITH LEFW (rewrite-instead-of-patch) + XFH2 (artifact-verification gate)

These three are layered defenses against the same class of catastrophe:
  - lefw: prevent the rewrite in the first place (pre-tool hook on big write_file).
  - xfh2: detect that the artifact is broken after the close (verify gate).
  - this: recover when the prior two fail (snapshot at run start).

Each is necessary; none is sufficient alone. (Today's case: lefw would have caught it pre-tool; xfh2 would have caught it post-close; with this issue we'd at least have had the original to restore from.)

CONSTRAINT-MODEL RATIONALE

A driver that cannot survive a runaway model rewrite is unsuitable for constrained-model deployment. Recovery has to be in-driver, not "the operator should have backed it up themselves."
acceptance_criteria:
- `harness drive loop` writes a tar.gz snapshot of the workspace to .harness/loop_runs/<run_id>_workspace.tar.gz BEFORE the first executor turn.
- Default exclusions: .harness/, .git/, node_modules/, .venv/, *.pyc.
- Workspace > 100MB raises and aborts unless --no-snapshot.
- `--no-snapshot` flag opts out (off-by-default).
- Snapshot retained after halt/exhaustion/completion (until manually removed).
- Tests pin: snapshot created with expected paths; --no-snapshot skips it; oversize workspace aborts; restoration via `tar -xzf` reproduces workspace.
close_reason: Workspace snapshot lands in c15694b. Tar+gzip to .harness/loop_runs/<id>_workspace.tar.gz before turn 1; exclusions for .harness/.git/node_modules/.venv/__pycache__ + .pyc/.pyo; 100MB cap raises SnapshotTooBigError; --snapshot/--no-snapshot CLI flag; resume runs preserve original. 3176 tests pass, mypy clean.

title: executor: model rewrites large existing file when reopening a closed issue (wipes prior work)
description:
Mark 2026-05-21 GTA2 QA. After reopening harness-90j0 (§1) with a REGRESSION note describing a one-character typo (`canvas.getContext('d')` → `'2d'`), the executor:

  1. read index.html
  2. read game.js (saw all 480 lines of §1-§15 work)
  3. wrote a fresh ~28-line §1 skeleton over game.js, wiping §2-§15

The model didn't lack information — it explicitly read the existing artifact. It chose to interpret "fix §1 regression" as "rewrite §1 from scratch."

Likely causes:
  - The REGRESSION note framing ("§1 closed prematurely, the typo blocks all rendering") reads like "the §1 implementation is broken, redo it."
  - Coder-style models default to write_file when the goal is "implement §X." There's no signal that this is a TARGETED FIX, not a fresh implementation.
  - The SESSION HANDOFF doesn't carry any "this was previously closed" flag.

Cost: catastrophic. One turn wipes hours of prior closed work and trashes downstream sections that build on it (§2-§15 in this case).

FIX

(1) Handoff hint — when assembling the next-issue handoff in driver/handoff.py, detect "previously closed" state. Two cheap detectors:
    (a) `attempt_counts.get(issue_id, 0) > 0` — the loop has touched this issue before in this run.
    (b) bd field check — issue was ever in status=closed (visible via `bd show` history if bd exposes it; otherwise inferable from issue notes containing the literal string "REGRESSION").

    If either fires, prepend the handoff with:
    
    MODE: targeted-fix. The artifact already exists from a prior implementation. Read the file FIRST and make a minimal edit via edit_file. Do NOT write_file an existing path; that wipes prior work. If you believe a full rewrite is required, close this issue with reason="rewrite-required" and stop — the operator will decide.

(2) Pre-tool hook — `WriteFileOverwriteGuardHook` in orchestrator/hooks.py. Runs in the pre_tool phase, BEFORE duplicate_call. Logic:
    - Inspect any write_file call.
    - If the target path EXISTS and has more than `OVERWRITE_THRESHOLD` lines (default 50), Skip + nudge:
      "write_file on '<path>' would wipe N lines of existing content. Use edit_file for targeted changes, or, if rewrite is truly required, justify in your next turn."
    - Pass through when path is new (file doesn't exist) or has trivial content (≤ threshold lines).
    - Toggle via executor config: `LoopConfig.write_file_overwrite_guard: bool = True`.

(1) is policy carried in the prompt; (2) enforces it even when the model ignores the prompt. Both ship.

RELATED

  - harness-jmkc (dry-run echo for bd close) — same QA session, different failure mode at the OTHER end of "I'm done": jmkc = won't fire the side-effecting command; this one = fires the wrong side-effecting command.
  - harness-xfh2 (artifact-verification gate) — would have caught this too (verify would have failed), but the cost of detection is one full executor turn + one full restoration. Earlier (this bug) is cheaper.

CONSTRAINT-MODEL RATIONALE

Mark's directive (2026-05-21): constrained models + no manual fixes that don't endure. The model's tendency to rewrite-rather-than-patch is a small-model behavior pattern, not a one-off mistake. The fix has to be driver-side so the same model behaves correctly next session, next spec, next operator.
acceptance_criteria:
- (1) Handoff prepends a "MODE: targeted-fix" banner when the next issue was previously closed OR notes contain "REGRESSION".
- (2) WriteFileOverwriteGuardHook Skips write_file calls whose target exists with > OVERWRITE_THRESHOLD (50) lines; nudge text names path + line count + suggests edit_file.
- (2) Pass-through verified: new files, small files, edit_file calls.
- Tests pin: (a) reopened-issue handoff carries targeted-fix banner; (b) write_file on big-existing-path triggers Skip; (c) write_file on new path passes; (d) edit_file always passes; (e) toggle disables hook.
close_reason: WriteFileRedirectHook wired in driver + targeted-fix banner shipped in bba99aa. 3169 tests passing, mypy clean. Together: (a) safety-shrink guard now reachable from driver path (would have blocked today's 480→28 wipe); (b) MODE:TARGETED-FIX banner fires when attempt>1 OR notes contain REGRESSION marker.

title: Catch empty reply after successful tool work
description:
Mark's 2026-05-20T22:01 GTA session (Qwen3-Coder-30B, --tool-set minimal). Model successfully:

- listed gta/, gta/spec/, gta/agents/, gta/evaluations/
- discovered + loaded read_file via tool_search → load_tool
- read gta/spec/gta2-spec.md, gta2-research.md, gta/agents/orchestrator.md

Then on the next round emitted an EMPTY reply (no content, no tool calls). The orchestrator's bail catchers all returned Continue (the regex-shape catchers don't match empty content), and the loop exited with last_reply.content="" — rendered as "[tool loop exhausted without final reply]".

The wrap-up infrastructure (harness-0gss) only fires when last_reply.tool_calls is non-empty AND work_rounds >= max_rounds. The "empty mid-loop" case isn't covered: model has rounds left, just chose to produce nothing.

## Root cause

No catcher handles "reply is empty AND tool_calls is empty AND tools succeeded this turn." Empty content sails through every regex-shape catcher (FalseSuccess / Teaser / MetaConfirm / FabricatedSearch / etc. all require text to match). The orchestrator treats Continue as "this is the final answer" and exits.

## Fix shape

New bail catcher EmptyReplyAfterToolsHook, placed early in the bail order:

Gate:
- `ctx.reply.content.strip() == ""` (no narrative)
- `ctx.reply.tool_calls is empty` (already checked at the call site — bail only runs on 0-tool replies, but assert explicitly via context)
- `ctx.tools_ran_this_turn is True` (some tool succeeded earlier in this turn)

Response: Nudge with text that forces synthesis OR more work — phrasing TBD but along the lines of "your last reply was empty. You have data from earlier tool calls. Either call another tool to gather more, or give the user a final answer using what you already have. Empty replies are not acceptable when tools have already returned useful data."

Bail retries handle exhaustion the same way as other catchers — if the model keeps emitting empty after 3 retries, fabrication_fallback substitutes the canned refusal.

## Placement

Early in the bail order (between false_success and post_dup_completion_claim). The empty-reply signal is mechanically simple — no regex risk — and orthogonal to the other catchers. Putting it before the regex-shape catchers means an empty reply gets the empty-specific nudge instead of confusingly-named fallthroughs.

## Acceptance

- New unit test: empty content + no tool calls + tools_ran=True → Nudge.
- Empty content + no tool calls + tools_ran=False → Continue (different pathology; FalseSuccess / etc. own the no-tools-no-content case).
- Non-empty content + tools_ran=True → Continue (legitimate wrap-up reply, regardless of content shape).
- Whitespace-only content (whitespace, newlines) → still treated as empty.
- Composition pin: catcher registered in default_hook_pipeline.
- New attribution fixture entry where the catcher carries unique load.

## Out of scope

- Synthesis-quality nudging beyond the canned text (e.g., LLM-driven prompt tuning per-tool). Separate work.
- Distinguishing "model is thinking but emitted nothing" from "model deliberately gave up." Not observable from output.
- Wrap-up infrastructure changes — keep harness-0gss's logic intact; this catcher fires BEFORE wrap-up would.

## Related

- harness-0gss (wrap-up infrastructure; this catcher fires on the no-tool-calls path that harness-0gss doesn't cover).
- harness-2h3m (post-dup completion fabrication; complementary catcher in the same neighborhood).
- harness-jwp3 / harness-a4q4 (preamble / intent-restatement loop catchers; different shape — talking too much rather than not at all).
close_reason: Shipped EmptyReplyAfterToolsHook (bail phase, after FalseSuccess, before PostDupCompletionClaim). Fires when reply.content is empty/whitespace AND tools_ran_this_turn is True — the silent-give-up shape that regex-shape catchers can't see. Nudge forces the model to either continue tooling or synthesize. Repeated empty replies exhaust the bail budget; fabrication_fallback substitutes the canned refusal instead of the '[tool loop exhausted]' debug sentinel. 5 new unit tests + 1 attribution fixture entry. Updated 2 existing tests that pinned the old sentinel behavior. 2998 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: WriteFileRedirectHook misses lazy-loaded write_file (constructed too eagerly)
description:
Mark's 2026-05-20T21:47 session (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit-dwq-v2) hit the exact failure WriteFileRedirectHook was supposed to prevent:

  ✗ error calling write_file: gta/index.html already exists. Use
    edit_file for partial changes, or pass overwrite=true to re…
  [tool loop exhausted without final reply]

The session was launched with the minimal tool set (load_tool / tool_search / introspect only). The model used tool_search + load_tool to discover and activate write_file mid-session. By the time the model called write_file, my hook wasn't registered with the pipeline.

## Root cause

src/harness/cli_classic.py:_make_write_file_redirect_hook returns None when `"write_file" not in registry` at construction time. The hook is built ONCE at session start, before any model-driven load_tool can fire. With --tool-set minimal (the default), write_file isn't initially registered, so the hook is permanently None.

The bidirectional companion pairing (write_file ↔ edit_file in _TOOL_COMPANIONS) ensures edit_file lands alongside write_file, but it doesn't help here — the hook itself is missing.

## Fix shape

Drop the eager `"write_file" not in registry` check. Always construct the hook when registry + workspace_path are both available. The hook's runtime guards already handle the cases:
- `ctx.call.name != "write_file"` → Continue (cheap is-eq check)
- `ensure_edit_file_active()` returns False → Continue (existing recovery path)
- `read_existing(path)` returns None → Continue (file doesn't exist)

Cost: one extra hook in the pre_tool pipeline that no-ops on every non-write_file call. The is-eq check is O(1); negligible overhead.

## Acceptance

- New test: build the hook against an empty registry (write_file not yet registered). Verify the hook is constructed (not None). Then register WriteFileTool + EditFileTool, fire the hook with a write_file call on an existing path → Skip with redirect.
- Existing tests for the hook stay green.
- Full pytest stays green.

## Out of scope

- The "tool loop exhausted without final reply" outcome is a downstream symptom — once the redirect fires the model never sees the error in the first place. If the loop-exhaustion path needs its own catcher, file separately.
- Auto-loading write_file when the redirect fires on an unloaded edit_file. Already covered by load_tool companion pairing.

## Related

harness-hnt7 (the original hook — landed; this is a follow-up defect).
harness-cck4 (load_tool dispatch recovery — landed; complementary).
close_reason: Removed the eager 'write_file not in registry' short-circuit in _make_write_file_redirect_hook. Hook is now constructed whenever registry + workspace_path are both available, regardless of write_file's initial registration state. Closures consult the live registry at call time, so lazy-load via tool_search + load_tool mid-session works correctly. 2 new tests cover the lazy-load case + the no-op-on-unrelated-tool case. 2993 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: Catch post-duplicate-call completion fabrication
description:
Mark's 2026-05-20 GTA2 session ran for ~68 minutes (4100s). The model hit at least one duplicate_call skip (re-emitting an identical edit_file call), paraphrased the dedup result as "task done," and emitted a confident enumerated list of features it had "successfully implemented" — most of which almost certainly aren't in the file.

The wrap-up looks like:

    I have successfully created a GTA2 browser clone that implements...
    1 Basic game structure - ...
    2 Canvas setup - ...
    3 Map rendering - ...
    [... 10 numbered items ...]
    The implementation follows all the technical requirements from the spec...

Self-attestation fabrication. None of the shipped catchers fire:
- FabricatedSearch / FabricatedItemization: gate on web-search shape, not coding wrap-ups.
- FalseSuccess: keys on terse "done!" claims, not multi-paragraph enumerated lists.
- ConfidentFactualClaim: gates on tools_ran_this_turn=False; tools DID run earlier this turn.
- DuplicateCall: short-circuits the call but doesn't see the wrap-up reply.

## Two changes, one bd

### Lever A — Tighten the duplicate_call result prefix

Current _DUPLICATE_CALL_PREFIX wraps the prior result with a soft "(duplicate of an earlier call — re-issuing prior result)" header. The model paraphrases this as "the call worked, move on." Replace with a directive that explicitly tells the model the duplicate is NOT progress and that completion claims require verification.

New text:

    [DUPLICATE CALL — you already made this exact call this turn. The
    prior result is below. DO NOT claim the task is done based on this.
    If you believe the work is finished, call read_file (or the
    equivalent for your domain) to verify the actual state of what you
    edited matches what you intended to do.]

One-line change in hooks.py. Minimal risk — just stronger framing on existing infrastructure.

### Lever B — New PostDupCompletionClaimHook (bail phase)

Tracks the signature: last tool-role message in this turn carries the duplicate_call prefix AND the model's reply has an itemized completion-claim shape (3+ numbered items + completion language like "successfully created", "the implementation includes", "implements all the requirements"). When both fire, Nudge with an honest-fallback directive that forces the model to acknowledge looping and verify via read_file before claiming done.

Lives in hooks.py alongside FalseSuccessHook etc. Bail-phase hook. Gates:
- prior_tool_outputs non-empty AND last entry contains _DUPLICATE_CALL_PREFIX
- reply.content has both completion-language signal AND structural-list signal (numbered or bulleted, ≥3 items)

Nudge text:

    [POST-DUPLICATE FABRICATION — your last tool result was a
    duplicate-call dedup, which means you re-emitted an identical call
    instead of making progress. Before listing what you "implemented",
    call read_file on the files you claim to have changed and verify
    the contents match your claims. If they don't, acknowledge that and
    continue the actual work. Do not fabricate a completion summary.]

## Acceptance

- Lever A: existing tests for DuplicateCallHook + dedup behavior stay green; renamed string is asserted in those tests.
- Lever B: 4 new tests covering: (a) the catch case (last output has dedup prefix + reply has itemized completion claim → Nudge), (b) dedup prefix present but no completion claim → Continue, (c) completion claim but no dedup → Continue (legitimate wrap-up), (d) registered in default_hook_pipeline (composition pin).
- Existing eval suite stays clean.

## Why land A and B together

A reduces the upstream misreading; B catches the case where A wasn't enough. Belt-and-suspenders. Both edit hooks.py only; a single PR keeps the test surface coherent.

## Related

- harness-jwp3 (preamble-loop catcher — open; different signal: shared opening prefix across truncated retries).
- harness-cck4 (unknown_tool dedup carve-out — landed; complementary).
- Separate bd at P3 will track the wall-clock turn cap (Lever C from triage) which would have bounded the 68-min runtime independently.
close_reason: Shipped both levers. Lever A: tightened _DUPLICATE_CALL_PREFIX to a directive ('[DUPLICATE CALL — you already made this exact call this turn. This is NOT progress. DO NOT claim the task is done … call read_file to verify')'). Lever B: new PostDupCompletionClaimHook (bail phase, universal) that fires when the LAST tool output starts with the dedup prefix AND the reply has completion-language + a ≥3-item numbered/bulleted list. Forces the model to verify via read_file before claiming completion. 9 new unit tests + 1 fixture entry; 2976 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: _TagMasker leaks </tool_call> on Qwen3-Coder nested format
description:
Mark's 2026-05-20 GTA2 session with mlx:Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit-dwq-v2 shows multiple bare close-tool-call lines rendering as Airton's visible reply. Reproduces every turn the model emits a Qwen3-Coder tool call.

## Root cause

src/harness/model/qwen_parse.py:169 (_TagMasker) treats both close-tool-call and close-function as close tags and exits hidden mode on whichever appears first in the buffer (lines 210-214). Qwen3-Coder emits the NESTED format:

    open-tool-call + open-function + open-parameter + VAL + close-parameter + close-function + close-tool-call

When the masker enters hidden mode on the open-tool-call, the inner close-function is found first, flips _hidden back to False, and the trailing close-tool-call remains in the buffer. In visible mode the masker only looks for OPENING tags; the close-tool-call is not an opening so it sits in the rolling tail. Once subsequent text pushes past the 15-char tail guard, the close-tag leaks into output.

(Pre-existing on Qwen 2.5 because the flat format open-tool-call + JSON + close-tool-call has only one close tag — no inner close to confuse the masker.)

## Fix shape

Pair opens with their matching closes. When entering hidden mode on the open-tool-call, only exit on the matching close-tool-call. When entering on open-function, only exit on close-function. Keep the existing earliest-of behavior within each pair (irrelevant since each pair has one close, but preserves shape).

Implementation:
- _TagMasker.__init__ adds a self._close_tag of type Optional string
- When transitioning to hidden, record the matching close based on which open fired
- When in hidden mode, search only for self._close_tag (not the full _CLOSE_TAGS tuple)
- Clear self._close_tag on transition back to visible

## Acceptance

- New test: feed a Qwen3-Coder-shaped stream and assert output is the prefix + suffix with no orphan close tag.
- New test: feed a Qwen 2.5 flat-JSON stream and assert output is prefix + suffix (regression guard).
- New test: feed an interleaved stream where the close tag arrives across a delta boundary and assert it is still elided.
- Existing _TagMasker tests stay green.
- Full pytest stays green.

## Out of scope

- _MAX_TAIL tuning (15 chars is fine if pairing is correct).
- Adapter-side parser changes — _parse_qwen_tool_calls already handles both formats correctly via its two regex patterns; only the stream-side masker is broken.

## Repro

Run: harness chat --model mlx --model-repo mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit-dwq-v2 --tools --tool-set coding

First turn that emits a tool call leaks the close-tool-call as visible text.

Related: harness-738f (budget-progression marker — landed; orthogonal). harness-gt0m (default tightening — open; orthogonal). harness-jwp3 (preamble-loop catcher — open; complementary).
close_reason: Paired open/close tags in _TagMasker so hidden-mode exit only fires on the matching close (open <tool_call> waits for </tool_call>; open <function= waits for </function>). Qwen3-Coder's nested format no longer leaks the outer </tool_call> when the inner </function> appears first. 2 new tests + 8 existing tag_masker tests all green; 2959 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: duplicate_call replays stale unknown_tool errors after load_tool resolved them
description:
Session repro 2026-05-20 (Qwen3-Coder-30B, GTA-spec read): model called read_file before activating it; got the catalog-aware 'unknown tool' error from yczi telling it to load_tool. Model correctly called tool_search → load_tool(read_file) → tool activated. Re-emitted the original read_file call. DuplicateCallHook intercepted and replayed the cached unknown_tool error from R1, so the tool never actually ran.

Trace (abbreviated):
  R1: read_file({path: 'docs/gta/spec/gta2-spec.md'})
      → unknown tool: 'read_file'. The tool exists in the catalog but is not active...
      (stored in seen_calls)
  R2: tool_search({query: 'read file', tag: 'filesystem'}) → fallback to query-only → 10 hits
  R3: load_tool({name: 'read_file'}) → built and activated 'read_file' on demand
  R4: read_file({path: 'docs/gta/spec/gta2-spec.md'})
      → DUPLICATE CALL SKIPPED, replayed the R1 unknown_tool error
  R5+: model loops on tool_search('file reader') / dedup'd load_tool / dedup'd read_file

Root cause: PreToolContext.seen_calls is keyed on (name, args_json) and DuplicateCallHook re-issues the EXACT prior ToolResult on a key hit. The hook was designed for harness-pun (model wraps a real answer around a redundant re-call) and harness-v5w (don't fabricate success after a real failure). Neither path anticipated that an `unknown_tool` error specifically signals 'tool isn't loaded' — a state load_tool can resolve mid-turn.

Fix: narrow carve-out in DuplicateCallHook. If the prior ToolResult's error is 'unknown_tool', fall through (Continue) instead of Skip. Rationale:
  - unknown_tool is the one error code whose root cause (tool absent from registry) load_tool / synthesize_tool can fix mid-turn.
  - Re-running the call is correct: it either succeeds now (the loaded path) or fails again with the same unknown_tool error (harmless — the model gets the recovery hint a second time).
  - Other errors (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, HTTP failures, etc.) stay deduped — they're persistent for the same args.

Acceptance:
- DuplicateCallHook.check() returns Continue() when prior.error == 'unknown_tool'.
- Unit test: PreToolContext with seen_calls={(read_file, args): ToolResult(success=False, error='unknown_tool')} → Continue (no Skip).
- Unit test: PreToolContext with seen_calls={(some_tool, args): ToolResult(success=False, error='TypeError: ...')} → Skip (existing behavior preserved).
- Unit test: PreToolContext with seen_calls={(some_tool, args): ToolResult(success=True, ...)} → Skip (existing behavior preserved).
- End-to-end tool-loop test (test_tool_loop.py): scripted sequence R1 unknown-call → R2 load_tool → R3 re-emit → call EXECUTES (not deduped), gets the real result.
- No fixture change needed at the orchestrator level; existing fixtures don't exercise the load-then-retry shape.

Companion: harness-yczi (the catalog-aware unknown_tool hint) shipped first; this bead closes the loop so models can actually act on the hint. Without this fix, yczi's recovery path is broken on the second emission.
close_reason: DuplicateCallHook gets a narrow carve-out for unknown_tool errors. When prior.error == 'unknown_tool', the hook returns Continue instead of Skip — load_tool / synthesize_tool can fix the absent-from-registry state mid-turn, so re-running the call is correct. Other error codes (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, HTTP errors, etc.) remain deduped. 2 unit tests (carve-out fires, other errors still dedup) + 1 end-to-end tool-loop test scripting R1 unknown-call -> R2 register -> R3 real execution. Closes the yczi recovery path that was broken on the second emission. Suite 2939 -> 2942. Commit: 6c771b4.

description:

Record per-case rank of the first expected section and the RRF score. Total runtime: seconds, not minutes.

Minimum scaffold:
- src/harness/evals/atc_retrieval.py — new module, mirrors the shape of evals/router.py (pure-Python scorer; pluggable search callable so tests can inject a fake store).

title: atc corpus chunker drops NOTE / PHRASEOLOGY / REFERENCE blocks
description:
scripts/atc_chunk.py is truncating JO 7110.65 (and likely AIM/PCG/PHAK) sections at italic-bold sub-headings like '## _**NOTE−**_' and '## _**PHRASEOLOGY−**_', treating them as section boundaries instead of children of the parent §X-Y-Z section.

Evidence: 189 / 721 (26%) of ingested JO 7110.65 sections are under 200 chars. Example — §4-6-4 HOLDING INSTRUCTIONS in the corpus is 132 chars (opening line + paragraphs a and b only). Source markdown has the full section including the NOTE ('The holding fix may be omitted if included at the beginning of the transmission as the clearance limit'), paragraphs c/d/e with 'only if' conditions, and a multi-line PHRASEOLOGY block. All dropped.

Impact: controller-side characters (airton_c1) literally cannot cite the omission rules, exceptions, or phraseology for huge swaths of the book. Today's failure: 'when may a controller omit holding instructions' — the canonical answer is in the §4-6-4 NOTE, which is missing from the corpus. Retrieval fell back to §5-13-9 (ERAM mechanics). Forced grounding (harness-3uh) worked correctly; the cited content was just shallow because the deep content was never ingested.

Fix path: update scripts/atc_chunk.py to attach NOTE / PHRASEOLOGY / REFERENCE / EXAMPLE sub-blocks to their parent §X-Y-Z section rather than splitting at them. Re-chunk + re-ingest (the extractor run is cached; only the chunker output changes). Idempotency is on external_id — existing shorter rows will need delete-and-rewrite OR external_id rev bump.

Affects airton_c as well as airton_c1 (shared corpus source).
close_reason: scripts/atc_chunk.py _parse_numbered now folds non-anchor ## headings (NOTE, PHRASEOLOGY, REFERENCE, EXAMPLE, FIG, TBL, phraseology-term sub-headings) into the previous §X-Y-Z anchor's body instead of dropping them. §4-6-4 HOLDING INSTRUCTIONS went from 132 chars to 1,725 chars across 2 chunks — the omit NOTE + PHRASEOLOGY + EXAMPLE are now all present. §4-6-1 went from 420 chars to 5,059 chars across 5 chunks. Total JO 7110.65 rows: 721 → 1,843. Sections under 200 chars: 189 → 92. Retrieval for 'when may a controller omit holding instructions' now correctly ranks §4-6-1 and §4-6-4 as top-2. 6 new chunker tests. All gates green (1161 passed).

title: Subagent primitive (spawn_subagent tool, sota §1.A)
description:
Add a spawn_subagent meta-tool that runs in an isolated context window and returns a summary string.

Design (locked with user 2026-04-22):
- Tier: read — subagent itself takes no confirmation; child tools restricted to read-tier only. Any write work routes back through the main agent with the summary as input.
- Child tools: must be a subset of parent's registry AND read-tier only. 'spawn_subagent' explicitly not allowed in child list.
- Child router: on by default (reuses parent's Router instance).
- Re-entrance: max depth 1; nested spawn returns error ToolResult.
- Child loop shares parent's HookPipeline (fabrication catchers still catch).
- Isolation: child's 'working' starts with [system, user(task)]. Parent never sees child tool calls.
- Return value: child's final reply verbatim as the summary string (no second LLM summarize pass). If child hits max_rounds, return canned '[subagent budget exhausted: <last partial>]'.
- Events: subagent_start + subagent_end added to ToolLoopEvent kinds. v1 observer routing deferred (CLI just sees a single tool_call_start/end around spawn).
- Profile membership: coding, research, diagnostic. Not in minimal, core.

Args: task: str, tools: list[str], max_rounds: int = 6, system_prompt: str | None = None.

Tests: recursion refused at depth 1, write-tier child tools refused, unknown child tool refused, budget exhaustion fallback, basic echo-adapter integration, hooks fire inside child (fabrication caught).

Depends on harness-9sr (hooks refactor) so the child can share the pipeline cleanly.

title: tool loop: truncated-recovery widens main cap but not wrap-up cap
description:
Repro: 'review the file structure and summarize its purpose'. Directory-summary wrap-up round needs > 384 tokens; model truncates. _diagnose_bail returns 'truncated', current_max_tokens doubles (1024→2048), bail_retries decrements, loop retries. But the round-budget calc is `round_max_tokens = min(current_max_tokens, wrap_up_max_tokens) if tools_already_ran` — wrap_up_max_tokens stays at 384. So every retry re-truncates at the same spot, and with _BAIL_RETRIES_PER_TURN=2 the user sees 3 different partial summaries streamed, each cut at ~384 tokens.

Fix: also widen wrap_up_max_tokens on truncated recovery. Mirror current_max_tokens: track current_wrap_up_max_tokens, double it in the 'truncated' branch. Test: scripted adapter that returns truncated reply on round 1 then non-truncated on round 2; assert the second wrap-up round got a wider max_tokens.
close_reason: Fixed. current_wrap_up_max_tokens now tracked alongside current_max_tokens and widened on the 'truncated' recovery branch. Without this, wrap-up rounds that overran the 384-token cap would re-truncate at the same spot because round_max_tokens = min(current_max_tokens, wrap_up_max_tokens) kept clamping to 384 even after current_max_tokens doubled. Test: test_wrap_up_cap_widens_on_truncated_recovery asserts the retry gets 256 tokens (up from initial 128).

title: TUI shows only the first tool call per turn; subsequent tool invocations hidden
description:
When the agent chains multiple tools in a single turn, only the first tool call is rendered in the chat TUI. Later tool invocations run and influence the final reply but are invisible to the user, making it hard to audit what actually happened.

Repro:
  you › tell me about the origin of jehovah's witnesses religion
  airton ›
  → routed to search_facts
  🔧 Recall facts ({'query': "origin of Jehovah's Witnesses", 'k': 5, 'min_confidence': 0.8})
     ✓ [0.365] ... (weak hits)
  [model then runs a web search and returns web results, but no 🔧 line is shown for it]
  <final reply contains clearly-web-sourced results>

Expected: every tool call in the loop emits its own 🔧 label + args + compact result line, in order.

Likely location: orchestrator/tool_loop.py display-label path, or the CLI renderer that consumes tool events. Probably a 'first call only' guard or a display-state variable that isn't reset per-iteration.

Fix scope:
- Audit the tool loop: confirm each iteration's tool_calls are emitted to the renderer.
- Check whether the renderer dedupes on tool name, session, or missing event ID.
- Add a test: fake adapter that emits two sequential tool_calls, assert both appear in captured output.
close_reason: Not a renderer or orchestrator bug. Added 5 regression tests proving every tool_call_start event reaches the observer and every observer event renders a 🔧 line — across multi-round, multi-call-per-round, and router-prelude scenarios. Extracted _render_tool_event from the chat-command closure to make it testable. Root cause of the repro was fabrication: the main model hallucinated web-sourced prose after the router's weak search_facts result, without ever calling search_web. Refiled as harness-cwx.

title: Model hallucinates search_web results instead of calling the tool
description: 7B observed: user asked 'what is the first non-ad result for <query>', Airton replied 'Here are the results: 1. Title: [...] URL: https://www.example.com/...' with a clearly fabricated URL, placeholder snippet, and NO tool call. The orchestrator's bail diagnostics don't catch this because the reply isn't meta-confirm and isn't past-tense-success; it's a third category: 'fabricated tool output shaped like the real thing'. Fix: (1) _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE to detect 'Here are the results:' + URL patterns in a numbered list without a tool call; (2) detect placeholder/example domains (example.com/org, localhost, your-site.com) as hallucination tells; (3) system prompt rule: 'if asked to search the web, you MUST call search_web — never fabricate URLs or results.'

title: Airton still picks write_file overwrite=True for appends
description: Observed: after user said 'yes' to Airton's (unwanted) chat-confirm, Airton called write_file(content='scratch\n', overwrite=True) on existing .gitignore — the exact clobber we tried to prevent in harness-gni. Nudges in write_file description toward edit_file didn't stop the 7B model. Two-pronged fix: (1) strengthen the write_file description further — 'overwrite=true destroys ALL previous content; for adding a line to an existing file use edit_file with empty old_string'. (2) Add a regression test fixture that scripts the flow and asserts edit_file is chosen, not write_file. (3) Consider: refuse write_file(overwrite=true) when the length of new content is smaller than the existing file by some margin — likely a truncation/mistake.
close_reason: Landed: write_file refuses overwrite=True when new content is drastically smaller than existing (<50% AND <1KB); system prompt teaches ADDING vs CHANGING vs CREATING with examples; tool descriptions rewritten. 2 new regression tests.

title: Airton asks for chat-level confirmation instead of calling tool

The tool layer already enforces write-tier confirmation; asking again in chat is redundant AND wastes a round without progress. Add regression test in test_tool_loop.py: adapter that returns such a meta-question without tool calls should trigger a _diagnose_bail nudge.

title: edit_file should treat empty old_string as append
description: Observed: asked Airton to 'add scratch to .gitignore'. The model's intuitive move was edit_file(old_string='', new_string='scratch\n') — which we rejected with 'use write_file to create a file'. That error misdirects: write_file refuses when the file exists. With no working primitive for append, the model falls back to write_file overwrite=true, which is the clobber we were trying to prevent. Fix: empty old_string in edit_file appends new_string to the end of the file (unambiguous semantic). Update description + tests + the existing 'empty rejected' test inverts.

title: write_file silently clobbers existing files

title: driver: artifact-verification gate before bd close sticks
description:
Mark 2026-05-21. Surfaced during GTA2 QA after three stacked regressions (harness-90j0 §1 typo `getContext('d')`, harness-vjb6 §2 malformed tileGrid 28×inconsistent-width, harness-d8ey §6 blocked by §2). All three sections passed the model's self-declared "done" and got `bd close`d; the runtime error only surfaced when the operator loaded the page.

Root cause: the driver trusts `bd close` without verifying the artifact actually functions. Static `forbidden_patterns` (harness-60rv neighborhood) catches TODO/FIXME-shaped sloppiness but cannot catch typos, malformed data structures, or downstream-breaking changes.

DESIGN

Extend PlanItem schema with a `verify` list — per-item shell commands that must exit 0 for the close to "stick" in the driver's state:

  - key: "§1"
    bd_issue: harness-90j0
    spec_quote: "..."
    verify:
      - cmd: "node scripts/smoke.js scratch/index.html"

Per-item granularity is the whole point — §1's verify is "page loads, no console error"; §6's is "page loads + spawnPeds finishes without throwing"; §15's is "key bindings present in source". Each item builds on prior verifies, so the cascade fails at the first broken substrate.

Empty `verify: []` (or omitted) preserves current trust-the-close behavior. Opt-in by design — operator authors verify steps alongside spec_quote.

PIPELINE

In driver/loop.py `_on_success(issue)`:
  1. Look up the PlanItem for `issue`.
  2. If verify list empty → existing behavior (count close, write state).
  3. Run each verify cmd in the workspace dir; capture stdout/stderr/exit.
  4. If all exit 0 → count close, write state.
  5. If any non-zero → reopen the bd issue (bd update --status=open), record `last_failure[issue] = "verify_failed: <stderr tail, 200 chars>"`, do NOT add to closed_this_run, fall through to next turn.

The verify failure path becomes part of the SESSION HANDOFF for the next turn — so the model sees "your prior close was reverted because verify failed: <message>" and can fix without operator backstop.

OUT OF SCOPE

- The verify runner itself (e.g. node/jsdom smoke harness) — that's per-spec. For GTA2 we'll author one alongside the plan; for future specs operator builds their own.
- Cycle detection ("model keeps closing → verify keeps failing → close → fail → ..."). Existing attempt_counts cap handles it: max_attempts hits → halt.
- Generalizing forbidden_patterns into verify (harness-60rv is separate work; can compose).

DEPENDENCIES

- Touches driver/loop.py (`_on_success` + state), driver/handoff.py (PlanItem schema + render carries verify-failed hint), driver/cli.py (none — plan is read fresh each loop).
- Plan YAML schema change is additive; existing plans without `verify` keep working.

CONSTRAINT-MODEL RATIONALE

Per Mark's directive (2026-05-21): "we need to develop this for constrained models and resources, not with the expectation that we can simply run a larger model. ... manual fixes are not enduring." A trust-but-don't-verify driver pushes verification onto the operator — exactly the failure mode the directive forbids. This gate moves the verify into the driver loop where it bounds the failure cascade automatically.

- _on_success(issue) runs verify commands in workspace; non-zero exit reopens the bd issue, records last_failure, blocks the close from counting.
- Verify failure surfaces in the next turn's SESSION HANDOFF (so model self-corrects).
- Tests pin: (a) empty verify → close sticks (existing behavior); (b) failing verify → bd issue reopened + last_failure recorded + closed_this_run unchanged; (c) passing verify → close counts + state advances.
- GTA2 plan_draft.yaml gets verify steps for §1/§2/§3/§6 minimum (the sections we've seen regress).

Together (C) + jmkc bound the model's "I'm done" claim from two angles: jmkc forces the close command to actually run; (C) forces the artifact to actually work.

title: executor: model emits echo "Would run: bd close X" dry-runs instead of executing
description:
Mark 2026-05-21 GTA2 §4 (harness-nyya) double-halt.

Model verified §4 was fully implemented (all sub-sections grepped successfully, code matches acceptance), then on both attempts emitted shell commands like:
  - echo "Would run: bd close harness-nyya"
  - echo "Checking if all acceptance criteria are met"
... instead of executing `bd close harness-nyya`. Turn ends with the issue still open → fail. Two attempts → halt.

Distinct from edit_file dedup loop (harness-w0gw). The work was DONE; the failure was the model substituting a dry-run echo for the side-effecting command. Likely cause: small models over-trained on "be careful with destructive commands; dry-run first" patterns. `bd close` looks destructive (modifies state). The dry-run echo is the model's idea of safe behavior — but the operator instructed it to close when acceptance was met.

Fix candidates:
  1. Pre-tool hook: ShellEchoNoopHook. Detect shell calls whose command is essentially `echo "Would run: ..."` / `echo "Checking ..."` / any pure-narration echo. Skip + nudge: "this is a dry-run echo, not the real command. If acceptance is met, run `bd close <issue-id>` for real. Do not narrate intent — execute."
  2. Strengthen executor user message in src/harness/driver/loop.py. Add: "Do NOT echo intent-strings. Execute commands directly. Narration in shell echoes is invisible to the loop and equivalent to not acting."

Recommend (1) + (2). v0 ships both.
acceptance_criteria: ShellEchoNoopHook detects pure-narration echo commands; executor user message forbids dry-run echoes; tests pin echo dry-run → Skip and real shell command (bd close, ls) → pass through.

title: handoff: workspace_contents format misparses as 'd/<name>' / 'f/<name>' paths
description:
harness-po0v added a workspace block to the handoff with format `f <name>` for files and `d <name>/` for dirs (matching list_dir tool output). Mark 2026-05-21 GTA2 §6 retry: the model consistently misparsed `d gta/` as a path `d/gta/`, emitting `read_file path=d/gta/game.js` calls that failed. Both attempts at §6 in loop_run=ad381610 halted on this misparse — the model never recovered to use the correct workspace-relative path `game.js`.

The `f` / `d` type-prefix shape with whitespace separator is too easy to misread as `<prefix>/<name>`. The model treats the prefix as a directory component.

Fix: drop the type prefix. Use `ls -F` convention — just the entry name with a trailing `/` for directories. Files have no suffix. That matches what the model has seen thousands of times in training data:

Before:
  Contents:
    f game.js
    d gta/
    f index.html

After:
  Contents:
    game.js
    gta/
    index.html

Implementation: tweak `_list_workspace_top_level` in src/harness/driver/handoff.py to emit `f"{name}/" if dir else name` without the `f ` / `d ` prefix.

title: orchestrator: cap truncated_retry count per turn (default 2 or 3)
description:
truncated_retry is unbounded per turn except by _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING (32768). When the model gets stuck in a "write the entire file as text" failure mode — emitting prose/checklist instead of edit_file calls — every retry doubles the budget. Each retry is 3-5 min of MLX inference. By the time the ceiling clamps, the operator has burned 15+ minutes on inference that produced nothing.

Mark 2026-05-21 GTA2 §6 stall: turn 9 hit truncated_retry three times in a row (budgets 2048 → 4096 → 8192 → 16384). Model output was visible as single-char fragments ("2", "3. The", "4. S", "L") — coherence collapse from generating beyond its effective context. Process burned ~13 minutes before operator killed it.

The constrained-model directive (no escape to bigger models) means we MUST treat this as a recoverable failure mode at the driver level. Models WILL get stuck like this; the orchestrator needs a circuit breaker.

Fix: cap consecutive truncated_retry events per turn. Default 2 (matching the bail-retry budget). When the cap is hit:
  - emit a synthetic bail outcome (Nudge with "wrap_up_forced — model kept truncating, stop generating prose and either call a tool or emit a final answer"), OR
  - escalate to fab_fallback directly with a turn-specific message ("model is generating beyond its coherence ceiling")

Implementation in src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py: _BailController already tracks retries; add a parallel counter for truncated retries. The truncated branch already calls on_truncated() to widen the budget; gate that doubling on `truncated_retries_left > 0`.

Out of scope: dynamic token-cap selection based on file size / task shape. Just a hard count cap for v0.
acceptance_criteria: (1) _BailController tracks truncated_retry count per turn separate from bail_retry; (2) default cap = 2 (configurable); (3) when cap hit, the orchestrator stops doubling the budget and either bails or wraps up; (4) test pins: 3 consecutive truncated_retry events exits the turn instead of doubling to ceiling; (5) test pins: the cap is per-turn (next turn gets a fresh count).

title: hooks: edit_file dedup-loop catcher + 'old_string mismatch' error surfaces current file contents
description:
Executor stalls happen when the model's mental model of a long file drifts from disk: it emits edit_file with an old_string the file doesn't contain (sometimes fabricated, sometimes outdated), gets a generic "old_string not found, re-read the file" error, re-emits a variant of the same call, dedup_hook intercepts, fab_fallback fires, turn fails.

Mark's 2026-05-21 GTA2 §6 halt: turns 8 + 9 burned this way — model fabricated `// Canvas setup` lines that don't exist in game.js, tried no-op edits where old_string and new_string were identical, never reached for read_file between failures. Same shape as the §2 stall earlier.

Two fixes that compound:

1. **edit_file error includes current file contents on old_string mismatch.** Today the error says "old_string not found in game.js. Re-read the file and match it exactly". Models routinely interpret this as "try a different formulation of what you think is there" instead of "go fetch the actual content". Fix: append the actual file contents (or a relevant window — say ±20 lines around the closest fuzzy match if we can compute one) to the error. Model gets ground truth in the same response.
   - Tradeoff: error response gets bigger. For a 200-line file that's ~4-8KB. The orchestrator already streams large tool outputs; this is bounded.
   - Cap: skip if file > 1MB (no point including the whole thing).

2. **EditFileDedupLoopHook (pre-tool) catcher**: when the most recent tool result was an edit_file FAIL with `error == "edit_no_match"` OR `error == "edit_noop"` AND the next edit_file call is on the same path, Skip with a Nudge that forces a read_file first. Either: synthesize a read_file call inline (like write_file_redirect does for the create→edit pattern) and feed back the contents, OR rewrite the tool result so the model is told "call read_file path first; refusing to dispatch edit_file until you have current contents in scope".
   - Placement: BEFORE duplicate_call so the loop is caught at the source, not via the generic dedup nudge that doesn't mention re-reading.
   - Opt-in via default_hook_pipeline parameter for now (similar to write_file_redirect_hook); enable in cli_classic / driver.

Out of scope:
- AST-aware edit_file (real fix but big).
- Restoring write_file_overwrite as a model-facing path (intentionally trapped by write_file_redirect for safety).
- replace_file tool (could come later as a `write_file --overwrite` alternative).
acceptance_criteria: (1) edit_file's old_string mismatch + no-op errors include the current file contents (capped at 1MB); (2) EditFileDedupLoopHook detects (last edit_file FAIL with edit_no_match/edit_noop) AND (next call is edit_file on same path) and Skip+Nudges with a forced read_file response; (3) test pins the error-message change for both failure modes; (4) test pins the hook's loop-detection + nudge; (5) test pins the placement BEFORE duplicate_call.

title: driver: halt path doesn't save state (attempt_counts + turns_used go stale on disk)
description:

  - _exit_exhausted persists state before returning
  - Test pins: halt-then-load shows the post-halt attempt_counts + turns_used values

title: driver: --max-turns ignored on resume (saved state's value wins)
description:
Resume loads LoopRunState from disk including the saved max_turns. The CLI's --max-turns is then unused on the resume path, so the user's intent ('let it run with a different cap') is silently dropped.

description:

Mark's 2026-05-21 GTA2 §1 turn closed bd-clean but the model wrote game.js with `e.key` instead of `e.code` (direct §15.4 violation), index.html with wrong title/id/style, and placeholder comments that are implicit TODOs without using the word. Generic patterns can't catch any of these.

Fix: extend PlanItem (and the YAML draft schema) with two optional per-issue lists:
  - forbidden_patterns: tuple[str, ...] — substrings that must NOT appear in any file modified during the turn (e.g. for §1: ['event.key', 'setInterval'])
  - required_substrings: tuple[str, ...] — substrings that MUST appear in some modified file (e.g. for §1: ['id="c"', '<title>GTA2 Clone</title>'])

Wiring:
  1. PlanItem dataclass + to_yaml_dict / from_yaml_dict: add the two fields (defaults to empty tuples).
  2. commit_plan: pass the lists through to the bd issue via labels (forbid:<pattern> and require:<pattern>) OR notes JSON. Labels are more queryable but escaping is awkward for patterns with spaces; structured notes JSON is cleaner.
  3. DriverBd.show: existing path returns BeadsIssue.raw which already includes notes — parse per-issue forbidden/required at handoff-build time.
  4. _classify_post_turn: extend forbidden-pattern check to UNION the generic patterns from LoopConfig with the per-issue forbidden from the bd issue. Also add required-substring check (fail if any required not found in any modified file).
  5. handoff.render: surface the per-issue checks so the executor knows what NOT to write.

Out of scope: AST-level checks (requires per-language parsers). Substring-based is enough to catch the common failures.
acceptance_criteria: (1) PlanItem.forbidden_patterns + PlanItem.required_substrings fields with empty-tuple defaults; (2) YAML round-trips both fields; (3) commit_plan serializes them via structured bd notes JSON or labels; (4) _classify_post_turn checks per-issue forbidden patterns alongside LoopConfig.forbidden_patterns; (5) _classify_post_turn fails turn when a required_substring is missing from all modified files; (6) handoff.render surfaces both per-issue lists so the executor sees them; (7) tests pin: forbidden hit fails turn, required miss fails turn, neither passes.

title: driver: post-turn forbidden-pattern verification
description:
After a turn closes its bd issue, the driver classifies as success. But the model can close an issue while leaving anti-pattern code in the files it wrote — Mark's 2026-05-21 GTA2 §1 turn left scratch/game.js with TODO comments AND event.key bindings (§15.4 violation), both spec-forbidden, AND would have been marked success if the model had only remembered to bd close.

Fix: in src/harness/driver/loop.py _classify_post_turn, after the bd.show check passes, scan workspace files modified during this loop run for any of LoopConfig.forbidden_patterns. If any pattern hits, return False with the violation list as the reason (lands in last_failure for retry context).

Implementation:
  - Walk workspace.rglob('*') filtering: not in (.git, .harness, .beads), file size < 1MB, mtime > state.started_at, decodable as UTF-8 text.
  - For each surviving file, check substring match against each pattern.
  - Return list of '<rel_path>: contains <pattern>' strings.

Default forbidden patterns: ('TODO', 'FIXME', 'XXX', 'HACK'). The spec opens with 'If you skip a requirement and write TODO or future improvement you fail that item' — generic enough to be useful across GTA2-style specs.

Per-issue / per-spec customization (e.g. 'event.key' for §15 of GTA2, 'setInterval' for §1.3) is out of scope for v0 — file as harness-9bpt sibling if Mark wants it. The generic check is the high-leverage win.

CLI: --no-verify flag on harness drive loop to disable the check entirely (escape hatch for operators with looser standards or specs).
acceptance_criteria: (1) _classify_post_turn checks forbidden patterns after the bd.show check; (2) LoopConfig.forbidden_patterns defaults to (TODO, FIXME, XXX, HACK); (3) --no-verify flag disables the check; (4) walk skips hidden dirs + binary files + large files; (5) test pins: clean code = success, TODO in modified file = failure with violation list; (6) test pins --no-verify disables the check.

title: driver: executor observability — event log + --verbose
description:
Same shape fix as harness-mzce for the planner, but for the executor (run_loop). Today run_loop calls run_tool_loop without an observer, so the per-turn tool events (which tools fired, which tool calls failed, which catchers tripped, what the model said) are invisible after a turn ends. Mark's 2026-05-21 GTA2 §1 turn FAILED (issue still open after turn) but we have zero visibility into WHY — only the driver-side lifecycle log.

Fix: in src/harness/driver/loop.py _run_executor_turn, accept a per-turn ObserverFn and pass it to run_tool_loop's observe=. Write events to the existing <workspace>/.harness/loop_runs/<id>.log alongside the lifecycle markers (prefix per-turn events with 'turn N |' so the operator can grep). Add --verbose to harness drive loop that mirrors the per-turn events to stderr.

Future: per-turn separate log files if the combined log gets too long. For v0 a single file is enough.
acceptance_criteria: (1) _run_executor_turn accepts an observer + passes it to run_tool_loop's observe=; (2) the existing loop log file gets per-turn tool events alongside lifecycle markers; (3) --verbose flag mirrors per-turn events to stderr; (4) test pins the observer plumbing.

title: driver: add --model-repo / --lora-path / --draft-repo to drive commands
description:
harness drive plan and harness drive loop only support --model {echo,mlx,ollama} via the factorys default — no way to override the HF repo (e.g. swap Qwen 2.5-7B for Qwen3-Coder-30B), attach a LoRA, or use speculative decoding. harness chat supports all three via _resolve_adapter in cli.py. title: driver: dirty-tree check ignores .beads/ + untracked files
description:
harness drive loop refuses to run when git status shows ANY uncommitted change. Two problems with that gate:

1. `.beads/*` is bd-managed state. Every `bd close`/`bd update` an executor turn runs (and they run frequently — every successful turn closes an issue via shell `bd close <id>`) writes to `.beads/export-state.json` / `.beads/interactions.jsonl` / `.beads/issues.jsonl`. The loop is GOING to dirty `.beads/` legitimately; checking on them is exactly backwards. The user also commonly arrives at `harness drive loop` with `.beads/*` already dirty from prior bd CLI activity (the pre-commit hook re-exports on every commit, but interactive bd reads/writes between commits routinely modify these files).

2. Untracked files (e.g. `.coverage`, scratch files) shouldnt gate either. The handoffs "files touched this loop_run" diff is `git diff --name-status base..HEAD` which only walks tracked-file changes. Untracked files are invisible to the diff, so they cant make the diff "misleading" — they cant make it anything.

Fix `_git_tree_is_dirty` in src/harness/driver/cli.py:
  - Use `git diff --name-only HEAD` instead of `git status --porcelain` so untracked files are ignored.
  - Filter `.beads/` from the result.
  - Return True only if any tracked, non-.beads/ path is modified.

Surfaced during Marks 2026-05-21 GTA2 QA pass: after committing the manual workplan and shipping harness-2pj3, `harness drive loop --dry-run` worked, but a real run would have tripped the dirty gate due to .beads/export-state.json churn from bd activity in the same session.
acceptance_criteria: (1) _git_tree_is_dirty returns False when only .beads/* files are modified; (2) _git_tree_is_dirty returns False when only untracked files exist; (3) _git_tree_is_dirty returns True when any tracked non-.beads/ file is modified; (4) tests pin all three cases via subprocess.run monkeypatch.
close_reason: Closed

title: driver: render assembled handoff in --dry-run output
description:
harness drive loop --dry-run currently returns a LoopResult with the assembled Handoff in result.handoffs[0], but the CLI _print_result only prints the one-line summary (loop_run=... exit=dry_run turns_used=0 closed=0). The whole point of --dry-run is for the operator to inspect the handoff BEFORE burning real model turns; today they have to dig into the loop_run state file and reproduce the handoff manually to actually see what the executor would see.

Surfaced during Marks 2026-05-21 GTA2 QA pass: after harness drive plan --commit landed the 16-item GTA2 epic, harness drive loop --epic <id> --dry-run completed cleanly (turns_used=0, exit=dry_run) but printed nothing actionable.

Fix: in src/harness/driver/cli.py _print_result, when result.exit_reason == "dry_run" AND result.handoffs is non-empty, echo the handoff.render() output to stdout before / after the summary line. Use the existing Handoff.render() — no new rendering needed.

Out of scope: streaming the handoff during build, multi-issue dry-run (current dry-run intentionally exits after one handoff per harness-ml66 spec).
acceptance_criteria: (1) _print_result renders the handoff when exit_reason='dry_run' and handoffs is non-empty; (2) test in tests/test_driver_cli.py verifies the [SESSION HANDOFF] block appears in stdout for the dry-run path; (3) the summary line still appears alongside the handoff.
