title: §15 Controls — key mapping + edge-trigger + pause
description:
> **Do NOT bind to** `event.key` lowercase letters — caps lock and shift state will break it. **Always** use `event.code`.

Consolidate input per §15. Most key reads have been wired inline by §4, §10, §11.5, §14 — this turn audits and finalizes:

  - §15.1 listener audit: confirm the keydown/keyup listeners declared in §1 set `keys[event.code]` (NOT `event.key`) and call `event.preventDefault()`. Fix if §1's executor took shortcuts.
  - §15.3 edge-trigger pattern: declare `let prevKeys = {};` (if not already). At the END of each frame's update: `prevKeys = {...keys};`. Replace ad-hoc edge-trigger checks from §10.5 / §11.5 / §14.2 with the canonical `keys.X && !prevKeys.X`.
  - §15 key map (audit each existing read, verify mode gating):
    - forward: `keys.ArrowUp || keys.KeyW` — both modes
    - reverse: `keys.ArrowDown || keys.KeyS` — both modes
    - steer left: `keys.ArrowLeft || keys.KeyA` — both modes
    - steer right: `keys.ArrowRight || keys.KeyD` — both modes
    - handbrake: `keys.Space` — driving only (gate on `mode === 'driving'`)
    - fire: `keys.ControlLeft || keys.KeyJ` — foot only (gate on `mode === 'foot'`)
    - cycle weapon: `keys.KeyQ` (edge) — foot only
    - enter/exit/jack: `keys.Enter || keys.KeyF` (edge) — both modes
    - respawn: `keys.KeyR` (edge) — dead only (gate on `!player.alive`)
    - pause: `keys.Escape` (edge) — always
  - §15.2 pause toggle:
    - `let paused = false;`
    - Escape edge-trigger: `paused = !paused`
    - gameLoop: when `paused === true`, SKIP the update step but still render + draw 'PAUSED' centered on the canvas in white 48px monospace (`ctx.fillStyle='#fff'; ctx.font='48px monospace'; ctx.textAlign='center'; ctx.fillText('PAUSED', canvas.width/2, canvas.height/2)`).
    - requestAnimationFrame keeps firing — don't stop the loop.
  - §15.4 anti-pattern audit: grep `event.key` across game.js. If any found, swap to `event.code`. Common drift: `if (e.key === 'w')` slipped in somewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Every §15 action works via BOTH primary and alternate key codes. Mode-gated keys respect their gate (Space only when driving, KeyJ only when on foot, KeyR only when dead). Edge-triggered keys fire ONCE per press (no rapid-fire jacking by holding Enter). Pause via Escape stops the update step but renders the world + 'PAUSED' overlay. Caps lock does not break controls. No `event.key` reads remain in game.js.

title: §14 Death and respawn — overlay + R-key handler + state reset
description:
> **Respawn**: pressing `R` while dead spawns a fresh car at the original spawn point with full health, `mode = 'driving'`. Reset wanted to 0 and multiplier to 1 (per §12.4 and §8 cooldown rule); score persists. Inventory (weapons + ammo) resets to all zeros, `currentWeapon = null`.

Implement §14:
  - §14.1 death:
    - Each frame after damage applies, if `player.health <= 0` AND `player.alive`, set `player.alive = false`.
    - Drawing: when `player.alive === false`, draw the existing player sprite (car or foot pose — both already drawn by §3 and §10 respectively) PLUS a `#400000` 50%-alpha rect over the sprite bounding box AND a black `×` glyph centered on the sprite.
    - The on-foot variant of the overlay was partially wired in §10's executor turn; verify and extend if it only handled foot or only handled car.
  - §14.2 respawn handler (R-key, edge-triggered, ONLY when `player.alive === false`):
    - `player.health = 100`
    - `player.alive = true`
    - `player.mode = 'driving'`
    - `player.car = <reset to the original player-car object at the §3.5 spawn point (480, 320), angle 0, speed 0>`. If the player jacked a civilian car before dying, the original player-car may still exist abandoned on the map — leave it there; spawn a fresh one to drive.
    - `wanted = 0`
    - `multiplier = 1`  (§12.4)
    - `inventory = { pistol: 0, machinegun: 0, rocket: 0 }`
    - `currentWeapon = null`
    - `score` PERSISTS — do NOT reset.
    - `chainCount = 0`, `chainTimer = 0` (implicit; the chain is broken on death)
    - `wantedTimer = 0` (reset §8.3 cooldown timer)
  - §14.3 no auto game-over screen. Continue indefinitely; the player can die and respawn any number of times.

The R-key binding is finalized in §15.2/§15.3 (edge-triggered, dead-only). Until §15 lands, read `keys.KeyR` directly with a `prevKeys.KeyR` edge check.
acceptance_criteria: When `player.health` reaches 0, `player.alive` flips to false and the player sprite renders with a `#400000` overlay + black `×`. Pressing R while dead respawns a fresh player car at (480, 320), restores health to 100, sets mode='driving', resets wanted/multiplier/inventory/currentWeapon/chainCount/wantedTimer. Score persists across deaths. No game-over screen — game continues indefinitely.

title: §13 HUD — score / chain / wanted heads / health / weapon / mode
description:
> **Tech: HUD draws AFTER the world**, in screen-space (no camera transform). Reset transform with `ctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0)` before drawing the HUD.

Implement HUD per §13. ALL drawing in this section happens AFTER `ctx.restore()` for the §5 camera transform AND after `ctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0)` resets to identity. If a HUD element appears to scroll with the camera, the transform reset is missing.

  - §13.2 top-left score + multiplier: `ctx.fillStyle='#ffcc00'; ctx.font='20px monospace'; ctx.fillText('SCORE: ' + score, 10, 30); ctx.fillText('×' + multiplier, 10, 56);`
  - §13.3 top-center chain: if `chainCount >= 2`, draw `'CHAIN ×' + chainBonus + '!'` at `(canvas.width/2, 30)` with `ctx.textAlign='center'`. Compute `chainBonus = Math.min(5, Math.max(1, chainCount))` inline (same formula §6/§9b use).
  - §13.4 top-right wanted heads: up to 6 small 14×16 head icons, right-aligned. Each head: `#f0c090` filled 14×16 with `#000` 2×2 eyes at fixed positions. Filled if `wanted >= index`, outlined only if not. SHAKE if any cop is within 250px of player (skip the "no building between" line-of-sight — simplify to distance only). Shake = ±1px x offset every other frame for filled heads only.
  - §13.5 bottom-left health bar:
    - background: `#400000` rectangle 200×16 at `(10, canvas.height - 26)`
    - foreground: `#ff3030` rectangle width `200 * (player.health / 100)`, same y, same x
    - border: `#fff` 1px stroke around the background
  - §13.6 bottom-center weapon + ammo (draw only when `mode === 'foot'` OR any `inventory[type] > 0`):
    - 32×32 mini-icon of `currentWeapon` (re-use the §9.6–§9.8 pickup shape but shrunk — 18px wide) at `(canvas.width/2 - 60, canvas.height - 40)`
    - label: `ctx.fillStyle='#ffcc00'; ctx.font='18px monospace'; ctx.fillText(currentWeapon + ': ' + inventory[currentWeapon], canvas.width/2 - 30, canvas.height - 22)`
    - if `currentWeapon === null`, draw `'UNARMED'` in the same spot.
  - §13.8 mode indicator (top-right, LEFT of the wanted heads): `'ON FOOT'` when `mode === 'foot'`, `'DRIVING'` when `mode === 'driving'`. `#ffcc00` 14px monospace.

§13.7 (money counter) is Bonus tied to cash pickups, which are out-of-scope per §16. SKIP.

§13.4 line-of-sight simplification ("no building between") is operator-approved here — center-vs-tile distance check only. The full LoS would need raycasting through the tile grid and is overbudget for v0.
acceptance_criteria: HUD renders in screen-space (not scrolling with camera). Top-left shows `SCORE: <n>` and `×<multiplier>`. Top-center shows the chain indicator when chainCount ≥ 2. Top-right shows up to 6 wanted heads — filled per current wanted level, outlined for empty slots, shake when a cop is within 250px. Bottom-left shows health bar. Bottom-center shows weapon icon + ammo (or 'UNARMED'). Mode indicator shows 'ON FOOT' or 'DRIVING' to the left of the wanted heads. §13.7 money counter is skipped per §16.

title: §12 Score and multiplier — chain decay + cross-section score events
description:
> **Tech: multiplier is the persistent number; chainBonus is the short-term streak.** Score per kill is `100 × multiplier × chainBonus`.

Most score events are already wired in their owning sections — §6.7 (ped run-over), §9b (ped shot, cop shot), §9a (pickup +50), §11.5 (jack +50). This turn implements the parts that span sections:

  - **Chain timer decay per §12.3.** Each frame:
    - `chainTimer -= dt`
    - if `chainTimer <= 0`: `chainCount = 0`
    Every score event resets `chainTimer = 3` (seconds). The `chainBonus` formula `Math.min(5, Math.max(1, chainCount))` is already inlined at each kill site from §6/§9b; this turn adds ONLY the decay loop, not the per-event chainCount++ (those landed where the events fire).

  - **Police car destroyed score event per §12.2:** hook off §8's existing "cop.health <= 0 → cop.alive = false + wanted bump" code. ADD `score += 1000 * multiplier` at the same point. Grep for the cop-death handler §8 wrote.

  - **Civilian car destroyed score event per §12.2:** hook off §11.7's existing "civ.health <= 0 → wreck + wanted bump" code. ADD `score += 200 * multiplier`. Grep for the §11.8 wreck transition.

  - **Persistent multiplier on death per §12.4:** when `player.alive` flips to false (will be wired in §14), reset `multiplier = 1`. For this turn, the reset can be a placeholder hook — `// §14.3 will set multiplier = 1 on respawn` — that §14's executor turn picks up. OR write it now: in the per-frame check, `if (!player.alive && multiplier !== 1 && /* one-shot guard */)` set it to 1. Either works; pick the cleaner one for the current code shape.

  - **No new score events on this turn.** Don't add scoring for cop-on-cop, ped-on-ped, environmental destruction. Those aren't in the spec.
acceptance_criteria: Chain timer decays from 3 to 0 over 3 seconds with no kills; chainCount resets to 0 when timer expires. New score events fire: cop destroyed = +1000 × multiplier; civilian car destroyed = +200 × multiplier. Multiplier reset hook for §14.3 is in place (either inline or as a comment that §14 picks up). All previously-wired score events (§6.7 ped run-over, §9a pickup, §9b shooting, §11.5 jack) still work — no regression.

title: §11 NPC traffic & car-jacking — civilian cars + jack from foot
description:
> do **NOT** path-plan civilian cars on a graph of intersections. The 30/70 random-decision rule in 11.4 is sufficient and produces convincing traffic.

Implement civilian cars + jacking per §11:
  - `let traffic = [];` per §11.1. Each car: `{ x, y, angle, speed, maxSpeed: 140, color, alive: true, driver: 'npc', health: 60, intent, nextDecisionAt: 0 }`.
  - Spawn per §11.2: 6 civilian cars at startup on random `.` road tiles ≥150px from player. `intent` = cardinal heading (0, π/2, π, 3π/2) of the road tile (pick whichever has another road tile in front). Colors from `['#d04040', '#40b040', '#d0a020', '#a040d0', '#40b0d0', '#d0d0d0']`, no two adjacent in the spawn order.
  - Spawn maintenance per §11.3: every 8s, if alive count < 4, spawn 1 more at a road tile >480px from player. Cap at 8 alive.
  - AI per §11.4 per frame per NPC-driven car:
    - cruise: `speed` accelerates toward `maxSpeed` at 80 px/sec².
    - heading: rotate `angle` toward `intent` at up to 2.0 rad/sec (same wrap-to-[-π,π] as §7.3). When `|angle - intent| < 0.05`, snap.
    - intersection decision: when car's center is in a `+` tile AND `now >= nextDecisionAt`: 30% pick a new perpendicular cardinal direction for `intent`; 70% straight. Set `nextDecisionAt = now + 800`.
    - car-ahead stop: if any car (civ or player) is within 25px AHEAD (along current heading), `speed = 0` this frame.
    - building collision: per §4.5; on hit revert position, `speed = 0`, pick a new random perpendicular `intent` immediately.
    - NO map wrap.
  - §11.5 jacking (extends §10's enter handler): when `mode === 'foot'` AND Enter/KeyF edge-triggered AND a civilian car is within 24px:
    - if `driver === 'npc'`: spawn a new ped at the car's position with `state: 'panic'`, `angle = atan2(car.y - foot.y, car.x - foot.x)`, `speed: 70`, push to `peds[]`. Then `car.driver = 'player'`, `car.speed = 0`, `mode = 'driving'`, `player.car = <that car>`. Bonus: `score += 50`.
    - if `driver === null` (abandoned): take over without ejection.
  - §11.6 jacked-car driving: `player.car` is now a reference to the civilian car; §4's driving code reads physics constants from `player.car.*`. If §4 hardcoded values, refactor to read from the ref.
  - §11.7 damage to civilian cars:
    - player car ramming: if player.car is within 20px of an alive civ AND `|player.car.speed| > 80`, `civ.health -= 30 * dt`. On `civ.health <= 0`: §11.8 wreck AND `wanted = min(6, wanted + 1)`.
    - bullets/rockets: add `traffic` to §9b's bullet-vs-target loop so projectiles damage civilian cars. Rocket direct hit (100 dmg > 60 hp) instantly destroys.
  - §11.8 wreck: `alive = false`, `driver = null`, draw a smaller darker rect (color channels × 0.4) with a `#aa2020` 4×4 fire dot at center. Wrecks DO NOT block driving — treat the tile as still drivable.
  - §11.9 civilian-on-pedestrian: if an NPC-driven car runs over a ped (12px proximity, speed > 50), kill the ped (§6.7-style) but award NO player score, NO wanted bump.
  - Also wire the §10.7 foot-side civilian-car damage check: `traffic[]` now has entries, so the "moving civilian car (speed > 50) within 12px of foot → player.health -= 80 * dt" branch starts firing.
  - Visual per §11.10: same shape as §3.3 (reuse the player-car drawing function) but body = `color` from the spawn list, 2px `#000` outline, roof = (color channels × 0.5) as a 10×8 rectangle, no light bar.

§11.11 anti-pattern: do NOT write A*, Dijkstra, or any pathfinding. The 30/70 random rule IS the AI. Models that built graph search ran out of turns.
acceptance_criteria: 6 civilian cars spawn at startup with distinct §11.10 colors on road tiles ≥150px from player. NPC cars cruise toward maxSpeed; turn at intersections (30/70 rule); stop when another car is ≤25px ahead; bounce off `B` tiles. Population maintenance keeps 4–8 alive. Player can jack at foot: NPC ejects as a panic ped (+50 score). Player car ramming + bullets damage civilian cars; wreck visual + wanted bump on destruction. NPC-car-vs-ped still kills the ped but gives no player score. The §10.7 foot-damage-from-civilian-car branch fires correctly now that `traffic[]` is populated.

title: §9b Weapons firing — bullets, projectile travel, hit detection
description:
> **In-car firing**: do **NOT** implement weapons firing from inside the car. Driving is the in-car weapon (run-over from §6.7). Exit the car (§10) to shoot.

Implement firing + projectile system per §9.4, §9.15, §9.16:
  - `let bullets = []; let lastShotAt = 0;` at top of game.js (one shared `lastShotAt` is enough — per-weapon fire-rates handled at the trigger check).
  - Declare weapon stats per §9.4 — `const weaponStats = { pistol: {damage:20, fireRate:0.30, projectileSpeed:480, range:240}, machinegun: {damage:8, fireRate:0.08, projectileSpeed:540, range:280}, rocket: {damage:100, splashDamage:60, splashRadius:40, fireRate:0.90, projectileSpeed:260, range:600} }`.
  - §9.15 firing trigger — per frame, if `player.mode === 'foot'` AND fire key held AND `currentWeapon !== null` AND `inventory[currentWeapon] > 0` AND `now - lastShotAt >= weaponStats[currentWeapon].fireRate * 1000`:
    - `inventory[currentWeapon]--`; `lastShotAt = now`
    - push `{ x: foot.x, y: foot.y, angle: foot.angle, speed: <stats.projectileSpeed>, ttl: stats.range / stats.projectileSpeed, type: currentWeapon }` to `bullets`
    - if `inventory[currentWeapon] === 0`, auto-cycle to next slot with ammo > 0, or null per §9.4 trailing line
  - per-frame bullet update: `b.x += cos(b.angle) * b.speed * dt; b.y += sin(b.angle) * b.speed * dt; b.ttl -= dt`. Remove on `ttl <= 0` OR if bullet's tile is a `B`.
  - bullet-vs-ped: if `dist(b, ped) < 6`, kill ped (same §6.7 effects: `ped.alive = false`, score+chainCount bump, wanted bump on first-of-chain). Remove bullet.
  - bullet-vs-cop: if `dist(b, cop) < 20`, `cop.health -= weaponStats[b.type].damage`. On `cop.health <= 0`: `cop.alive = false`, `wanted = min(6, wanted + 1)` (matches §8). Remove bullet.
  - rockets — on hit OR `ttl <= 0`: kill every ped within 40px outright; subtract 60 from every cop within 40px. Spawn the §9.16 explosion visual.
  - §9.16 visuals: bullets = 2×2 `#ffe040` squares. Rockets = 4×3 `#aa2020` rectangles with a `#ffaa20` 2×2 trail behind. Rocket explosion = `#ffaa20` filled circle expanding from radius 4 to 40 over 0.25s.
  - §15 binds fire to `KeyJ` / `ControlLeft` (foot-only). Until §15 lands, read those codes directly.

§9.17 — DO NOT wire in-car firing. The car already has run-over (§6.7) and that's the in-car weapon by design.
acceptance_criteria: On foot with a weapon equipped + ammo > 0, holding the fire key emits projectiles per §9.4. Bullets travel straight at the documented speed, expire after `range/speed` seconds OR on entering a `B` tile. Bullets within 6px of a ped kill it (+§6.7 effects). Bullets within 20px of a cop apply damage; cop death sets `alive = false` and bumps wanted by 1. Rockets explode (§9.16 visual) with 40px splash damage. Firing is BLOCKED when `player.mode === 'driving'`.

title: §10 On-foot mode — exit/enter + walking + damage
description:
> do **NOT** invent a second physics system for on-foot. Reuse the same `x / y / angle / speed` fields with different constants (lower `walkSpeed`, higher `turnRate`, no friction-based glide — speed is set directly each frame from key input, not integrated).

Implement on-foot mode per §10:
  - Extend `player` per §10.1 with `player.mode = 'driving'` and `player.car = <ref to player's car>`. Declare `let foot = { x: 0, y: 0, angle: 0, speed: 0, walkSpeed: 90, turnRate: 4.0, radius: 5 };`.
  - Walking physics per §10.3 (only when `mode === 'foot'`):
    - forward → `foot.speed = walkSpeed`; released → `foot.speed = 0` (no inertia).
    - backward → `foot.speed = -walkSpeed * 0.6`.
    - left/right → `foot.angle ±= turnRate * dt`. NOT speed-dependent (different from §4.2 driving).
    - position: `foot.x += cos(foot.angle) * foot.speed * dt`, same for y.
    - building collision: center-vs-tile per §4.5; revert position; NO bounce (just stop).
  - Exit per §10.5: when `mode === 'driving'` AND `|player.car.speed| < 20` AND Enter/KeyF edge-triggered → `mode = 'foot'`, place `foot.x = player.car.x + 14*cos(player.car.angle + π/2)`, `foot.y = player.car.y + 14*sin(player.car.angle + π/2)`, `foot.angle = player.car.angle`, `foot.speed = 0`, `player.car.speed = 0`, `player.car.driver = null`. Refuse exit if car speed > 20.
  - Enter per §10.5: when `mode === 'foot'` AND Enter/KeyF edge-triggered → find nearest car within 24px. SCOPE FOR THIS TURN: only the player's own abandoned car. The "jack a civilian car" branch lives in §11.5; §10's executor writes the re-enter-own-car path and §11.5 extends it. If found, `mode = 'driving'`, `player.car = <that car>`, `player.car.driver = 'player'`.
  - Camera per §10.6: when on foot, the §5 follow rule reads `foot.x, foot.y` instead of `player.car.x, player.car.y`. Same map-bounds clamp.
  - Damage on foot per §10.7: per frame, any cop within 12px of foot → `player.health -= 50 * dt`. Any moving civilian car (speed > 50) within 12px → `player.health -= 80 * dt` (the civilian car does NOT stop). Civilian-car branch lands when §11 does — wire the cop branch now, leave the civilian-car branch reading from `traffic[]` (which §11 declares; will be empty until then).
  - Visual per §10.4: blue body circle r=5, skin head circle r=3, black 1px outline, 8-pixel facing line from `(foot.x, foot.y)`, plus a 3px `#404040` weapon-in-hand square at `(foot.x + 5*cos(angle), foot.y + 5*sin(angle))` when `currentWeapon !== null`.
  - Drawing order per §10.10: tiles → pickups → cars → dead peds → bullets → live peds → on-foot character → HUD. Foot draws ON TOP of cars.
  - Extend §9.12 pickup collection: in addition to the player-car check from §9a, ALSO collect when `mode === 'foot'` AND foot is within 20px of a pickup. This matches the §9.12 "active actor" rule.

§10.8 (score events from shooting peds/cops) is wired in §9b — no work here.
§10.9 death-on-foot overlay (red tint + black ×) is implemented here per §14.1; the respawn handler lives in §14.
acceptance_criteria: Driving slowly (<20 px/sec) + Enter/KeyF exits the car; foot character spawns beside the abandoned car. WASD/arrows walk with no inertia. On-foot turning works at zero speed. Building collision reverts position (no bounce). Enter/KeyF near the abandoned car re-enters driving mode. Camera follows foot.x/y when on foot. Foot character draws on top of cars. Pickups collect on-foot too. Cop proximity drains HP at 50/sec. Weapon-in-hand stub visible when `currentWeapon !== null`. Drawing order matches §10.10.

title: §9a Pickups — world objects (spawn, spin, collect)
description:
> **Tech: simulate Y-axis rotation as horizontal squash using `ctx.scale(Math.cos(t*4), 1)`** (where `t` is `now/1000`) around the pickup center.

Implement §9 pickup-side (weapons-firing lands in §9b):
  - `let pickups = []` and `let inventory = { pistol: 0, machinegun: 0, rocket: 0 }; let currentWeapon = null;` per §9.1 + §9.3. `currentWeapon` starts null because no weapon is picked up yet.
  - Spawn the 7 hand-placed pickups per §9.2 at the listed (x, y) with the listed type / ammo. Do NOT randomize.
  - Spin per §9.5: at draw time, `ctx.save(); ctx.translate(p.x, p.y); ctx.scale(Math.cos(t*4), 1); <icon centered on 0,0>; ctx.restore()` where `t = now/1000`. Do NOT use `ctx.rotate` — that gives a top-down spin which reads as "tumbling" instead of "hovering."
  - Icons per §9.6 (pistol), §9.7 (machinegun), §9.8 (rocket), §9.9 (multiplier), §9.10 (bribe), §9.11 (health). Each draws its `#40ff40` alpha-0.25 glow circle FIRST, then the icon on top.
  - Collection per §9.12: per frame, for every alive pickup, if the player CAR is within 20px of the pickup center, apply the §9.12 effect (ammo into `inventory[type]` capped at 99; `multiplier = min(99, multiplier + 1)`; `wanted = max(0, wanted - 1)`; `player.health = min(100, player.health + 50)`), set `pickup.alive = false`, `pickup.respawnAt = now + 30000`, and `score += 50`. §9.12 says BOTH car and on-foot can collect — wire the car-side now; §10 will extend the active-actor check to include on-foot.
  - Respawn per §9.13: `if (!p.alive && now >= p.respawnAt) p.alive = true;` each frame.

§9.14 anti-pattern: pickups are always visible, always spinning, always collectable. Don't gate them behind a state machine.

Weapon pickups currently just refill `inventory[type]` — firing them does nothing yet. Firing logic is §9b.
acceptance_criteria: All 7 pickups visible at their §9.2 coords, spinning via the §9.5 `ctx.scale` technique (not `ctx.rotate`). Each renders with its §9.6–§9.11 icon over the `#40ff40` glow circle. Driving over a pickup fires the §9.12 effect (correct inventory / multiplier / wanted / health update), marks `alive = false`, schedules `respawnAt = now + 30000`, and adds `+50` to score. After 30s the pickup is visible + collectable again.

title: §8 Wanted level — triggers + cooldown
description:
> if **no triggering event happens for 30 seconds** AND no police car is currently within 200 px of the player, decrement `wanted` by 1. Repeats every 30s of clean play until 0.

Implement §8 around the `wanted` variable declared in §6.

Triggers per §8.2:
  - First-of-chain ped kill: already wired in §6.7 — no new work, just don't double-fire here.
  - Player rams cop at speed > 100: per-frame, check if player is within ~20px of any alive cop AND `|player.speed| > 100`. Edge-trigger ONCE per contact entry (don't re-fire every frame of contact) — `wanted = min(6, wanted + 1)`.
  - Player kills a cop (cop.health → 0): each frame, if player within 20px of cop AND `|player.speed| > 80`, drain `cop.health -= 30 * dt` (per §12.2). When `cop.health <= 0`, set `cop.alive = false` AND `wanted = min(6, wanted + 1)`. The score event (+1000 × multiplier) lives in §12 — don't add it here.

Cooldown per §8.3:
  - Track `let wantedTimer = 0;`. Each frame: `wantedTimer += dt`. Reset `wantedTimer = 0` on every wanted-bump event (any of the three triggers above OR §6.7's first-of-chain).
  - Each frame: if `wantedTimer > 30` AND no cop within 200px of player AND `wanted > 0`, decrement `wanted` and reset `wantedTimer = 0`.

§8.4 (heads HUD visual) lives in §13.4 — this section is logic only.
acceptance_criteria: Ramming a cop at >100 px/sec bumps `wanted` once per contact entry (edge-triggered). Ramming at >80 px/sec drains cop.health at 30/sec; cop death sets `cop.alive = false` and bumps `wanted` by 1. 30 seconds of clean play with no cop within 200px decrements `wanted` by 1, repeating until 0. The first-of-chain ped-kill bump from §6 still works (no regression).

title: §7 Police — spawn-by-wanted + chase AI + flashing light bar
description:
> A police car spawns at a random `.` (road) tile **at least 200 pixels from the player**, never inside a building.

Implement police per §7:
  - `let police = [];`. One array of cop-car objects.
  - state per §7.1: same shape as §3 but with `maxSpeed: 200, acceleration: 160, turnRate: 2.0`, plus `chasing: bool, health: 100`.
  - spawn rule per §7.2: count of alive cops on the map equals `wanted` (0–6). When wanted ticks up, spawn the missing car(s) within ~5s at a random `.` tile ≥200px from the player; never inside a `B`. When wanted drops (cooldown from §8.3), leave existing cops in place — they'll despawn the next time wanted ticks back up and they're already extra.
  - chase AI per §7.3 per frame per cop:
    - `dx = player.x - cop.x; dy = player.y - cop.y; dist = hypot(dx, dy)`
    - `targetAngle = atan2(dy, dx)`; steer via `angleDiff = wrap(targetAngle - cop.angle)` to `[-π, π]`. `angleDiff > 0.05` → right; `< -0.05` → left; else straight.
    - throttle: `dist > 60` accelerate to maxSpeed; `dist < 30` brake.
    - building collision: same center-vs-tile technique as §4.5.
    - ramming: if within 20px of player, `player.health -= 25 * dt`.
  - visual per §7.4: same shape as §3.3 (use the player-car drawing function with color overrides) — body `#1a1a3a`, roof `#0a0a1a`, 1px white outline. Light bar = 12×3 rectangle on the roof, alternates `#ff0000`/`#0000ff` every 200ms via `Math.floor(now/200) % 2`.

§7.5 siren is Bonus — skip (audio is out of scope per §16).
acceptance_criteria: Police cars spawn within ~5s of `wanted` ticking up; alive cop count tracks wanted level (0–6). Each cop chases the player via the §7.3 steer + throttle rules. Cops bounce off `B` tiles. Ramming drains player.health at 25/sec while within 20px. Visual is dark-navy body, white outline, 12×3 roof light bar alternating red↔blue every 200ms.

title: §6 Civilian pedestrians — wander/panic + run-over
description:
> **Spawn**: 15 pedestrians at startup. Each spawns on a random `=` (sidewalk) tile.

Implement peds per §6:
  - `let peds = [];` — one array. Spawn 15 at startup on random `=` (sidewalk) tiles (§6.1).
  - per-ped state per §6.2 — `{ x, y, angle, speed: 30, state: 'wander', stateTimer: random(2,5), alive: true }`.
  - `wander` (§6.3): move forward; every `stateTimer` seconds re-pick a random angle and `stateTimer` (2–5s). When player within 80px AND `|player.speed| > 50`, transition to `panic`.
  - `panic` (§6.4): `angle = atan2(self.y - player.y, self.x - player.x)`, `speed = 70`, hold 3s, back to `wander`.
  - run-over (§6.7): if `dist(ped, player) < 12` AND `|player.speed| > 30`, set `ped.alive = false`, `score += 100 * multiplier * Math.min(5, Math.max(1, chainCount))`, `chainCount++`, and on the FIRST kill of a chain `wanted = min(6, wanted + 1)`.
  - dead-ped visual (§6.8): `#5a0a0a` radius-4 filled circle, drawn on the ground; DO NOT remove from the array (§6.9 — no respawn).
  - §6.5 visual: 8×8 ped sprite — red body circle r=4, skin head circle r=2, black outline, direction-indicator line.

Shared state setup: if `score`, `multiplier`, `wanted`, `chainCount`, `chainTimer` aren't already declared at the top of game.js, declare them with the §12.1/§8.1 defaults (`0, 1, 0, 0, 0`). §8 and §12 refine the cooldown / persistence rules — don't over-build them here.

§6.6 panic `!` indicator is Bonus.
acceptance_criteria: 15 peds spawn on sidewalk tiles at game start. Peds wander; transition to `panic` when player car is within 80px and >50 px/sec. Run-over triggers `ped.alive = false`, score increment via the §6.7 formula, `chainCount++`, and `wanted = min(6, wanted + 1)` on first-of-chain. Dead peds render as red-brown splats and persist (no respawn). The shared variables are declared at the §12.1/§8.1 defaults.
notes: REGRESSION 2026-05-21: blocked by §2 (harness-vjb6) regression. spawnPeds crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined" because tileGrid was malformed. Once §2 is regenerated as a proper 30×40 grid, this section's logic should work as written — but re-verify by loading the page in a browser (or running the artifact through a smoke check) before re-closing.

title: §5 Camera — follow + clamp
description:
> **Tech: a `camera = { x, y }` object** holding the world coordinate of the **top-left corner of the screen**. Render by translating: `ctx.translate(-camera.x, -camera.y)` once at the start of the world-render pass.

Implement §5.1 + §5.2:
  - declare `let camera = { x: 0, y: 0 }`
  - per-frame: `camera.x = player.x - canvas.width/2`, `camera.y = player.y - canvas.height/2`
  - clamp to map bounds — `camera.x = max(0, min(camera.x, mapWidth - canvas.width))`, same for y. `mapWidth = 40*32 = 1280`, `mapHeight = 30*32 = 960`.
  - render pass: `ctx.save(); ctx.translate(-camera.x, -camera.y); <world render>; ctx.restore()`. Every world-coord draw (map from §2, player from §3, every later section) lives inside this block.

§5.3 (speed-based zoom-out) and §5.4 (lead the player) are Bonus — skip unless budget allows.

HUD draws AFTER the world pass with the transform reset (`ctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0)`) — that's §13.1, not here.
acceptance_criteria: Map scrolls as the player drives — moving toward the map's right edge reveals new terrain on the right. Camera clamps at map boundaries (no black void past perimeter buildings). World render is inside one save/translate/restore block; canvas transform is the identity outside that block. §5.3 and §5.4 not required.
close_reason: Closed

title: §4 Driving — forward/reverse/steer/handbrake/collision
description:
> **turning is proportional to current speed**. Stationary car cannot turn (this is GTA2-correct and easy to implement).

Wire driving controls per §4. Read input from the `keys` object — the actual key bindings come in §15, so for now read `keys.ArrowUp || keys.KeyW` etc. directly (matches the §15 mapping ahead of time):
  - §4.1 forward/reverse: accelerate when forward; brake-then-reverse when reverse; friction-toward-zero when neither
  - §4.2 steering proportional to current speed; `angle ±= turnRate * (speed/maxSpeed) * dt`. Stationary car must NOT turn.
  - §4.3 handbrake (Space): friction → ~600 while held; optional turnRate → ~3.6
  - §4.4 position update: `x += cos(angle)*speed*dt`, `y += sin(angle)*speed*dt`
  - §4.5 building collision via center-vs-tile (`floor(x/32), floor(y/32)`); on hit revert position AND `speed = -speed * 0.3`. Do NOT use polygon-vs-AABB.

§4.6 sidewalk penalty is Bonus — skip if budget tight; v6/v7/v8 lacked it and still passed.
acceptance_criteria: Forward accelerates to maxSpeed; reverse brakes first then reverses to maxReverseSpeed; friction returns speed to 0 with no input. Left/right steer; stationary car does NOT rotate. Handbrake (Space) decelerates faster. Driving into a `B` tile reverts position and produces a small bounce. All motion uses `dt` from §3.2. No polygon collision.
close_reason: Closed

title: §3 Player car — state + visual
description:
> **State** — a single object literal `player = { x, y, angle, speed, ... }`

Declare the player state object per §3.1 with EVERY field at the documented value (don't improvise the numerics — they're the contract for §4). Spawn at (480, 320) per §3.5; if that tile is a `B`, adjust the map or spawn rather than spawning inside a wall.

Wire the fixed-dt scaffold per §3.2: `dt = (now - lastNow) / 1000`, clamp to max 1/30 so a backgrounded tab doesn't teleport on resume. Store `lastNow`; every motion uses `dt` (never raw frame counts).

Draw the player per §3.3 — blue body, dark outline, roof, windshield, headlights, taillights, wheels — using the §3.4 transform pattern (save → translate(x,y) → rotate(angle) → draw each component centered on (0,0) → restore). Each visual element is its own fillRect in local space.

No driving controls yet — that's §4. No camera transform yet — that's §5; for now the car renders in world coords and may be off-screen if you didn't add the camera.
acceptance_criteria: `player` is an object literal with every §3.1 field at the documented value (no improvised numerics). Spawn world coord is (480, 320); spawn tile is not a building. Render shows a blue rotated rectangle at the spawn with roof, windshield, two headlights, two taillights, four wheels per §3.3. The draw call uses save/translate/rotate/restore (§3.4). `dt` is computed and clamped to 1/30 (§3.2).

title: §2 World map — tile grid + drawTile
description:
> **Tech: a tile grid stored as a multi-line string** in `game.js`. Each character is one tile. Render by iterating the grid and drawing each tile.

Build the world per §2:
  - tile grid as multi-line string with the §2.2 alphabet (`.` `=` `B` `+` `|` `-`)
  - 32px tiles, 40 cols × 30 rows → 1280×960 world pixels (§2.3)
  - map content satisfies §2.4 (perimeter buildings, 4-way street grid with ≥3 horiz + ≥3 vert roads, sidewalks, intersections). The reference layout in §2.4 may be copied verbatim — do NOT ship a blank canvas.
  - render loop is the row/col iterate in §2.5 with a single `drawTile(char, x, y)` switch
  - tile visuals per §2.6–§2.11. Road markings (`|`, `-`) draw the road background first, then the marking on top.
acceptance_criteria: 40×30 grid renders at 32px tiles (canvas shows the map, not blank). Tile palette matches §2.2 colors. Map has perimeter buildings, ≥3 horizontal and ≥3 vertical roads, sidewalks, intersections. Buildings show the §2.8 4-window pattern. Intersections (§2.9) are visually distinct from plain road. Road markings (`|`,`-`) draw the §2.10/§2.11 yellow dashes over a road background.

title: §1 Project shape — index.html + game.js skeleton
description:
> **Tech: one `requestAnimationFrame` callback** named `gameLoop`. Inside it: read input → update fixed-dt physics → render. No `setInterval`, no multiple loops.

  - reads `canvas.width`/`canvas.height` from JS rather than hardcoded (§1.6)

No game logic, no rendering yet — those land in §2+.

title: planner: actionable plan_add validation errors + system-prompt example
description:
Marks 2026-05-21 GTA2 QA pass (after harness-mzce). Planner now emits tool calls (good) and we have full observability (good), but the model cant reliably recover from plan_add validation errors:

Observed in .harness/planner_20260521T171908Z.log:
  1. World map: failed once (no blockquote), succeeded on retry. ✓
  2. Player car: failed once (no blockquote), then re-emitted the IDENTICAL broken call twice (DuplicateCallHook caught both), gave up.
  3. Driving: same shape as Player car. Failed, deduped, gave up.
  4. Turn 1: hallucinated six "Liberty City missions" that arent in the spec, all failed blockquote check, then plan_finish.

Two failures compound:
  - Model cant figure out the blockquote format from the current error message ("description must include a > blockquote of spec_quote. Format: > <the spec text>"). It re-emits the same description without the > prefix.
  - When confused, model hallucinates spec content rather than re-reading the actual spec.

Fix:
  1. Make the plan_add error message ACTIONABLE. Show:
     - the spec_quote that was attempted (truncated to ~200 chars)
     - the blockquote lines actually found in the description (lines starting with >)
     - explicit corrected example: "description=\"> <your spec_quote here>\\n\\nYour prose here.\""
  2. Add a CONCRETE worked example to PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT showing exactly what a valid plan_add call looks like (title + description with leading > blockquote + spec_quote + acceptance).
  3. Consider: when a plan_add fails validation, prepend a synthesis nudge to the next model round: "Your last plan_add failed because <reason>. Re-read the spec section if needed (read_file again), then retry with the corrected format."

Out of scope for this issue (file separately if needed):
  - Relaxing the blockquote-in-description requirement entirely (its useful for operator review).
  - Forcing re-read_file on each iteration (would slow the planner).
  - Adding plan_remove / plan_edit tools for the model to correct prior items.
acceptance_criteria: (1) plan_add validation error includes the attempted spec_quote AND the blockquote lines found in the description; (2) PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT contains a worked plan_add example; (3) test pins the new error message shape (substring assertion on attempted_quote + found_blockquotes); (4) test pins the worked example appears in the system prompt; (5) re-run against gta2-spec.md should produce >= 5 successfully-added items without dedupe failures (manual QA; not gated by test).

title: planner observability + tighter tool-call directives
description:
Marks 2026-05-21 GTA2 QA pass: harness drive plan against scratch/gta/spec/gta2-spec.md returned an empty draft (items: []). Root cause unknown today because the planner has ZERO observability — run_planner calls run_tool_loop without an observer, so we cant see which tools fired, what plan_add validation errors landed, or whether the model just emitted prose without any tool calls.

Two changes:

1. Observability. Pass an ObserverFn to run_tool_loop that appends one line per ToolLoopEvent to <workspace>/.harness/planner_<timestamp>.log. title: driver: executor loop (run_loop)
description:
Implement src/harness/driver/loop.py: the executor control flow.

API:
  - LoopConfig: epic_id, max_turns=20, profile="coding", workspace=None, resume_from=None, dry_run=False, log_path=None.
  - LoopResult: loop_run_id, epic_id, closed, halted_on, turns_used, exit_reason (Literal["success","halted","exhausted","interrupted","dry_run"]).
  - run_loop(adapter, bd, config) → LoopResult.

Control flow per iteration:
  1. SIGINT check (signal handler sets a flag; loop top checks it).
  2. turns_used >= max_turns → exit_exhausted.
  3. bd.ready_under_epic(epic_id) → if empty, exit_success.
  4. Take top of ready. Increment attempt_count.
  5. Build handoff. If dry_run: print handoff, return exit_reason="dry_run".
  6. Call orchestrator.tool_loop.run_tool_loop with:
     - system prompt = character core + handoff.render()
     - user message = "Drive this bd issue to closure. Call bd_close when the acceptance criteria are met."
     - tool registry = profile (default "coding")
     - NO retrieval block (handoff covers it)
     - NO persona rewrite pass
  7. Classify outcome: success = current_id in {call.args["issue_id"] for call in turn.tool_calls if call.name=="bd_close" and call.success} AND not turn.fabrication_fallback_fired.
  8. On success: bd.write_session_state(status="success"), state.closed_this_run.append, save state, log, loop.
  9. On first failure: state.last_failure[current_id] = <reason>, save state, log, loop.
  10. On second failure: bd.flag_human(current_id, reason=...), bd.write_session_state(status="halted"), save state, log, exit_halted.

Resume: if config.resume_from: state = LoopRunState.load(state_path(resume_from)) instead of fresh().

Progress log file (.harness/loop_runs/<id>.log by default, override via config.log_path): one line per turn with timestamp, attempt#, bd-id, outcome, reason. Plus one line per loop event (started, resumed, interrupted, halted, exhausted, success). Supports `tail -f` for live monitoring.

Driver does NOT go through harness chat — it imports run_tool_loop directly. The chat machinery does voice retrieval + persona rewrite + history tracking the driver doesn’t want.

This is phase 4 of the [epic] harness loop multi-turn driver.
acceptance_criteria: (1) run_loop with the control flow above; (2) SIGINT handler writes session-state bead and saves state before exit; (3) progress log writes one line per turn + lifecycle events; (4) --dry-run prints handoff and exits without running a turn; (5) --resume rehydrates state file; (6) test covers: success path closes 3 issues across 3 turns; (7) test covers: first-failure retry then halt-on-second-failure flow; (8) test covers: resume picks up at correct turn index.

title: [epic] harness loop: bd-driven multi-turn driver
description:
Multi-turn driver for harness that converts a free-form spec doc into a bd workplan (planner phase) and drives the workplan to closure turn by turn (executor phase). Designed during Marks 2026-05-20 GTA2 debug session — the failure mode of "implement from beginning to end" inside a single chat turn is well-understood; the fix is a driver that owns the multi-turn lifecycle and a deterministic handoff format that spans turns.

Two phases, separated by a YAML approval gate:
  1. Planner (harness plan --spec PATH) reads a spec doc with read-only tools + plan_add / plan_finish, dumps a YAML draft to ./harness-plan-draft.yaml. Operator reviews + edits. harness plan --commit creates the bd epic + children with deps. Spec quotes validated as substring matches.
  2. Executor (harness loop --epic ID) iterates bd ready under the epic. Per turn: claim top issue, assemble handoff (current bd issue + parent epic + files touched since loop start + recency-truncated thought:decision / thought:observation / open thought:question), call orchestrator.tool_loop.run_tool_loop directly (bypassing harness chat to avoid voice retrieval / persona rewrite), classify outcome (success = bd_close called AND fabrication_fallback did not fire). On first failure: retry same issue with prior-attempt-failure block prepended. On second failure: bd human flag + halt. Default cap: 20 turns.

Handoff format renders into the system prompt as a structured [SESSION HANDOFF] block, ≤1k tokens. Loop-run scoping via bd labels (loop-run-<id> on every thought-bead the driver writes), not timestamps or assignees. State persists to .harness/loop_runs/<loop_run_id>.json (atomic writes); harness loop --resume rehydrates.

Existing related work: harness-dset (catcher-aware fabrication_fallback text — improves the no-success-path UX for the executor), harness-2uso (auto-load on catalog-known unknown tool call — makes core_minimal viable for executors, though coding is the planned default profile).

Out of scope for this epic: token-cost caps (turn count only for v0), acceptance-criteria test runner (close = bd_close called, no automatic verification), planner emitting bd writes directly (YAML draft is the gate).

title: Auto-load on catalog-known unknown tool call
description:
In core_minimal sessions the model frequently calls a catalog-known tool (e.g. read_file, write_file) before issuing load_tool. Today src/harness/tools/base.py:262-288 returns a recovery hint and the model self-corrects on the next round, costing 2 wasted rounds per session (one per first-use of each tool). The existing write_file_redirect hook (hooks.py:5076-5081) sets the precedent: a pre_tool hook can transparently rewrite a malformed-but-recoverable call into the intended one within a single tool turn, instead of relying on round-trip error recovery.

Repro: Marks 2026-05-20 GTA2 session. tool_search returned 5 filesystem tools. Model emitted read_file directly (round 4), got the unknown_tool hint, called load_tool (round 5), retried read_file (round 6). Same pattern repeated for write_file (rounds 8-10). 4 of 10 rounds were pure recovery overhead.

Fix: add an AutoLoadOnUnknownHook in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py at the pre_tool phase. Gate: ctx.call.name not in registry.active_names() AND catalog.get(name) is not None. Action: invoke load_tool builder in-hook (registry has the catalog reference; load_tool.py already does this work), then return Continue so the original call proceeds against the now-active registry. Failure modes (builder raises, session-state-required, etc.) fall through to the existing unknown_tool error path — no regression in observability.

Placement: BEFORE write_file_redirect so a write_file call on a non-existent path still resolves to a clean write_file load (vs. redirect-then-load).
acceptance_criteria: (1) New pre_tool hook auto-loads catalog-known tools before the call dispatches; (2) registry exposes the catalog reference the hook needs (or hook reuses load_tool internals); (3) test covers: first-time read_file in core_minimal completes in one round, not three; (4) test covers: builder-raises path still surfaces the original failure; (5) write_file_redirect interaction tested (auto-load then redirect to edit_file should still work).

description:

Try rephrasing, or ask me something I can answer without live data." That text is a lie when tools landed cleanly and the actual pathology was a preamble/intent loop after partial real progress.
