title: Structural intent-restatement loop catcher
description:
Mark's 2026-05-21 follow-up GTA2 session emitted four discarded retries with the pattern:

  Reply 0: "I'll implement the GTA 2 browser clone according to the spec. Let me start by creating the required files."
  Reply 1: "Now I'll create the game.js file with the implementation. I'll work through this systematically…"
  Reply 2: "Now I'll create the game.js file with the implementation. Let me start by writing the basic structure…"
  Reply 3: "Now I'll create the game.js file with the implementation of the GTA 2 clone according to the spec…"

Replies 1-3 share the opening "Now I'll create the game.js file with the implementation" — about 56 chars of LCP. PreambleLoopHook (harness-jwp3) has a 100-char floor and does NOT fire. The 8K token ceiling eventually terminated the loop, but ~19 minutes of wall-clock was burned producing four discards of the same intent restatement.

## Why not lower the LCP floor

100 chars is the right floor for the textual LCP signal — lower thresholds trip on generic conversational openers ("Let me check the file", "I'll search for X") that aren't pathological. Picking ~50 chars on LCP alone would catch this session but inflate false positives on normal multi-step planning.

The right shape is a STRUCTURAL gate: when both the current reply AND the most recent discarded opening start with an "intent-statement" regex (I'll | Let me | Now I'll | I need to | First I'll | I'm going to + verb + object), and they share a meaningful prefix in that opening structure, the model is restating intent in the same shape as before — that's the loop, regardless of textual LCP length.

## Fix shape

New bail catcher IntentRestatementLoopHook, placed AFTER PreambleLoopHook (the long-LCP catcher is more specific) but still before truncated/teaser/etc. Detection:

1. Current reply opens with the intent-phrase regex (the catcher's own pattern: case-insensitive match against the first ~120 chars).
2. Most recent discarded opening ALSO opens with that regex.
3. LCP between current and most-recent ≥ _INTENT_RESTATEMENT_MIN_LCP (default 30 chars). This catches cases where the prefix shares the intent phrase + verb + object slot ("Now I'll create the game.js") but diverges past that.

When all three: Nudge with text that names the structural failure ("you're emitting the same intent restatement in a slightly different wording — skip the planning, emit a tool call or concrete content").

## Why this is distinct from PreambleLoopHook

PreambleLoopHook: textual signal, high precision (≥100 char LCP), low recall.
IntentRestatementLoopHook: structural signal + lower LCP floor, higher recall on the shape Mark just saw.

Two narrow catchers are easier to tune + audit than one fuzzy one. PreambleLoopHook stays first in pipeline; IntentRestatementLoopHook runs immediately after so the more specific signal wins first-match-wins ordering.

## Acceptance

- New unit tests: (a) fires on Mark's 2026-05-21 shape (replies 1-3 with ~56-char LCP, intent-phrase opener); (b) passes when only one side opens with intent-phrase; (c) passes when both open with intent-phrase but LCP < threshold; (d) passes when LCP ≥ threshold but neither opens with intent-phrase (would be a different signal anyway); (e) pipeline placement pin (after preamble_loop, before truncated).
- New attribution fixture entry where the catcher carries unique load (disabling it lets replies 1-3 pass as final answers).
- Existing PreambleLoopHook tests stay green; the two catchers don't interfere because PreambleLoop checks LCP ≥ 100 first.

## Out of scope

- Lowering the existing PreambleLoopHook threshold. Keep its 100-char floor where it is.
- Cross-reply structural similarity beyond first-N-chars (e.g. detecting the same intent emerging in the middle of a reply). YAGNI.
- The wall-clock cap (harness-8y9e) is independent — that bounds runaway sessions regardless of catcher behavior.

## Related

- harness-jwp3 (PreambleLoopHook, landed; complementary).
- harness-2h3m (post-dup completion fabrication, landed).
- harness-8y9e (wall-clock cap, open; orthogonal backstop).
- harness-gt0m (default tightening, open; orthogonal).
close_reason: Shipped IntentRestatementLoopHook (bail phase, immediately after PreambleLoopHook). Structural complement to PreambleLoop: requires BOTH current reply and most recent discarded opening to match _INTENT_PHRASE_RE (case-insensitive intent-phrase like 'Now I'll create', 'Let me write', 'I'll implement') AND share ≥30 chars of LCP. Catches the Qwen3-Coder-30B 2026-05-21 GTA2 shape (~56-char shared opening under 'Now I'll create the game.js') that PreambleLoop's 100-char floor missed. 8 new unit tests + 1 attribution fixture entry (preamble_loop fixture also reshaped to use non-intent-phrase openings so the two catchers have non-overlapping attribution coverage); 2991 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: Transparently redirect write_file on existing path to edit_file
description:
When the model calls write_file on a path that already exists, the current path is wasteful: write_file errors, the model parses the error, decides to use edit_file, edit_file is not loaded, the model calls load_tool, then finally calls edit_file. Four round-trips for what should be one.

Visible in Mark's 2026-05-20 GTA2 session: write_file failed on game.js, then edit_file failed with "unknown tool", then the model had to load_tool. Each failure consumed a model round.

## Fix shape

New pre_tool hook (WriteFileRedirectHook in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py) that intercepts write_file calls and transparently routes them to edit_file when the target exists. Skip(result=...) feeds the edit_file result back as the tool-role message named for the original write_file call, with a one-line prefix explaining the redirect so the model knows what happened.

Behavior matrix:
- write_file(path, content) where path does NOT exist → Continue (normal write_file path)
- write_file(path, content, overwrite=True) → Continue (user explicitly asked to replace)
- write_file(path, content) where path EXISTS and content looks like an edit (>= half existing size, OR >= 1KB) → redirect to edit_file(path, old_string=current, new_string=content); auto-load edit_file if not active; Skip with the edit_file result prefixed by "(write_file → edit_file: file existed)"
- write_file(path, content) where path EXISTS and content looks like an accidental shrink (< half existing size AND < 1KB) → Skip with the same safety-shrink error write_file would have raised. Preserves the existing harness-2tq guard.

## Auto-load coupling

When the hook redirects, it also activates edit_file in the registry (the same pattern load_tool dispatch uses). The model then has edit_file available for subsequent rounds — no separate load_tool needed.

## Why pre_tool + Skip, not a new outcome variant

The PreToolOutcome = Continue | Skip protocol is currently the only outcome surface. A clean "RedirectCall" variant would also work but extends the protocol; this issue stays inside the existing shape by dispatching edit_file from inside the hook and feeding back its result. The tool-role message names the original call (write_file) so the model knows it was its emission that got handled; the prefix tells it the redirect happened.

Subsequent landings (separate bd) could introduce a RedirectCall outcome and audit the assistant turn as edit_file directly. Not in scope here — that is a protocol change that affects more than one hook.

## Acceptance

- New test: write_file on non-existent path runs as before (no redirect, no auto-load).
- New test: write_file on existing path with content >= half size redirects, edit_file becomes active, result.output starts with the redirect prefix.
- New test: write_file with overwrite=True bypasses the hook entirely.
- New test: write_file on existing path with content under half size AND under 1KB does NOT redirect; emits the safety-shrink error.
- Existing write_file + edit_file tests stay green.
- Full pytest green; ruff + mypy strict clean.

## Out of scope

- Renaming or removing the existing write_file error path. The hook only fires when edit_file is in the catalog; absent that, the original error message + multi-round recovery is the fallback.
- Replacing edit_file's semantics. The hook synthesizes a call that edit_file already supports (full-replace via old_string=current, new_string=new).
- The PreambleLoop catcher (harness-jwp3) which is independent.

## Related

harness-cck4 (load_tool dispatch recovery — same auto-load pattern this hook reuses). harness-2tq (write_file safety-shrink check this hook preserves). harness-od8w (tag-masker fix — landed; orthogonal).
close_reason: Implemented WriteFileRedirectHook (pre_tool). When write_file fires on an existing path and overwrite is not set, the hook reads the current contents, dispatches edit_file(path, old_string=current, new_string=content) directly, and feeds back the result via Skip — single tool turn instead of the 4-round write_file → unknown_tool → load_tool → edit_file recovery. Preserves harness-2tq safety-shrink guard. Idempotent on identical content. Falls through cleanly when edit_file isn't available. Bidirectional load_tool companion pairing (write_file ↔ edit_file) makes the second tool land alongside the first so ensure_edit_file_active doesn't usually need to do anything. 8 new unit tests + companion-coverage; 2967 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: Catch runaway-preamble loop (consecutive retries share long opening prefix)
description:
Mark's 2026-05-20 GTA2 session emitted six consecutive 'I need to implement the full GTA2 clone according to the spec. Let me create a proper implementation...' drafts, each truncated, each retried with a doubled budget. No catcher fired because:

- Teaser only gates on 0-tool-calls replies, and these drafts DID call tools.
- truncated_retry assumes 'more tokens = closer to finishing'; past 2-3 retries this is wrong — it's a runaway loop, not progress.
- bail_retry catchers (FabricatedSearch, MetaConfirm, FalseSuccess, etc.) all gate on content shape, not on inter-draft similarity.

## Fix shape

New post_model catcher:  (or similar — pick the term that names the pathology cleanly). Tracks the opening N characters of every discarded draft in the current turn. When two consecutive retries share a >100-char identical opening, trip with a Nudge that breaks the loop:

- If retries-left > 0: Nudge text 'You opened with the same sentence twice. Skip the intent restatement — your next reply must START with code or a tool call, no preamble.'
- If retries-left == 0: Halt with a canned refusal naming the issue ('I'm stuck restating intent. Try --tool-set coding or break this into a narrower step.').

## Where it lives

src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py. New PostModelContext-using hook, registered in default_hook_pipeline. Carries per-turn state via a small helper class (similar to BanterStreakTracker) or via a frozenset of seen openings on the BailContext (cleaner — no new state-on-self).

Actually cleanest: BailController already holds per-turn state. Add  to it. Every truncated_retry / bail_retry path appends the discarded draft's first 200 chars before consuming the retry. New catcher reads from a snapshot fed into the BailContext.

## Acceptance

- New attribution test: scripted adapter that emits the same 150-char opening three times in a row. After the second emission, PreambleLoop fires (visible as a bail_retry event with catcher='preamble_loop' or a Halt finalize, depending on shape chosen). Without the catcher: three full retries fire.
- Existing eval suite shows zero regression on non-loop cases.
- Threshold tuning: ship with N=100 chars / 2 consecutive matches as the default; expose as a module constant so tuning is one edit.

## Why this matters

The current behavior burns 3x the wall-clock budget AND leaves the user staring at progress-looking markers ('⋯ truncated, retrying with wider budget…') while the model digs deeper into the same hole. Mark's session went 6 retries before he interrupted. Each retry at growing budgets means the wasted time grows geometrically (1024 + 2048 + 4096 + 8192 = ~15s + ~27s + ~55s + ~110s on M4 Pro). Catching at retry 2 saves the user 3+ minutes of staring.

## Related

harness-738f (budget marker — landed; complements this by making the pathology diagnosable inline, but this catcher actually breaks the loop).
close_reason: Shipped PreambleLoopHook (bail phase, first in pipeline order). Captures the first 200 chars of every discarded draft in _BailController.discarded_openings; the catcher checks longest-common-prefix between the current reply and the most recent discarded opening, firing a Nudge when LCP ≥ 100 chars. Placement-first means a reply that's both truncated AND looping gets the loop-break nudge instead of another budget-doubling retry that wouldn't help. 7 new unit tests + 1 new attribution fixture entry that proves the catcher has a unique effect (disabling it lets the looped retries pass as final answers). 2983 total pass; ruff + mypy strict clean.

title: Tighten default token budgets to match 7B's actual sweet spot
description:
Two defaults currently inherited from optimistic upper bounds rather than measured operating points. Tightening both lands more useful turns out-of-the-box and kills most truncated_retry pathology without raising any ceilings.

## 1. Per-round max_tokens: 1024 → 2048

run_tool_loop signature at tool_loop.py:883 sets max_tokens=1024 and wrap_up_max_tokens=1024. With tool-use, the model often needs to emit a tool call AND a paragraph of reasoning in a single round; 1024 is tight and trips truncated_retry on routine tool-use turns. 2048 is humane, costs ~13s extra wall-clock at 150 tok/s on M4 Pro (still feels interactive), and stays well under the 4-6K coherence ceiling for Qwen 2.5 7B.

Touchpoints:
- src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py:883 — run_tool_loop default
- src/harness/cli.py — chat command passes max_tokens through; surface a CLI flag if not present (--max-tokens), default to 2048
- src/harness/tui/chat_app.py:512 — ChatApp constructor default
- src/harness/cli_classic.py — classic REPL default
- _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING (32768) and _BAIL_RETRIES_PER_TURN (3) UNCHANGED — they're the safety rail, not the operating point

## 2. MLX context_window: 131_072 → 32_768

mlx.py:53 defaults context_window=131_072 (Qwen 2.5's YaRN-extended max). Three problems:
- Native non-YaRN limit is 32K; past that, attention quality degrades + lost-in-the-middle hurts retrieval from packed contexts
- compaction/runner.should_compact fires at compact_at * context_window. At 128K with default 0.7 threshold, that's ~91K — effectively never fires interactively. At 32K it fires at ~22K which is the actual sweet spot
- KV cache memory at 128K full ≈ 8 GB (single-turn). At 32K, ≈ 2 GB. Plenty of headroom either way on 48 GB but lower memory pressure helps tool-loop hot paths

Touchpoint: src/harness/model/mlx.py:53 — change the parameter default. Keep callers' ability to override (--context-window or env var if it exists) so long-doc work can still opt into 128K + YaRN explicitly.

## Why one issue, not two

Both are 'tighten defaults to match where Qwen 2.5 7B is actually competent.' Lockstep change reduces churn — the same regression run validates both. If we split later we can.

## Out of scope

- Adapter-side ceiling enforcement (still 32K per round). 
- Changing _BAIL_RETRIES_PER_TURN. 
- Tunables for 32B model — its sweet spot differs but it's not the default. Document the override pattern in usage.md if not already.
- Bumping max_rounds. Separate axis; file separately if we want it.

## Acceptance

- New defaults applied + propagated through CLI / TUI / classic REPL.
- Tests updated for any that asserted on the old defaults.
- No new test failures in the full suite.
- truncated_retry rate on the existing eval suite drops (or stays flat). If it rises, something else is wrong.

Related: harness-738f (truncated_retry marker should show budget progression — lands first ideally so this change's impact is visible inline).
close_reason: Tightened operating-point defaults. run_tool_loop max_tokens 1024→2048 (also wrap_up_max_tokens 1024→2048); ChatApp max_tokens 1024→2048; MLXAdapter context_window 131_072→32_768. _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING, _BAIL_RETRIES_PER_TURN, and compact_at left unchanged — at the new ctx-window default, compact_at=0.8 fires at ~26K which is the sweet spot for Qwen 2.5 7B / Qwen3-Coder-30B native attention. 2991 tests pass; ruff + mypy strict clean. No doc updates needed — usage.md / roadmap.md didn't pin the old numbers.

title: Mid-turn message injection: soft-inject path
description:
Add a third input mode to the TUI alongside Enter (queue) and Ctrl+X (interrupt): a soft-inject path that appends new user messages into the running tool loop at iteration boundaries without restarting the turn.

Design:
- run_tool_loop gains an optional inbox: Callable[[], list[ChatMessage]] | None parameter, drained at top of while (tool_loop.py:1157) and after _execute_tool_calls (tool_loop.py:1279). Never between assistant(tool_calls=...) and its tool-role results (Qwen 2.5 template invariant).
- ChatApp grows a separate _state.pending_injections deque distinct from pending_prompts. New keybinding submits to the inject queue while is_busy; existing Enter behavior unchanged.
- Injected messages echo into the transcript with an [injected] marker so timing is visible.
- Multiple injections drained at the same boundary append as N separate user-role ChatMessages (no concatenation).
- turn_user_message stays frozen to the original prompt — grounding hooks must not see injected text as the turn's subject.

Out of scope: classic REPL (no concurrent input surface).
close_reason: Implemented soft-inject path. run_tool_loop gains optional inbox callable drained at top of while loop and after _execute_tool_calls; appends drained user-role ChatMessages as separate turns, emits message_injected events. TUI grows pending_injections deque + alt+enter binding + action_inject / _inject_prompt / _drain_injections / _promote_stale_injections (stale injections fall through into pending_prompts on turn end or interrupt). turn_user_message stays frozen to original prompt. 5 new tests; 2955 total pass; ruff + mypy clean.

title: tool_search: promote 'family' filter over 'tag' in schema description
description:
The tool_search schema lists tag before family and emphasizes tag in the parameter help. Small models reach for tag first and get burned because the catalog's most discoverable axis is family ('filesystem', 'research', 'memory', 'ops'), not tag (which are fine-grained capability words like 'read', 'open', 'ls').

Look at catalog.py BUILTIN_TOOL_METADATA: every tool has exactly one family but its tags are subdivisions of that family. The model's mental model 'I need filesystem tools' maps cleanly to family=, not tag=.

Fix: reorder parameter declarations so family comes before tag in the JSONSchema. Rewrite both descriptions:
  - family: 'PRIMARY axis — restrict to tools in this family (filesystem/research/memory/ops/reckon/git/meta).'
  - tag: 'Fine-grained capability filter within a family. Use family= first; only narrow with tag= when family= still returns too many.'
Update the docstring example block to use family= as the canonical pattern.

Pair with the tag→family auto-rescue (separate issue) — together they make the discovery flow forgiving of the most common small-model mistake.
close_reason: Closed

title: tool_search: auto-rescue tag=<family-name> by retrying as family=
description:
When a caller passes tag=<X> and X is the literal name of a registered family (e.g. tag='filesystem' or tag='research'), the current intersection yields zero because tags are tuple membership and families are scalar. The query-only fallback fires, wasting a round and producing weaker results.

Repro: small-model session on --tool-set core_minimal kept calling tool_search(query='read', tag='filesystem') — every call fell back to query-only because no tool carries 'filesystem' in its tag tuple. 8 turns of thrash before list_dir got loaded; would have been 1 turn with family='filesystem'.

Fix: in tool_search.py phase 2/3, if tag is set, the candidates list is empty, AND tag matches a family in the catalog, retry as family=tag. Add a fallback_note that says 'fell back to family=X — tag and family aren't the same axis'. Keeps the existing query-priority semantics (3b runs before family-rescue).
close_reason: Closed

title: tool_search no-results message must teach capability-shaped queries
description:
Session repro 2026-05-20 (GTA-clone query, Qwen3-Coder-30B): user asked about game engines / frameworks. The model called tool_search with topic queries instead of capability queries:

  tool_search(query='game engine')        -> no tools found
  tool_search(query='2D game framework')  -> no tools found
  tool_search(query='game development')   -> duplicate-deduped
  tool_search(query='framework', tag='research') -> duplicate-deduped
  tool_search(query='engine', tag='research')    -> duplicate-deduped
  tool_search(query='Python game framework', tag='research') -> duplicate-deduped
  introspect(scope='tools')
  -> refusal: "I don't have access to tools that can search the web…"

search_web IS in the catalog (tags: search/web/lookup/weather/news), but every query was the *topic* of inquiry, never the *action verb*. The catalog's substring index has no "game"/"engine" tokens because those are subject-matter terms, not capability terms. Model concluded "no such tool exists" and refused.

Same shape would have helped harness-wpo0 (Kenya/ostrich): that model also failed to land on search_web from tool_search.

Root cause: the tool_search spec description DOES teach "retry with the abstract action ('search', 'web', 'lookup', 'fetch')", but the model only reads the spec at schema-rendering time. By the time it's iterating queries, it's reading the TOOL OUTPUT, and the current empty-result line is too curt:
  "no tools found (query='game engine')"
…to nudge a recovery. The model has nothing to anchor on, so it varies adjacent topic words instead.

Fix: make the empty-result message itself carry the recovery hint. When tool_search returns zero hits, surface a clear capability-shaped-query recovery line — examples included — so the next emission has a fighting chance to land.

Proposed message:
  "no tools found ({constraints}).
   Recovery: the catalog indexes tools by CAPABILITY (what they DO), not by topic. Try a capability-shaped query — e.g. query='search' to find data-gathering tools, query='lookup' / 'fetch' / 'time' / 'compute' / 'read' for the action you actually need. Topic words ('weather in Nairobi', 'game engine', 'JEPA architecture') will not match — they're subject matter, not capability."

Acceptance:
- ToolSearchTool empty-result branch returns the new recovery-bearing message.
- New unit test confirms the message contains: query echo, the word "capability", and at least one example capability term.
- Existing tests that asserted on the literal "no tools found (..." string update to match the new shape (substring assertions where reasonable, full-string only where the test specifically pins the wording).
- No changes to spec description needed — it already teaches the same lesson at schema-render time; this bead targets the output-time recovery path.

Out of scope (separate beads if worth):
- Catalog "capability index" suggesting hot tokens dynamically. Hardcoded list of common verbs is sufficient.
- duplicate_call interaction (model emitted 4 deduped queries after the 2 misses — also a recovery issue, but on a different axis).

Companion: harness-wpo0 (bare factual fabrication when meta-tools only ran) and harness-yczi (unknown-tool catalog-aware error) are siblings — same family of "model can't land on the right tool".
close_reason: tool_search's empty-result message now carries the recovery hint inline: echoes failed constraints, names topic-vs-capability distinction explicitly, lists example verbs (search/lookup/fetch/read/time/compute/write), reminds of load_tool follow-up. Hint scoped to empty branch only — success path stays clean. 3 new unit tests + the existing miss test upgraded to assert recovery shape. Class docstring updated. Suite 2936 → 2939. Commit: 9b15c06.

title: search_web: annotate denylisted hits so model skips known-403 hosts
description:
Session repro 2026-05-20 (Nairobi weather query): model called search_web, picked www.accuweather.com from results, called fetch_url, got the denylist short-circuit (host previously logged HTTP 403). The denylist did its job — the network call was avoided — but the model wasted a round on a host search_web should have known to deprioritize.

Current state:
- search_web (src/harness/tools/search_web.py) accepts allowed_hosts, classifies every result against the allowlist, floats allowlisted hits to the top, marks them `[allowlisted]` vs `[external]`.
- The denylist (src/harness/store/fetch_denylist.py, harness-4dgm) lives in the same per-character harness.sqlite and exposes is_blocked(host) → DenylistEntry | None with a 30-day TTL.
- The two never talk. search_web has no awareness of the denylist, so a denylisted host can surface in the top N results and the model has no signal until fetch_url shorts it out.

Fix: thread FetchDenylistStore into SearchWebTool the same way allowed_hosts is threaded today.

Two design choices on how to surface the signal:
  (a) Filter denylisted results out entirely. Strongest — the model can't pick what it can't see.
  (b) Annotate them `[denylisted]` (or `[denylisted — last status NNN]`) and sort below `[external]`. Preserves audit visibility; matches the existing allowlist-annotation pattern.

Going with (b): consistent with the allowlist surface, keeps the audit log readable, and a marked-but-still-visible entry teaches the model the connection between the marker and the eventual fetch_url short-circuit. Filtering can be a later opt-in if the marker isn't enough in practice.

Sort order: allowlisted > external > denylisted. Stable within each group (preserves DDG's intra-group ranking).

Acceptance:
- SearchWebTool gains a `denylist: FetchDenylistStore | None = None` field (mirror of `allowed_hosts`).
- call() classifies each result against denylist.is_blocked(host) and stores the flag on _Result.
- When denylist is set, results sort allowlisted > external > denylisted; sort key is stable.
- When denylist is set, the marker shape is `[denylisted — HTTP NNN]` so the model sees the reason inline. Allowlisted / external markers still show when allowed_hosts is set.
- CLI bootstrap (cli.py:_build_tool_registry_for_tui + cli_classic.py) passes the same FetchDenylistStore handle that FetchUrlTool already gets.
- Tests:
  * denylisted host gets the marker
  * denylisted hit sorts below external
  * no denylist → existing behavior unchanged (no marker, no sort)
  * allowlist + denylist together: allowlisted wins ordering even if a host is somehow in both
- No fixture change required; the existing search_web tool fixtures don't construct a denylist. Optional follow-up: a fixture that pins the marker shape end-to-end.

Companion: harness-vf6c (URL grounding investigation) — same family of "search_web → fetch_url handoff is too lossy". Separate failure modes; both worth landing.
close_reason: SearchWebTool gains a denylist field mirroring allowed_hosts. When set, denylisted hosts get '[denylisted — HTTP NNN]' marker and sink below '[external]'. Three-tier sort: allowlisted > external > denylisted, stable within tier. Carve-outs: allowlist wins on a same-host clash; no allowlist => no spurious external marker; expired entries don't annotate. CLI bootstrap (cli.py + cli_classic.py) passes the FetchUrlTool denylist handle. 7 new tests cover the motivating repro + status echo + carve-outs + sort. Suite 2929 → 2936. Commit: ff1dffd.

title: 'unknown tool' error should teach load_tool recovery when tool exists in catalog
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 (EV-production query): model called search_web directly without calling load_tool first. The orchestrator returned:

  unknown tool: 'search_web'. Available: ['load_tool', 'tool_search', 'introspect']

The error tells the model WHAT'S currently available but NOT that search_web exists in the catalog and just needs to be activated. The model interpreted 'unknown tool' as 'doesn't exist anywhere', retried tool_search instead of calling load_tool, and entered a doom loop.

Fix: error message is conditional on whether the called name is in the catalog.

  - If name IN catalog (just not active):
    'unknown tool: <name>. The tool exists in the catalog but is not active in this session. Call load_tool(name=<name>) first to activate it, then retry. Currently active: [<list>].'

  - If name NOT in catalog at all (the existing case):
    'unknown tool: <name>. Not in the catalog. Currently active: [<list>]. Use tool_search to find an available tool, or tell the user you cannot answer.'

Acceptance:
- src/harness/tools/base.py (or wherever the registry's 'unknown tool' error is constructed) gains a catalog-presence check.
- ToolRegistry.call (or its caller) consults the ToolCatalog before erroring — if the name is in the catalog, return the load_tool-recovery message; otherwise the standard not-in-catalog message.
- Tests: unit-test the registry error path for both shapes (in-catalog name not-active → recovery hint, not-in-catalog name → standard).
- No fixture change needed — the error path runs at registry-dispatch time and the existing tool_search_loop fixture would naturally consume the new error text. Optionally add a positive-recovery fixture: model emits search_web (unknown) → gets the load_tool hint → emits load_tool → emits search_web → succeeds.

Tight change. Low false-positive risk — the recovery hint only fires when the catalog lookup succeeds.

Companion: harness-? tool_search_loop attempts-counter — same session repro, different failure mode (the loop itself).
close_reason: ToolRegistry now consults an optional catalog handle in the unknown-tool error path. Production CLI bootstrap (cli.py + cli_classic.py) wires the session catalog so catalog-known names get a 'call load_tool(name=X) first' recovery hint; genuine misses keep pointing at tool_search. Eval/subagent/web registries stay catalog-less (legacy single shape). 4 new unit tests + existing test_loop_handles_unknown_tool_gracefully pass. Suite 2917 passed. Commit: 8b37138.

title: tool_search_loop misses dedup-masked attempts (duplicate_call hides the loop)
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 (EV-production query): user asked 'how many EVs were produced in 2023? Of those EVs what percentage were non-Tesla?'. Model entered a 10+ round doom loop calling tool_search and search_web (search_web wasn't loaded, so it errored 'unknown tool'). tool_search_loop catcher (harness-lmwm) didn't fire even though the model made many tool_search attempts.

Root cause: pre_tool pipeline order is:
  1. DuplicateCallHook
  2. ToolSearchLoopHook  
  3. ArgumentGroundingHook

DuplicateCallHook Skips on exact-args repeats and the call NEVER reaches ToolSearchLoopHook OR adds an entry to seen_calls. ToolSearchLoopHook counts entries in seen_calls — and seen_calls only grows on EXECUTED calls (the first attempt with given args). 10 deduped tool_search attempts with the same args register as 1 entry in seen_calls; the threshold of 2 priors never trips.

Two-layer fix:

LAYER 1: Add attempted_calls counter to PreToolContext.
  - Orchestrator tracks every tool_call the model EMITTED this turn, regardless of dedup/skip outcome.
  - PreToolContext gains `attempted_calls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], int]` (or similar) — call_key → count of emissions.
  - This is what tool_search_loop should count. duplicate_call still uses seen_calls (correct — it cares about prior RESULTS to re-issue).

LAYER 2: ToolSearchLoopHook counts attempts.
  - Replace `prior_tool_search = sum(1 for n in names_seen if n == "tool_search")` with `prior_tool_search = sum(count for (name, _), count in ctx.attempted_calls.items() if name == "tool_search")`.
  - Threshold of 2+ prior tool_search ATTEMPTS now sees the dedup-masked loop.

Acceptance:
- src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py PreToolContext gains attempted_calls.
- Orchestrator (tool_loop.py) populates attempted_calls EVERY time a tool_call is emitted (before pre_tool dispatch — so the current call is also counted as attempted).
- ToolSearchLoopHook updated to use attempted_calls.
- Unit tests: 5 tool_search emissions with same args → on the 3rd one Skip fires (threshold = 2 prior attempts + this 3rd = trigger).
- Existing tests for tool_search_loop still pass.
- Doom-loop scenario fixture (positive case for EV-production shape) added to evals/orchestrator/tool_search_loop.yaml.

Companion: harness-? 'unknown tool' error teaches load_tool recovery — same session repro.

Low-risk change. The new field is additive on the context; only one catcher reads it today.
close_reason: attempted_calls counter shipped on PreToolContext. Increments AFTER pre_tool dispatch (PRIOR-only state for catchers). Tool_search_loop reads it instead of seen_calls. load_tool reset also reads it. 2 new tests pin the repro + load_tool reset. Suite 2913.

title: tool_intent regex misses indirect intent ('I will need to', 'I will use', 'Let's proceed with')
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 (gum-export query): user asked 'which country is the largest export of gum? cite your sources'. Model called tool_search (returned 7 candidates), then emitted text-only:

  'I found that the query "largest export of gum" did not match any
  specific tool in my catalog. To find the largest export of gum, I
  will need to search the web. I will use the `search_web` tool to
  gather this information. Let's proceed with the search.'

No load_tool, no search_web, no tool_call at all. The reply IS the final answer — and it doesn't actually answer the question.

The existing TOOL_INTENT_RE matches:
  (I'll|I will|I need to|I should|I'm going to|let me|let's|now I'll|...)\s+
  (search|look up|find|check|read|run|fetch|call|invoke|execute|list|
  grep|edit|write|open|browse|query|retrieve|download|inspect|examine)

It misses the variants the model used:
  - 'I will need to search' — 'will' + 'need to' + 'search'. Interposed 'need to' breaks the direct adjacency.
  - 'I will use the `search_web` tool' — 'will' + 'use'. 'use' is not in the action-verb list.
  - 'Let's proceed with the search' — 'let's' + 'proceed'. 'proceed' not in the list.

Fix — expand TOOL_INTENT_RE with two additions:

(1) Action-verb list: add 'use', 'proceed (with)', 'go (ahead)', 'gather', 'pull', 'consult', 'reach for', 'engage'. These are common verbs the model uses to euphemize 'I will call the tool'.

(2) Interposing adverb / modal cluster: allow one or two filler words between the intent phrase and the action verb. e.g. 'I will (need to|have to|now|first|then|just) <verb>'. Keep the cluster tight to avoid false positives:

    (i'?ll|i\s+will|...)\s+
    (?:(?:need|have|want)\s+to\s+|now\s+|just\s+|first\s+|then\s+|"
    "go\s+(?:ahead\s+and\s+)?|"
    ")?
    (?:search|...|use|proceed|gather|pull|consult|engage|...)

(3) 'Let's proceed (with|to) ...' variant — capture as a top-level alternative, not just an intent + verb pair, because 'proceed' often stands without an object.

Tests:
- Positive: the 3 variants from the repro all fire when no tool_call emitted.
- Control: an actual tool_call alongside the intent text passes (existing ToolIntentHook gate).
- Control: 'I will use the data' / 'I will use my training' — benign 'use' that doesn't refer to a tool → must NOT fire. The gate is conservative because 'use' is overloaded; check that the object is tool-ish OR the surrounding context isn't (a follow-up sentence naming what 'use' applied to).

Sibling beads from same session pattern:
- harness-bylm (closed): same regex-narrowness shape, for FABRICATED_WEB_CLAIM_RE.
- harness-1jca, harness-lyyr: bigger fixes still queued.

Quick fix. Probably 30 mins including tests. Worth interleaving between the in-flight catcher work.
close_reason: Three regex additions land the gum-export trace variants: (1) interposing cluster between intent phrase and action verb, (2) 'proceed (with|to|by)' top-level alternative, (3) 'use ... tool' branch with tool-naming-object requirement. 5 new tests, teaser fixture reworked to maintain attribution-eval load-bearingness. Suite: 2881 passed. Pushed.

title: geography tool: country/region lookup using shared gazetteer with harness-lyyr
description:
Companion to harness-lyyr (scope-constraint verification). The catcher needs a static REGION_COUNTRIES data table to validate that a country named in the reply is actually in the user's named region; this bead exposes that same data through a tool the model can call PROACTIVELY before committing to an answer.

Why both surfaces:
- The catcher is a defensive backstop — fires after the fact when the model's reply violates the user's scope. The model can't skip it.
- The tool is a proactive primitive — the model uses it BEFORE answering when it suspects scope ambiguity. Lower cognitive load than 'check then bail'; the model just gets the answer it needs.
- Shared data file means one build, two surfaces. Same data, same maintenance.

Pattern matches existing deterministic-data tools (sun.py, tz_convert.py, date_math.py) — read-tier, no external network, small schema overhead.

Tool shape (proposed):
  src/harness/tools/geography.py
  GeographyTool with two calls:
    geography(country=<name>) -> {country, alpha2, alpha3, region, subregion,
                                  continent, capital, neighbors, area_km2,
                                  population_2024}
    geography(region=<name>) -> {region, countries: [...], country_count}
  Exactly one of country / region required (mutually exclusive).

title: FABRICATED_WEB_CLAIM_RE misses passive-voice 'this information is from a web search'
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 (avocado query, 2nd session): model emitted 'I found that the top South American avocado exporter is Chile. This information is from a web search.' on round 2 — BEFORE any web tool had run. Only tool_search (meta) had fired so far. The fabricated-search claim slipped through because the existing FABRICATED_WEB_CLAIM_RE only catches active-voice patterns:

  r'\bi(?:'ve|\s+have|\s+just)?\s+searched\s+(?:the\s+(?:web|internet)|online)'
  r'|\b(?:after|upon)\s+searching\s+(?:the\s+(?:web|internet)|online)'

It misses the passive-voice / attribution variants the model used:
  - 'This information is from a web search'
  - 'Based on a web search'
  - 'According to (search results|web search|the search)'
  - 'From my web search'
  - 'Per a web search'
  - 'The web search indicates' / 'showed' / 'returned'

All of these signal the model claims to have searched. Web tool actually running disarms the catcher; meta-only-ran does not.

Acceptance:
- FABRICATED_WEB_CLAIM_RE in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py extended with passive-voice / attribution alternatives:
    r'(?:this\s+information|that(?:'s|\s+is))?\s+(?:is\s+)?(?:from|based\s+on|according\s+to|per)\s+(?:a|the|my|recent|the\s+recent)?\s+(?:web\s+search|search\s+results?|online\s+search|web\s+sources?)'
    r'|the\s+web\s+search\s+(?:indicates|showed|returned|tells|reveals|says)'
- New unit tests in test_hooks.py covering each variant (silent when web tool ran; nudge when no web tool ran).
- The existing positive test (active-voice 'I searched the web') still fires.
- Optional fixture entry in evals/orchestrator/ if the existing fabricated_search fixture doesn't already cover passive-voice variants — likely just extending tests is enough.

Small, targeted fix. Low false-positive risk because the passive-voice forms are unambiguous about the model's claim. Sibling beads from same session:
- harness-?: scope-constraint verification (the Mexico case)
- harness-?: self-contradicting rank claim (the Chile contradiction)
close_reason: Passive-voice + reporting-verb attribution variants now match FABRICATED_WEB_CLAIM_RE. 6 new tests pin the new shapes (positive when no web tool ran, silent after real search_web, plus benign-uses guard so 'from the data' / 'from the article' don't over-fire). Suite: 2876 passed. Pushed.

title: self-contradicting rank claim: 'X is the top Y' + 'X is the Nth Y' in the same reply
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 (avocado query, 2nd session): final reply contained BOTH 'Chile, as reported by the article ... is the top South American avocado exporter' AND 'making it the third highest exporter in South America' — same paragraph, same entity (Chile), conflicting rank claims. Internally self-falsifying. The actual top SA exporter is Peru; the article ranked Chile #3.

Distinct from existing catchers:
- list_count_mismatch catches numeric-count claim vs enumerated list. This is rank-claim (e.g. 'top', '#1') vs ordinal claim (e.g. 'third', '#3') about the same entity.
- numeric_fabrication catches labeled-value drift between tool body and reply. This is internal-to-reply contradiction; the body may actually carry the #3 ranking.

Detection — tight pattern, low false-positive risk:
  1. Reply names a TOP claim: 'X is (the|a) (top|leading|highest|#1|number 1|number one|first|largest|biggest|most prolific) Y' OR 'X (leads|tops|ranks #1 in) Y'.
  2. Reply ALSO names a NTH claim about the same subject X with an ordinal/rank >= 2: 'X is (the)? (second|third|fourth|fifth|2nd|3rd|4th|5th|#2|#3|...) Y' OR 'making it (the)? Nth' OR 'X ranks Nth'.
  3. The two claims are about the same Y (same noun phrase). Conservative: require the Y of the TOP claim to share at least one substantive content word with the Y of the NTH claim, OR appear within a small textual window of each other (e.g. same paragraph / within 200 chars).

Subject-matching heuristic — keep it simple:
- Extract the subject of each claim (the noun phrase before the copula or the preceding rank verb).
- If both claims share the same proper-noun subject within a 200-char window, fire.

Action: Nudge — 'Your reply contradicts itself: you said <X> is the <top-word> <Y>, AND that <X> is the <ordinal-word> <Y>. Both cannot be true. Re-read the source — if your source ranks <X> as the <ordinal>, then a different entity is the top. Re-answer with the source's actual #1.'

This is a finalize-tier hook in spirit (self-consistency check), but bail phase works — the next round can fix the contradiction.

Acceptance:
- SelfContradictingRankHook in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py. Position: bail phase, after list_count_mismatch and before scope_violation.
- TOP_CLAIM_RE + NTH_CLAIM_RE regexes covering the common shapes.
- _same_subject(top_match, nth_match) helper — proper-noun extraction + 200-char proximity window.
- HOOK_SHAPES entry, pipeline registration, _CATCHER_NAMES wiring.
- Unit tests: positive (Chile-top + Chile-third repro), positive (variants: 'X tops the list' + 'X is #2'), controls (different subjects: 'X is top, Y is third'), control (only one rank claim, no contradiction), control (top + ordinal but in different paragraphs > 200 chars).
- evals/orchestrator/ fixture pinning the catcher.
- airton fixture coverage entry.
- pipeline_names_match_expected_surface updated.
- docs/hooks.md regenerated.

Companion bead: harness-? (scope-constraint verification). Both target the avocado session; this hook handles the internal contradiction shape, the scope hook handles the named-constraint mismatch.

Same-subject or back-ref match required within 300 chars. 7 new tests, 3 orchestrator fixtures, airton coverage entry. Suite: 2888 passed. title: scope-constraint verification: tools ran but reply names an entity outside the user's named scope
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 (avocado query): user asked 'which south american country exports the most avocados?' Model called search_web + fetch_url, got back a global ranking from worldstopexports.com, then replied 'The top avocado exporter in South America... is Mexico. Mexico exported \$4 billion worth of avocados, accounting for 41.9% of the total global avocado exports.' Mexico is not in South America. The model picked the global #1 without filtering by the user's named region.

Companion failure same session: 'Chile' picked despite the source data showing Chile as #3 in South America (real top SA exporter is Peru). That one is also a constraint-application failure (rank constraint: user said 'the most', but Chile is #3) — covered in a sibling bead for the self-contradicting rank shape.

Distinct from existing catchers:
- argument_grounding gates TOOL ARG entities against the user message; this is about REPLY entities not satisfying the user's scope constraint.
- ungrounded_citation gates section citations; this is about geographic / categorical scope.
- raw_results_dump catches verbatim-output dumps; here the model REWORDS but still picks wrong.

Two-layer fix (mirror the harness-akpx pattern):

LAYER 1 (preventive, system-prompt nudge clause):
Extend the existing _TOOL_USE_RULES_NUDGE (or add clause 3) to teach the constraint-verification step:
'(3) Named-constraint verification — when the user's request carries a constraint (a named region like "South American", a time window like "since 2020", a category like "Republican senators") AND asks for a top/most/largest/highest pick, verify BEFORE answering that your pick satisfies the constraint (a named country actually inside the region) AND is genuinely #1 WITHIN that constraint, not #1 globally. If the source returns a global ranking, filter it by the constraint first.'

LAYER 2 (defensive, bail catcher 'scope_violation'):
Targets the most common constraint type — geographic region — because the gazetteer is small and well-defined. Detection:
  1. user_message names a region/continent ('South America[n]', 'Africa[n]', 'Europe[an]', 'Asia[n]', 'North America[n]', 'Oceania' / 'Australia[n]', 'Antarctica[n]', 'Caribbean', 'Middle East[ern]', 'Scandinavia[n]', 'Baltic', 'Balkans', 'Sub-Saharan', etc.).
  2. user_message contains a top/most/highest/largest/leading word.
  3. reply names a country (capitalized proper noun matching a known country name).
  4. _content_tools_ran(ctx) — at least one content tool ran this turn (we're past the fabricated-search path).
  5. The named country is NOT in the named region per a static REGION_COUNTRIES table.
Action: Nudge — 'Your reply names <country> as the top <constraint> <thing>, but <country> is in <actual_region>, not <named_region>. Re-read your source data, filter by the constraint, and pick the actual top entry inside the region.'

Implementation notes:
- REGION_COUNTRIES table lives in src/harness/orchestrator/_geography.py (new). ~200-line static dict; pulled from a public CC-BY source like ISO 3166-1 + UN M49. Keep it deterministic and offline; no external lookups.
- Country-name detector is conservative: capitalized 2-3 word tokens that match the gazetteer. Handles common variants ('US' / 'USA' / 'United States', 'UK' / 'United Kingdom').
- Skip when the user message ALSO names another region the country DOES belong to — e.g. 'compare top exporters from North America and South America' — too many regions, defer to other catchers.
- Future expansion (out of scope here): time-window constraints, party / political constraints, industry constraints. Geographic gives the most ROI and is the only one with a manageable static lookup.

Acceptance:
- _TOOL_USE_RULES_NUDGE extended with clause (3) — test asserts the multi-part clause keywords ('Named-constraint', 'verify', 'filter').
- ScopeViolationHook in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py — bail phase, after thin_source_fabrication / incomplete_multipart, before ab_fabrication / tool_intent.
- REGION_COUNTRIES table + helper in src/harness/orchestrator/_geography.py.
- HOOK_SHAPES entry, pipeline registration, _CATCHER_NAMES wiring.
- Unit tests: positive (Mexico-for-SA repro), positive (Asian-country-for-Africa shape), controls (correct country, region without a top-word, no tools ran, country matches more than one region).
- evals/orchestrator/ fixture pinning the catcher.

title: catch bare factual fabrication when only meta-tools ran
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19: user asked 'what is the national bird of kenya?' Model called tool_search seven times (all meta), called zero content tools, then emitted 'The national bird of Kenya is the ostrich' as the final reply. Confident factual claim, no grounding, factually wrong (correct answer: lilac-breasted roller, unofficial).

Existing catchers don't cover this shape:
- fabricated_search requires 'here are the results' patterns / URL lists / past-tense 'I searched' narration.
- fabricated_itemization requires an itemized list shape.
- thin_source_fabrication requires a prior tool body to compare against.
- ungrounded_citation requires the reply to CITE a section.
- raw_results_dump requires the reply to overlap with a tool output.

Plain 'X is Y' falls through every gate. The bare form is the hardest fabrication shape to catch heuristically because parametric knowledge is sometimes correct ('What's the capital of France?' → 'Paris' is fine without a tool call).

Proposed detector — multi-gate to keep false positives low:
  1. user_message contains a question-shaped factual ask. Heuristics: ends with '?', begins with what/who/when/where/how/why/which, or contains 'is the' / 'what is' / 'who is'. Reasonably reliable.
  2. user_message contains at least one PROPER NOUN. Approximation: a capitalized multi-letter word that's not at the start of a sentence (e.g. 'Kenya', 'Nairobi', 'Mount Kilimanjaro'). Excludes generic 'What is the capital of a country?' shape with no specific entity.
  3. Only meta-tools ran this turn (_content_tools_ran(ctx) is False).
  4. Reply contains a copula assertion: '<noun phrase> is <noun phrase>' / '<X> is the <Y>' / '<X> are <Y>'. The bare-claim shape.
  5. Reply does NOT contain hedging language ('I think', 'I believe', 'might be', 'unofficially', 'not officially recognized', 'I'm not sure'). A model that already qualifies its claim doesn't need a catcher — the user can read the hedge.

If all gates pass → Nudge: 'Your reply makes a specific factual claim about <named entity> without any data-gathering tool having run. Either: (a) call search_web / fetch_url to verify, or (b) explicitly hedge ("I'm not certain, but based on training data...") and let the user decide. Bare confident claims about named entities — especially proper nouns — are how you hallucinate.'

Acceptance:
- ConfidentFactualClaimHook (or similar name) — bail phase, position AFTER thin_source_fabrication and AFTER incomplete_multipart so the more-specific catchers get first pass.
- HOOK_SHAPES entry, pipeline registration, _CATCHER_NAMES wiring.
- Unit tests: positive (Kenya ostrich repro), positive (Nairobi-population-fabrication-without-tool), controls (hedged reply, content tool ran, generic question without proper nouns, user message that isn't a question).
- evals/orchestrator/ fixture pinning the catcher in isolation.
- airton fixture coverage entry.
- pipeline_names_match_expected_surface updated.
- docs/hooks.md regenerated.

Hardest case to scope. False-positive risk is real. Conservative defaults: stay silent on:
- Replies starting with 'I think' / 'I believe' / 'According to my training' / 'Without verifying'.
- User messages without a proper noun (capital of <country> is generic enough that parametric answer is often fine).
- Replies that already contain the word 'unofficial' / 'allegedly' / 'reportedly' / 'sometimes'.

Even with conservatism, monitor false positives — this catcher is likely to need iteration after first deployment. Capture observed false-fire shapes as fast-follows.

Companion bead: harness-? (tool_search loop without progressing to load_tool). That bead targets the UPSTREAM loop bug — if the agent had progressed to load_tool + search_web, this fabrication wouldn't have happened. Both worth landing; (1) is preventive, (2) is defensive backstop for the cases the upstream fix misses.
close_reason: ConfidentFactualClaimHook landed in the universal bail block, positioned after thin_source_fabrication + incomplete_multipart. Five gates: factual-question shape, named entity in user_message, no content tool ran, copula assertion in reply, no hedge. 10 hook unit tests + 1 airton coverage entry + 5-case orchestrator fixture (5/5 pass). docs/hooks.md regenerated. Suite 2927 → 2937. Deliberate conservative gap: lowercase entity tokens ('kenya') silent — original chat repro shape; fixture pins the capitalized form. Worth iterating after deployment if lowercase traffic warrants. Commit: 9dae983.

title: tool_search loop without progressing to load_tool: model treats discovery as search engine
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19: user asked 'what is the national bird of kenya? Is that bird native to north america?' Model called tool_search SEVEN times in one turn without ever calling load_tool, then emitted a confident-but-wrong answer ('ostrich' — actual answer is lilac-breasted roller, unofficially recognized).

Trace:
  1. tool_search(query='national bird of kenya', tag='search')  -> 7 of 7 (search_web visible)
  2. tool_search(query='national bird of kenya')                 -> no tools found
  3. tool_search(query='kenya national bird')                    -> no tools found
  4. tool_search(query='kenya national bird of')                 -> no tools found
  5. tool_search(query='kenya national bird wiki')               -> no tools found
  6. tool_search(query='kenya national bird site:en.wikipedia.org')   -> no tools found
  7. tool_search(query='kenya national bird site:www.nationalparks.org')  -> duplicate, skipped

Note calls 5-7: 'wiki', 'site:en.wikipedia.org', 'site:nationalparks.org' are search-ENGINE operators, not catalog match keywords. The model thought tool_search WAS the search engine. Call 1's 'Next step: call load_tool(name=<one of the above>)' suffix didn't break the loop — the model didn't follow it.

Two-layer fix (mirror the pattern from harness-akpx / harness-111v):

LAYER 1 (preventive, in the tool_search spec description):
Strengthen the schema description so the model can't read tool_search as 'a search'. Concretely:
- Lead the description with 'Finds TOOL NAMES in the catalog, NOT answers to user questions. Returns up to `limit` tool entries.'
- Add: 'After ANY non-empty result, your next call MUST be load_tool(name=<one of the candidates>). Repeating tool_search with rephrased queries does not search the web — it searches the same catalog and produces the same answers.'
- Document that search-engine operators (site:, intitle:, etc.) don't apply: 'Operators like "site:" or "intitle:" are search-engine syntax, not catalog syntax — they will not match anything.'

LAYER 2 (defensive, new pre_tool catcher 'tool_search_loop'):
Detect: (a) the current call is tool_search, (b) tool_search has already run 2+ times this turn, (c) no load_tool has run this turn. Action: reject the tool execution and feed back a forced nudge ('You've called tool_search N times this turn without loading any candidate. The catalog has not changed between calls. Call load_tool(name=<top result>) now, or tell the user you cannot answer.').

Position: pre_tool phase, near argument_grounding. It's not a fabrication catcher — it's a flow catcher.

Acceptance:
- Strengthened tool_search description (the spec.description string) — unit test asserts on the new keywords ('TOOL NAMES', 'load_tool', 'site:', etc.).
- New ToolSearchLoopHook in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py with HOOK_SHAPES entry + pipeline registration. Pre-tool phase.
- Tests: positive (3rd tool_search call without load_tool → reject), control (1st/2nd tool_search call → execute), control (tool_search + load_tool + tool_search → execute, the prior load_tool resets the counter).
- Fixture under evals/orchestrator/ pinning the loop shape.
- airton fixture coverage entry.
- Pipeline canonical-names test updated.
- docs/hooks.md regenerated.

title: list_count_mismatch over-fires on total-vs-subset count claims
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19: user asked 'what types of orchids are unique to Kenya?' Model fetched a source that said 'Kenya is home to 283 species of orchids belonging to 50 genera' then enumerated 4 named species ('potential for cut-flower production'). list_count_mismatch caught the 283 vs 4 enumeration — but those aren't the same set. 283 is the POPULATION total; 4 is a SUBSET the source called out for a specific purpose. The reply was honest about this ('among these, some species are unique and potentially valuable for ornamental purposes').

Same trace second draft: model said 'lists five orchids' then enumerated 4. Genuine 5 vs 4 mismatch — that fire is correct.

So the catcher's BEHAVIOR is right when the count is supposed to match the enumeration. The bug is it doesn't distinguish:
  - 'X items, here they are: ...' (count IS the enumeration; mismatch = fabrication)
  - 'Y items total. Among these, some Z had property P: <list of n where n < Y>' (count is a population total; enumeration is a labelled subset, not the population)

Qualifying language that signals 'this is a subset, not the total':
  - 'among these'
  - 'some of (which|these|them)'
  - 'a few'
  - 'several'
  - 'for X' (after the count, naming a specific purpose / quality)
  - 'including' / 'such as' (signals open-ended subset, not exhaustive)
  - 'highlights' / 'notable' / 'examples'
  - 'particularly'

Proposed fix in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py (ListCountMismatchHook): before firing, scan a configurable window of text between the count claim and the enumerated list. If the window contains any subset-marker phrase, treat the list as a labelled subset and stay silent. The count is informational, not a claim about the list's length.

Edge cases:
- Reply says '5 X, here are 4' with no subset language → still fires (correct).
- Reply says '5 X, here are 4 examples' → silent (subset).
- Reply says 'I found 5 X. Here are some:' → silent (subset language).
- Pathological 'among 283 species, here are all of them: list of 4' — technically a fabrication shape but rare; accept as a false negative.

Acceptance:
- ListCountMismatchHook gains a 'subset language' carve-out. Detection covers the markers above.
- Existing positive tests still fire.
- New negative tests cover the population-vs-subset pattern (orchid repro shape + a few variants).
- A targeted unit test pinning the repro: 'Kenya is home to 283 species ... Among these, some species ... 1. ... 4. ...' must stay silent.

Trace context: 2026-05-19 orchid session. The catcher fired during draft 1 (false positive) AND draft 2 (true positive). The post-fix expectation is exactly that — draft 2 still gets caught.
close_reason:
Subset-language carve-out shipped. ListCountMismatchHook now skips count-claim matches whose 120-char span contains explicit subset-labelling language (among-these / some-of-them / a-few / several / for-purpose / including / such-as / examples-include / notable / partial / representative).

7 new tests pin the behavior:
- Orchid repro (50 genera vs 4 cut-flower species): silent
- 'among these' / 'some of them' / 'for ornamental use' / 'including' markers each tested with their own subset shapes
- Second-draft orchid shape ('lists five orchids' + 4 listed): STILL fires — real fabrication
- Distant subset language (after the list, outside claim span): STILL fires — span-scoped

All existing positive cases preserved (4-purposes repro, bullet lists, CFR/USC guards).

title: reserve a final wrap-up round when loop terminates mid-investigation
description:
Parent: harness-iz4x (round-budget reform epic).

Problem: when run_tool_loop hits max_rounds on a round that emitted a tool_call, the tool runs and its result is appended to the working messages — but there's no round (round_idx + 1) for the model to synthesize that result into a final reply. The orchestrator returns the previous round's text (typically an interim 'Let's try another search') as if it were final. The user sees a truncated investigation.

Proposed change: detect this terminal-tool-call shape and run ONE extra wrap-up round with a budget-aware nudge appended to the working thread. The nudge tells the model 'this is your final round; synthesize what you have, or say plainly what you couldn't find'. Cap the wrap-up round's max_tokens at wrap_up_max_tokens (already a parameter today) so it can't run away.

Detection conditions (must hold to trigger the wrap-up):
1. round_idx + 1 == max_rounds (i.e. just used the last allowed round).
2. The round's reply emitted at least one tool_call (the model is mid-investigation).
3. Tools actually ran (not blocked by confirm / duplicate_call / argument_grounding rejection — those cases get the rejection text back in the same round).

Implementation sketch:
- After the round-N tool execution, if conditions hold, increment a wrap_up_taken flag and run one more adapter.complete() with a budget-final system message:

    'You have one round left. Do not call another tool. Synthesize the data you have so far into a final reply, or tell the user plainly what you could not find. Do not promise to search more.'

- The wrap-up round's reply is whatever final text the model produces. Bail catchers still run on it; finalize catchers still run; ungrounded-citation / fabrication catchers still apply.

Edge cases:
- Wrap-up round emits another tool_call anyway: ignore the tool_call, take the text content as final. If text is empty, fall through to FabricationFallback canned refusal.

title: exempt meta-tool rounds from max_rounds budget
description:
Parent: harness-iz4x (round-budget reform epic).

Problem: tool_search, load_tool, introspect, spawn_subagent are bookkeeping primitives — they help the agent figure out WHAT to do, not DO it. Today they each consume a round slot against max_rounds, same as search_web / fetch_url. In the 2026-05-19 Nairobi multi-part repro, three of the eight allowed rounds went to discovery (tool_search ×2 + load_tool), leaving only five for actual data-gathering across two sub-asks.

Proposed change: maintain a separate work_round_idx (or skip the round-counter increment when the only tool calls in a round were meta-tools). Define the meta-tool set centrally — probably a module constant in src/harness/tools/profiles.py or src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py that the round-counter and other catchers (raw_results_dump, fabricated_*) can both share. Today, _content_tools_ran(ctx) in hooks.py already encodes this distinction — likely the right source of truth to lean on.

Edge cases to think through:
- A round that contains BOTH a meta-tool call AND a content tool call — does it count? Recommend: counts. The content tool is real work.
- A meta-tool call that fails (e.g. tool_search with a bad arg) — still doesn't count, but the next round still has to deal with the error message.
- Pathological infinite-meta-tool loops: a malformed agent calling tool_search forever would never burn budget. Need a separate guard (absolute round cap, e.g. 2× max_rounds) to prevent runaway.

Acceptance:
- src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py increments a work_round counter (or equivalent) only when a content tool ran on the round. Discovery-only rounds are free.
- Hard ceiling on total iterations (work + discovery) at e.g. 2× max_rounds so a pathological loop can't burn forever.
- Unit tests in test_tool_loop.py:
  - 3 meta-tool rounds + 6 content rounds — completes with max_rounds=8 (3 are free).
  - 12 meta-tool rounds — hits the hard ceiling at 16 iterations and terminates with a sensible error/event.
  - Single content round on a turn — still terminates normally.
- No regression in the existing tool-loop tests.

Companion to: harness-? (reserved wrap-up round). Both fixes solve the same Nairobi repro but address different parts of the structural cost. Either alone is incomplete.

Meta-tool rounds (tool_search/load_tool/introspect/spawn_subagent) now exempt from max_rounds budget. work_rounds counter tracks content rounds separately from total_iterations. Hard ceiling at 2 × max_rounds prevents pathological meta-only loops.

title: multi-part task abandonment: agent answers part 1, gives up on part 2 instead of issuing another search
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 post-l0wg fix. User asked TWO questions in one prompt:

  \"Find the population count of Nairobi, Kenya. What percent are female vs male?\"

Agent successfully searched + answered the population (5,545,000) but on the gender breakdown it said:

  \"the source does not mention any specific data on the percentage of males and females. For a precise breakdown, we would need to look at a more detailed demographic report or a specific source that provides gender statistics.\"

…and terminated the turn. No second search_web call for 'Nairobi Kenya gender ratio' or 'Nairobi demographics female male'. The agent treated 'one source didn't have it' as 'I'm done'.

This is DISTINCT from the harness-akpx synthesis-completion family. That covered synthesis VERBS (rank, prioritize, compare, summarize, group, score, categorize, order, sort, filter) — the kind where the user is asking for a transform of gathered data. Here the user is asking for a parallel SECOND lookup. The agent's tool budget allows it; the agent just didn't think to keep going.

Two-layer fix in the same shape as harness-akpx (preventive nudge + defensive catcher):

LAYER 1 (preventive, system prompt addition):
A short rule in the tool-loop system-prompt block: 'If the user's request contains multiple distinct asks (X and Y, X. then Y? two questions in one prompt), each sub-ask gets its own tool budget. Don't terminate the turn after answering only part of it. If a source covered X but not Y, issue another tool call targeting Y before giving up.'

LAYER 2 (defensive, bail catcher 'incomplete_multipart'):
Detect when:
  (a) prior_tool_outputs is non-empty (tool ran)
  (b) user_message has multi-part shape: 2+ '?' or imperative-then-question pattern, or 'and' + 'what'
  (c) reply contains give-up phrasing: 'we would need', 'for a precise', 'however, the source does not', 'you would need', 'doesn't provide', 'not mentioned', 'not available', 'not explicitly provided'
Fire a Nudge: 'Your reply addresses part of the user's request but signals you couldn't find the rest. Before terminating, issue another tool call (search_web / fetch_url with different terms) to find the missing pieces. Only return a partial answer if multiple attempts genuinely failed.'

Acceptance:
- New _SYNTHESIS_CONTINUE_NUDGE-style system-prompt rule for multi-part prompts, injected when registry has tools (mirrors the existing pattern in tool_loop.py).
- New IncompleteMultipartHook in hooks.py — name='incomplete_multipart', positioned in the bail pipeline AFTER fabricated_search (which handles the no-tool-ran fabrication case) and BEFORE the false_success catchers.
- HOOK_SHAPES entry + default_hook_pipeline + _CATCHER_NAMES wiring.
- Unit tests in test_hooks.py: positive (multi-part + give-up + tools-ran → fire), controls (single-part + give-up → silent; multi-part + complete reply → silent; multi-part + no tools → silent).
- evals/orchestrator/multipart_completion.yaml fixture with the population+gender repro shape.
- airton fixture coverage entry for test_shipped_fixture_covers_every_catcher.
- docs/hooks.md regenerated.
- pipeline_names_match_expected_surface updated with the new name in canonical position.

Cross-references:
- Same session as harness-l0wg (closed, tool_search fix), and the URL-grounding bead filed alongside this one.
- Pattern is the agent equivalent of TODO-not-done — the question count in the prompt is the source of truth for when the turn is finishable.

Verified working on live model. Trace (2026-05-19 post-fix) shows the multi-part nudge channeling persistence:

  Round 1: search_web('population count of Nairobi, Kenya')
  Round 2: fetch_url(worldpopulationreview.com) — population found, gender missing
  Round 3: 'The full article does not provide the gender distribution... Let's try another source for that information.' [continues turn]
  Round 4: fetch_url(citypopulationdata.com) — still no gender
  Round 5: 'The full article does not provide the gender distribution either. Let's try another source.' [continues]
  Round 6: fetch_url(worldpopulationreview) — duplicate_call catcher skips it
  Round 7: 'The current available sources do not provide the gender distribution. Let's try another search approach.' [continues]
  Round 8: search_web('population of Nairobi, Kenya by gender')

Exactly the behavior the bead targeted. Agent no longer treats one source's gap as turn-final; it iterates with refined queries. The bail nudge text directly drove the 'Let's try another source' phrasing.

Two-layer fix landed:
- Layer 1 (preventive): _TOOL_USE_RULES_NUDGE — bundled the synthesis-continue clause (harness-b7yd) and the new multi-part clause into one system message. Avoids cascading subagent-preamble index shifts.
- Layer 2 (defensive): IncompleteMultipartHook bail catcher — three-gate detector (content tool ran + multi-part user message + give-up phrasing in reply).

title: fetch_url URL grounding: confirm fetch targets came from search_web output, not parametric memory
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19 post-l0wg fix. After search_web returned 5 results for 'population count Nairobi Kenya', the model said:

  fetch_url(url='https://citypopulationdata.com/city/nairobi-kenya')

title: tool_search picks wrong tag for factual lookups (arithmetic for population query)
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19: user asked \"Find the population count of Nairobi, Kenya. What percent are female vs male?\" Model called tool_search with arguments:

  tool_search({'query': 'population count Nairobi Kenya', 'tag': 'arithmetic'})

tool_search returned: \"no match for query='population count Nairobi Kenya'; fell back to tag='arithmetic'\" — the harness-8rqw behavior. That dropped 'calc' into the active set. Model treated calc as authoritative, loaded it, and never reached for search_web / fetch_url, eventually fabricating an example (caught by thin_source_fabrication).

The tag='arithmetic' came from the MODEL, not the router (router emits a router-result, not tool-call arguments). So the model self-decided that a 'find the population' question is arithmetic-tagged. That's wrong on its face — a factual lookup should reach for search_web / fetch_url, not calc.

Hypotheses to verify (do trace work first):
- The tool_search schema description leads the model to associate 'calculate percentages later' with tag='arithmetic'. The eventual %-calculation contaminates the initial intent.
- The set of advertised tags makes 'arithmetic' look like the closest match when the model can't see 'web' / 'research' / 'lookup'.
- The model passes both query AND tag because the schema treats them as required/recommended together rather than as alternatives, encouraging spurious tag-matching when query is the right channel.

Acceptance:
- Trace where 'tag=arithmetic' was synthesized (schema review + repro). 
- If schema is the cause, tighten description/required-fields so the model passes query alone for factual lookups.
- If the issue is the advertised tag set, expose 'web'/'research'/'lookup' as visible tags so search_web/fetch_url surface for factual queries.
- Add an evals/orchestrator fixture pinning the corrected behavior: 'find population of X' → search_web / fetch_url, NOT calc.

Companion to harness-xszc (catcher caught the downstream fabrication but couldn't redirect upstream). See sibling bead for the bail-nudge upgrade that teaches what-to-do-after-bail.

Schema-bias fix verified working on live model. New trace (2026-05-19 post-fix) shows model called:
  tool_search(query='population count Nairobi Kenya', tag='search', family='research')
i.e. it picked the data-side tag now ('search') and added family='research' — exactly what the new schema steers toward. Phase 3b fallback fired (query yielded zero, tag='search' matched), returned search_web, model loaded it and ran a real web search.

The 'arithmetic' bait is gone. tool_search now channels factual lookups toward search_web/fetch_url. Three regression tests pin the schema content.

Remaining: downstream behavior past the search is still imperfect (model fetched a different URL than the search returned, then gave up on the second half of the multi-part prompt — gender breakdown — without issuing another search). That's a SEPARATE failure pattern (multi-step task abandonment / fabricated-URL-from-context). Filing a follow-up bead.
