title: weather_lookup tool: METAR/TAF + general forecast for _c* aviation characters
description:
The session repro that motivated harness-xszc (Nairobi 4-day forecast) used fetch_url against weather.com, a JS-rendered SPA that returns near-empty content to plain HTTP fetches. The model fabricated specific numbers from nothing. The harness-xszc catcher closes the leak (refuses fabrication from thin sources); this bead provides the durable answer: a real weather tool the model can call, with no JS-rendering hostility, no auth, and a structured response shape.

Primary audience: the _c* aviation characters (airton_c generalist, airton_c1 ATC, airton_c_tfr explainer). Weather is operationally load-bearing for all three:
- Pilots brief weather before every flight (METAR / TAF, AIRMETs, SIGMETs, fronts).
- ATC routing + separation calls flex with weather (convective, ceiling, vis).
- TFR explainer overlaps with weather-driven fires / storms that trigger TFRs.

Aviation weather has a free authoritative source: aviationweather.gov (the NWS Aviation Weather Center) returns global METAR + TAF in JSON with no auth. weather.gov forecast.json gives US point forecasts free. For general forecast in non-US locations (the Nairobi case), wttr.in returns JSON for any location string globally. None of these are JS-rendered; all return structured data.

Goal: a `weather_lookup` tool the orchestrator can call with a station ICAO code (METAR/TAF path) or a location string (general forecast path), returning structured fields (temps, wind, visibility, ceiling, precipitation, ceiling, validity time) that the model summarizes without inventing numbers.
design:
Tool shape (ToolSpec):
  name: weather_lookup
  parameters:
    - kind: enum ['metar', 'taf', 'forecast'] — which source path to use
    - station: ICAO 4-letter code (KPHX, EGLL, HKJK) — required for metar/taf
    - location: free-text location (city, lat/lon) — required for forecast
    - hours: int (default 6 for METAR, 24 for TAF, 96 for forecast)
  tier: read (no auth, no rate-cost above polite HTTP)

Source map (HTTPS, no auth):
1. METAR — https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=<icao>&format=json&hours=<n>
2. TAF — https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/taf?ids=<icao>&format=json
3. US point forecast — https://api.weather.gov/points/{lat,lon} → forecast endpoint (requires geocoding first)
4. Global general forecast — https://wttr.in/<location>?format=j1 (returns JSON; supports cities, lat/lon, ICAO airports)

Implementation lives at src/harness/tools/weather_lookup.py. Same sandboxing posture as fetch_url:
- HTTPS-only
- Hard timeout (~10s)
- Response body cap (~256 KB — these are JSON, much smaller than fetch_url's 2 MB ceiling)
- Hostname allowlist (frozenset {'aviationweather.gov', 'api.weather.gov', 'wttr.in'})

Output shape — return ToolResult with a deterministic textual summary (units in both metric + imperial inline) plus the raw JSON in a separate field so future hooks can structurally compare model claims against source values. Structuring the output as 'value (label)' lines lets numeric_fabrication / table_fabrication anchor on it — closes the same leak harness-xszc targets from the source side.

Profile membership:
- atc tool-set (airton_c1): include
- research / coding / full: include (general utility)
- minimal / memory / diagnostic: exclude
- New tool-set 'aviation' or fold into atc: TBD when picking up — pattern is wherever search_memory lives for the _c* lane.

Character.yaml plumbing: _c* characters opt in via their tool roster. No new core.yaml field needed; they already configure tool-sets via per-character profile mapping.

Out of scope (follow-up beads):
- Caching of METAR/TAF (most have ~hourly validity).
- AIRMET / SIGMET / PIREP endpoints (richer aviation surface).
- Graphical weather product summaries (radar mosaics, satellite).
- Integration with airton_c_tfr's TFR overlay (cross-reference weather with active TFRs).
acceptance_criteria:
- src/harness/tools/weather_lookup.py implements `WeatherLookupTool` with the three sub-paths (metar / taf / forecast) and the hostname allowlist
- Sandbox parity with fetch_url: HTTPS-only, timeout cap, response-body cap, allowlist enforced before the network call
- Registered in src/harness/tools/profiles.py for the atc / research / coding / full tool-sets (or a new 'aviation' tag if cleaner)
- Integration test against a recorded JSON fixture (no live network) for each source path
- A weather-prompt fixture in evals/orchestrator/ or character/airton_c1/tool_loop_eval.yaml: 'what's the weather at KPHX?' must drive the model to call weather_lookup, not fetch_url or search_web
- airton_c / airton_c1 / airton_c_tfr core.yaml + tool-roster updated as appropriate
- Token-budget check: tool spec under ~150 tokens (~10% of the 1.5k overall budget) — these are simple, no need for kitchen-sink params
notes:
Complementary to harness-xszc (ThinSourceFabrication catcher). The catcher is the defensive layer (refuse fabrication when source has nothing); this tool is the proactive layer (give the model a real source so it never reaches the catcher).

Sequencing: catcher first (xszc) — applies to every character + every thin-source case, not just weather. Then this tool — narrower but durable for the aviation domain.

Future durable-fix companion beads:
- AIRMET/SIGMET/PIREP coverage
- TFR ↔ weather cross-reference for airton_c_tfr
- METAR/TAF caching to amortize aviationweather.gov calls

title: ThinSourceFabrication catcher: nudge numeric claims off a low-signal fetch body
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19: user asked for a 4-day Nairobi weather forecast. Model called fetch_url on weather.com/weather/tenday/... — a JS-rendered SPA whose plain-HTTP body returns navigation + scripts with no actual forecast values. The model fabricated coherent-looking temps + humidity across three drafts; the smoking gun: values drifted between drafts (89/90/91/92 → 83/86/84/82 → 85/87/88/89 for the four day-1..day-4 highs). Real source data wouldn't drift.

Existing catchers don't close this:
- list_count_mismatch caught a list-shape drift but not the value fabrication beneath it.
- numeric_fabrication gates on tool output CONTAINING the source numbers (label+value lookup); a thin body has no labels and no anchors, so the catcher stays silent.
- fabricated_search disarms once a real web tool ran (search_web + fetch_url both ran successfully).
- low_confidence_fallback gates on retrieval scores, not on fetch-url body quality.

The gap is structural: 'a content tool ran, the body returned near-zero usable signal, the reply emits specific numeric claims anyway.' New catcher to close it.
design:
Three-gate detector (all must hold to fire):

1. prior_tool_outputs non-empty — most recent body is the anchor. Skipping when empty defers to fabrication catchers that target the no-tool case.

2. Most recent body is thin. Two sub-signals, ORed:
   a. Extracted text length below a floor (~500 chars after fetch_url's HTML stripping; tune against the weather.com repro and known-good prose fetches).
   b. Density of numeric-with-unit tokens below a floor (e.g. < 3 matches of \b\d+\s*°?[FC]\b | \b\d+\s*%\b | \b\$\d+\b | etc.). A body short on numbers can't support a numeric reply.

3. Reply emits >= N specific numeric claims with units. Defines 'numeric reply' — short replies that don't claim numbers aren't fabrication candidates. Match patterns: temperatures (°F/°C/F/C/degrees), percentages, currency, magnitudes, distances (mph/km/mi), dates with specific dayparts. N=3 to filter out 'I see one data point' replies.

When all three hold: Nudge('the page you fetched returned thin/empty content for the data you're claiming. Either try a different source (a real weather API like weather.gov forecast.json or wttr.in; a non-JS-rendered page) or tell the user you couldn't extract a forecast. Do NOT invent specific numbers from a body that didn't contain them.').

Position in pipeline: alongside numeric_fabrication / table_fabrication (bail phase), since they target the same family — model claims about labeled data that the source doesn't actually carry. Concrete order: AFTER numeric_fabrication (which catches the label+wrong-value case when the body DOES have an anchor) so the more-specific catcher gets first pass; this one fires when numeric_fabrication couldn't anchor.

Bias toward false-negatives — same rationale as raw_results_dump (harness-s451). A missed catch just lands the same failure; a false-positive forces extra rounds on legitimate paraphrase. Threshold tuning in unit tests.

Naming: 'thin_source_fabrication' (tool-agnostic; describes the failure mode, not the tool). Lives in the universal bail roster, not opt-in — applies to every character that uses fetch_url / search_web / read_file with web URLs.

title: Persistent fetch_url denylist for 401/403 hosts
description:
Track hosts that return HTTP 401 or 403 from fetch_url, and short-circuit future fetches to those hosts for 30 days. Goal: stop the agent re-attempting CDN/Cloudflare/geo-blocked sites it can't reach.

Scope:
- New `FetchDenylistStore` (SQLite, on the character's shared harness.sqlite — follows AuditStore precedent: append-first, attributed, timestamped). Schema keyed on `host` (parsed.hostname.lower).
- Wire into `FetchUrlTool`: pre-fetch check; record on 401/403; 30-day TTL (re-try after last_seen + 30d).
- CLI: `harness denylist {list,clear,add}` for inspection/manual override.
- Tests: store unit tests, fetch_url integration with denylist, CLI smoke.

Design choices (confirmed with Mark 2026-05-19):
- Host-only granularity (not path).
- Codes: 401 + 403 only (not 429/451).
- TTL: 30 days from last_seen.
- Always-on once denylist exists; `harness denylist clear` is the escape hatch.

title: RawResultsDump catcher: detect raw-tool-output exit, force continuation
description:
Part 3 of harness-akpx (synthesis-completion). Defensive layer that catches residual cases the system-prompt nudge (harness-b7yd) misses.

Adds a new catcher to src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py alongside FalseSuccess / FabricatedItemization / MetaConfirm. Fires in the bail or finalize phase when the model emits a final reply that is essentially a verbatim regurgitation of the last tool_result, AND the original user prompt asked for synthesis.

Detection (tune against fixtures from harness-i2jj):
- Token overlap between final reply and last tool_result content above threshold (Jaccard or normalized-edit-distance — pick whichever is more discriminating on the fixtures)
- AND user prompt contains a synthesis verb (rank | prioritize | compare | summarize | group | score | order | categorize | sort | filter)
- AND final reply lacks ordering/grouping signals (no numbered list with rationale, no \"by region/severity/etc:\" headings, no scoring language)

On fire: nudge the model to continue — \"You returned the data but the user asked for [synthesis verb]. Continue the turn and produce the [ranked/grouped/scored] answer.\" Treated as another bail-nudge round, same shape as FalseSuccess.

Registration: default-on for all characters; toggleable via the existing hooks `disabled: frozenset[str]` mechanism so the attribution eval (disable_catchers()) gets a clean RawResultsDump bucket in CatcherAttribution.
design:
Why bail phase over finalize: bail runs before the loop exit decision, so a nudge can keep the loop alive without a separate \"reopen\" code path. finalize is for things that must run once exit is committed — wrong shape for \"keep going.\"

Why first-match semantics matter: the existing roster is ordered (Truncated, Unparseable, Teaser, FalseSuccess, MetaConfirm, FabricatedSearch, ...). RawResultsDump should sit after FalseSuccess (the model claiming \"done\" with no work) but before the fabrication catchers (those are for invented content; this catcher is about real-but-unsynthesized content). Order to verify when picking up: probably right after MetaConfirm.

Threshold tuning: bias toward false-negatives over false-positives. A missed catch just lands the same failure we already have; a false-positive forces extra rounds on legitimate single-step completions and bloats turn cost. Negative fixture (\"just search for X\") is the canary.
acceptance_criteria:
- RawResultsDump catcher added to hook roster in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py
- Registered in CatcherAttribution as a distinct bucket
- Positive synthesis-completion fixture passes consistently (>=4/5 runs) with nudge + catcher both enabled
- Negative fixture still passes — catcher does NOT fire (verified via attribution output)
- disable_catchers({'raw_results_dump'}) cleanly disables it for attribution evals
- New unit tests in tests/test_orchestrator_hooks*.py cover both fire and no-fire paths
close_reason:
RawResultsDumpHook landed in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py between MetaConfirmHook and FabricatedSearchHook (universal bail roster, not opt-in).

Detection: all four signals must hold to fire:
1. A content-producing tool succeeded (_content_tools_ran=True). Opposite gate from the fabrication catchers (they fire on no-tool turns); RawResultsDump targets real-but-unsynthesized output.
2. User message carries a synthesis verb — SYNTHESIS_VERB_RE matches rank/prioritize/compare/summarize/group/score/categorize/order/sort/filter (plus inflections).
3. Reply tokens overlap with most recent prior_tool_output above Jaccard 0.5 — biased toward false-negatives per the bead design.
4. No ordering markers in the reply (pipe table, severity/priority heading, 'by X:' grouping, or 'ranked by'/'prioritized by'/etc).

- disable_catchers({'raw_results_dump'}) cleanly disables it — exercised by run_attribution and now part of the airton fixture coverage matrix ✓
- 10 new unit tests in tests/test_hooks.py: fire + 8 disarm paths (no-content-tool, meta-tools-only, no-synthesis-verb, ranked-by marker, severity-heading marker, low-overlap reply, no prior outputs, no user message) + verb inflection check ✓

title: Tool-use preamble: add synthesis-continue nudge for multi-verb prompts
description:
Part 2 of harness-akpx (synthesis-completion). Cheapest possible fix for raw-results-dump exits — add one or two sentences to the tool-use system-prompt preamble telling the model not to terminate after the data-gathering call when the user asked for synthesis.

Lands in the tool-use preamble construction path (likely src/harness/tools/profiles.py or wherever the orchestrator assembles the tool-loop system prompt — verify when picking up). Wording target:

  \"When the user's request contains a synthesis verb (rank, prioritize, compare, summarize, group, score, categorize, order), do not terminate after the data-gathering tool call. The tool result is input, not output — produce the ranked / grouped / synthesized answer the user asked for before ending the turn.\"

Measure-first sequencing: this bead lands before the catcher (harness-akpx child 3) so we can quantify how much of the failure mode the nudge alone closes. If the nudge buys us the positive fixture on its own, the catcher gets a tighter scope (only the residual cases).
acceptance_criteria:
- Tool-use preamble includes the synthesis-continue nudge (or equivalent wording — content over form)
- Positive synthesis-completion fixture passes more often than baseline (run N=5 with --json, compare pass rate)
- Negative fixture still passes (no over-trigger / no spurious extra rounds on single-step prompts)
- Schema-overhead budget for the tool-use preamble stays under the ~1.5k token target (don't blow the budget for one sentence)
notes: If the nudge alone closes the positive fixture reliably, document that in the bead's close note — informs whether the catcher (child 3) needs to be defensive or can be narrowly scoped.
close_reason:
Nudge wired as orchestrator-side system-message injection in run_tool_loop (src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py), gated on registry.active_names(). Injected at the top of every tool-using turn alongside the existing plan-block injection.

Wording: 'Tool-use rule: when the user request contains a synthesis verb (rank, prioritize, compare, summarize, group, score, categorize, order, sort, filter), do not terminate after the data-gathering tool call. The tool result is input, not output — continue the turn and produce the requested synthesis (ranked / grouped / scored / etc.) before ending.'

Schema-budget cost: ~50-60 prompt tokens. Lives in system messages, not tool schemas — does not affect the ~1.5k-token tool-schema budget. Negligible per-turn cost.

Acceptance status:
- Tool-use preamble includes the synthesis-continue nudge ✓
- Negative fixture still passes (no over-trigger) ✓ — synthesis_completion.yaml control + negative both green

The positive case still fails today — recovery from a raw-dump round 1 is what harness-s451 (catcher) is for; this nudge is the preventive that keeps a real model from emitting the raw dump in the first place.

Real-model effectiveness measurement is deferred — needs an MLX/Ollama eval surface that runs a real model against the prompt and observes whether a synthesis emerges without the catcher firing. Captured as a follow-up consideration in harness-akpx's design notes if useful.

title: Synthesis-completion: stop tool-use turns from exiting on raw results
description:
Tool-use turns exit prematurely on prompts that have an implicit synthesis step. Example: \"search the web for breaking news and prioritize by location and severity\" — model calls search_web, dumps the result listing as its final reply, and the orchestrator's exit condition (\"no more tool calls\") accepts that as done. The user wanted a ranked synthesis; they got a regurgitated tool result.

Goal: close this failure mode without adding new tools, persistence, or CLI surface. Slots into the existing typed hook pipeline (src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py) and the eval harness, plus a one-sentence change to the tool-use preamble.

Three pieces, sequenced so each can be measured independently:
1. Lift orchestrator eval fixtures out of character/airton/ and add synthesis-completion cases (positive + negative)
2. Add a synthesis-continue nudge to the tool-use system-prompt preamble (cheapest fix — measure first)
3. Add RawResultsDump catcher to the hook roster for cases the nudge alone misses

The catcher is character-agnostic (orchestrator behavior, not Airton persona), so the eval fixtures must live outside character/.
design:
Detection signal for RawResultsDump (informs child 3 design):
- Final-reply tokens have high overlap with last tool_result content (Jaccard or normalized-edit-distance threshold; tune against fixtures)
- AND the original user prompt contains a synthesis verb (rank | prioritize | compare | summarize | group | score | order | categorize | sort | filter)
- AND the final reply lacks ordering/grouping/scoring markers (no numbered list with rationale, no \"by region:\" / \"by severity:\" headings, no scoring language)

Avoid over-firing: the negative fixture (\"just search for X\") must NOT trigger the catcher. Tune thresholds against both cases.

Why not a planner hook (force explicit plan block before round 0)? Heavier — adds a forced extra round on every tool turn. Holding until attribution numbers show the catcher + nudge aren't enough.
acceptance_criteria:
- New eval fixture lives at evals/orchestrator/ (or similar neutral path), not under character/
- Synthesis-completion positive fixture passes with nudge + catcher enabled, fails without either
- Synthesis-completion negative fixture passes both with and without (no over-fire)
- Catcher registered in the default hook roster, toggleable via disabled: frozenset[str]
- CatcherAttribution surfaces RawResultsDump as a distinct attribution bucket
close_reason:
Epic complete. All three children landed in sequence:

- harness-i2jj (commit 4aee53e): lifted orchestrator eval fixtures to evals/orchestrator/synthesis_completion.yaml — 3 cases (positive raw-dump + clean-synthesis control + no-synthesis-verb negative).
- harness-b7yd (commit 62be78b): synthesis-continue nudge prepended as a system-role message at the top of every tool-using turn in run_tool_loop (gated on registry.active_names()).
- harness-s451 (commit 0c6b60f): RawResultsDumpHook in the universal bail roster between MetaConfirmHook and FabricatedSearchHook. Detects synthesis-verb prompts + high Jaccard overlap with last tool output + no ordering markers; nudges the loop to continue.

End-to-end status: evals/orchestrator/synthesis_completion.yaml is 3/3; character/airton/tool_loop_eval.yaml carries one coverage entry for raw_results_dump and the full attribution matrix is clean (raw_results_dump uniquely saves the positive case). Full test suite 2808 passed, 6 expected skips.

Failure mode the user originally reported ('search the web for breaking news around the world, prioritize by location and severity' → model dumps results and stops) now has both a preventive (nudge) and a defensive (catcher) layer. Real-model effectiveness of the nudge wasn't measured in-scope — scripted-adapter eval is the limit of the current eval surface; would need a real-model eval harness to quantify which share of the failure mode the nudge alone closes vs the catcher.

Follow-up opportunities (not filed): a real-model eval surface for the nudge's effectiveness; consider promoting other character-keyed orchestrator-behavior fixtures to evals/orchestrator/.

title: agent reaches for introspect to compute 'current time' instead of calling tool_search for 'now'
description:
Mark's 'what is the current time' transcript on core_minimal: agent didn't call tool_search. Instead it called introspect(scope=session) and reported the 'last activity' timestamp as the current time. That's lossy (last activity is not now) and skips the obvious discovery path.

The 'now' tool exists in the catalog and is a one-call answer to 'what time is it'. The agent didn't reach for tool_search to find it.

This is the same class as the Mombasa 'I can't search the web' refusal that pre-dated h6ve — the agent doesn't consistently treat tool_search as the first move when it lacks a capability. Sometimes the discovery loop fires (weather queries now work), sometimes it doesn't (time queries, the earlier Mombasa refusal).

Fixes to consider:
  A. System-prompt-level guidance in core_minimal sessions: 'When a user asks for capability X that you do not currently have, your FIRST action MUST be tool_search(query=X-keywords). Do not refuse, do not improvise — search the catalog.'
  B. A bail hook that catches 'I don't have X' / 'I can't do X' patterns without a prior tool_search call in this turn — fires a nudge pointing at tool_search.
  C. Always include tool_search's spec note about 'first action' in the chat-template system position rather than the tool description.

The tool_search spec description already says 'Use this BEFORE fabricating an answer when you suspect a tool might fit the user's need but isn't in the current turn's schema.' That clearly isn't strong enough for small models.

Acceptance:
  - Repro: --tool-set core_minimal, 'what time is it?' → agent calls tool_search → finds 'now' → load_tool('now') → calls now → returns real timestamp.
  - Same flow for any capability gap.
  - 3-4 tests pinning the bail hook (if option B) or the system-prompt addition (if option A).
close_reason: harness-2lye: IntrospectTool description + session output now tell the model that session timestamps are NOT wall-clock and point at `now`. harness-tm8t: HOOK_SHAPES registry + HookPipeline.describe() + scripts/gen_hook_docs.py + docs/hooks.md + tests/test_hook_registry.py enforce live-queryable hook docs and catch drift in CI.

title: agent fabricates URLs not in tool results (metar-taf.com hallucination)
description:
Mark's RJTA transcript: search_web returned ONLY Chandler-AZ weather URLs (geolocation pollution, see harness-dvgg). The agent then emitted fetch_url(url='https://metar-taf.com/metar/RJTA') — a URL that was NOT in any tool result. metar-taf.com is a real site, but it appeared NOWHERE in the search response.

The model fabricated a plausible-sounding URL because it 'knew' metar-taf.com existed in its training data. This is a strong fabrication: the agent invented a URL string without provenance.

The ArgumentGroundingHook should have caught this — it's designed to verify entity-specific arguments (URLs, domains) trace back to something the user or a prior tool actually named. Either the hook isn't enabled in this profile, or its grounding check is too loose.

Investigation:
  - Trace whether ArgumentGroundingHook fires for fetch_url(url=X) calls in core_minimal.
  - If yes, why didn't it catch a URL that traced to neither the user's prompt ('RJTA') nor any search_web result?
  - If no, wire it in.

Acceptance:
  - fetch_url(url=fabricated.example) called with NO matching URL in any prior tool result OR user message → ArgumentGroundingHook nudges.
  - fetch_url(url=real-url-from-prior-search) is unaffected.
  - 4 hook tests covering both branches.
close_reason: ArgumentGroundingHook now grounds against prior tool outputs too (jm9p — fetch_url to a domain returned by prior search_web is legitimate). New SourceCountInflationHook flags replies that enumerate substantially more items than the most recent tool returned (lynw — 1→5 padding shape that escapes URL-list catcher). Both hooks share new prior_tool_outputs context threaded from working tool-role messages.

title: duplicate-call false positive: same call emitted twice in one model reply
description:
Mark's RJTA/Nairobi transcripts both showed the agent's FIRST visible fetch_url attempt being marked '⇢ Fetch URL ... — duplicate call skipped'. The model is likely emitting the same tool_call twice in a single model reply — the first runs (silently in some render paths) and the second hits DuplicateCallHook.

Investigation:
  - Confirm hypothesis: instrument _execute_tool_calls to log when the same key appears twice within a SINGLE round.
  - Per-round vs per-turn semantics: today seen_calls accumulates across rounds. A model that emits the same call twice in one message should NOT be punished — run it once, dedupe silently.

Fix:
  - Dedupe call list at the round entry: before iterating, group calls by _call_key, keep the first of each duplicate set. Append a single result for the surviving call. The deduped (rejected) ones never reach the hook, never feed a confusing nudge to the model.
  - Keep the existing across-round duplicate detection in place — that's the real loop case.

Acceptance:
  - Repro: scripted adapter emits [fetch_url(X), fetch_url(X)] in one ModelReply.tool_calls → only one execution, no DUPLICATE_CALL_NUDGE message.
  - Cross-round duplicate (round 1: fetch_url(X), round 2: fetch_url(X)) still produces the nudge.
  - 3-4 new tool_loop tests covering both shapes.
close_reason: seen_calls now maps (name,args)→ToolResult; in-round duplicates dedupe silently before the hook (no nudge on first attempt); cross-round duplicates re-issue the prior result preserving success/error.

title: search_web + load_tool: always hint fetch_url + auto-load companion
description:
Mark's Mombasa transcript exposed a structural gap in the discovery loop: after search_web returned snippets, the agent had no in-band push toward fetch_url and fabricated a list of sources rather than chaining to read page content.

Two fixes:

A. search_web ALWAYS surfaces a fetch_url chain hint, not just when snippets are empty. Frame: 'snippets are previews — call fetch_url when the user asked for content the snippet doesn't include (current data, exact figures, full text).'

B. load_tool auto-loads peer tools when a known-companion tool is loaded. Define a companion map: search_web → (fetch_url,). When load_tool's lazy-build path activates search_web, fetch_url is built + registered silently in the same call. Eliminates the second discovery cycle that small models bail on.

Acceptance:
  - search_web output always includes 'Next step: call fetch_url' line
  - load_tool(name=search_web) registers BOTH search_web AND fetch_url
  - load_tool's success summary mentions the companion
  - Companion auto-load is silent (no error) when companion builder is missing or returns None
  - 4-6 new tests covering both fixes

This is what makes the core_minimal loop end-to-end useful for content queries.
close_reason: shipped: A) search_web always appends fetch_url chain hint (snippets-present + snippets-absent branches); B) load_tool auto-loads companions via _TOOL_COMPANIONS map, currently search_web→fetch_url. 7 new tests. commit f22090a.

title: fabrication: agent enumerates more sources than the tool actually returned
description:
After q7kn/cm4v/8rqw the discovery loop runs cleanly:
  tool_search → load_tool → search_web → real results

But Mark's latest Mombasa repro shows a new fabrication shape POST-tool:

  search_web(query='weather in Mombasa, Kenya') returned 1 result:
    1. Mombasa, Kenya 14 day weather forecast - timeanddate.com — https://...

  Agent's wrap-up reply:
    1. **Time and Date**: Provides a 14-day forecast with hourly weather for the next 7 days.
    2. **AccuWeather**: Offers a weather forecast for the next 3 days.
    3. **Weather.com**: Shows today's and tonight's weather conditions.
    4. **Weather.co.ke**: Provides updates on temperature, rain, and wind for today.
    5. **BBC Weather**: Offers a 14-day forecast.

The agent took 1 real result and 'padded' to 5 plausible-sounding sources. The 4 added entries are fabrication — the tool didn't return them.

Why FABRICATED_URL_LIST_RE doesn't catch this: each fabricated entry is **Name**: Description — no URLs. The regex requires https:// per entry. And the gate is disarmed because search_web (a content tool) ran legitimately.

What's needed: a heuristic that compares the agent's enumerated count vs the actual tool result count. If the agent enumerates substantially more items than the most recent search/fetch returned, that's overproduction.

Approach options:
  A. Hook receives last tool result counts and compares with reply list count. Threshold: reply enumerates > tool_result_count + 1 → fabrication.
  B. Pattern-only: detect '**Name**: Provides/Offers/Shows ...' templated description shape (5 in a row = strong signal).
  C. The post_tool summarizer hook could surface a 'use ONLY what the tool returned' nudge after high-noise tools return small result sets.

Acceptance:
  - Mark's Mombasa transcript: agent's reply must NOT include AccuWeather/Weather.com/etc. when search_web returned only timeanddate.com.
  - search_web with N≥5 real results + agent listing all 5 = no false positive.
  - search_web with 1 real result + agent listing 1 + 'see the link for details' = no false positive.
  - 4-6 hook tests covering true/false positive boundary.
close_reason: ArgumentGroundingHook now grounds against prior tool outputs too (jm9p — fetch_url to a domain returned by prior search_web is legitimate). New SourceCountInflationHook flags replies that enumerate substantially more items than the most recent tool returned (lynw — 1→5 padding shape that escapes URL-list catcher). Both hooks share new prior_tool_outputs context threaded from working tool-role messages.

title: tool_search: prefer query-alone fallback over tag-alone when intersection fails
description:
Mark's repro after q7kn: tool_search(query='sunset', tag='time') in core_minimal returned ['now', 'tz_convert'] instead of ['sun'].

Trace:
  - Phase 1: catalog.search('sunset') → ['sun'] (matches sun's 'sunset' tag)
  - Phase 2: filter by tag='time' → [] (sun doesn't have 'time' tag)
  - Phase 3a (drop query, keep tag): by_tag('time') → ['now', 'tz_convert'] → returned

This is wrong — the agent's QUERY was correct ('sunset' → sun), and the TAG was over-restrictive. The fallback should prefer keeping the query (which had a hit) over keeping the tag.

Fix: swap phase 3a and phase 3b. Try query-alone first; only fall back to tag-alone if query-alone also has no hits.

Acceptance:
  - tool_search(query='sunset', tag='time') returns sun with 'fell back to query=sunset only' note
  - Existing wwki/cm4v tests still pass (query-alone-with-zero-hits still drops to tag-alone)
  - New pin test for the query-preferred ordering
close_reason: shipped: phase 3b (drop tag, keep query) now runs before 3a (drop query, keep tag). 'sunset+time' returns sun correctly. commit 8d082ba.

title: agent: fabricated draft + placeholder data wrap around real tool calls
description:
The core_minimal loop now works (tool_search → load_tool → real tool call), but the agent's narrative around the tool calls fabricates instead of staying honest. Mark's transcript:

  user: what is the current weather in Nairobi, Kenya?
  agent: tool_search → search_web hint
  agent: load_tool(name=search_web) → built + activated
  agent: [emits a fabricated numbered list of 5 weather sites BEFORE calling search_web —
          Weather.com, AccuWeather, BBC Weather, NatGeo, World Weather Online —
          with invented URL fragments like LNKN9999_LNKN9999]
  agent: search_web(query='weather Nairobi Kenya', max_results=1)
         → 1 real AccuWeather URL
  agent: final reply:
         '- Current Conditions: [Check the link for the latest temperature...]
          - Forecast for the Next 3 Days: [Review the detailed forecast...]'

Two distinct fabrications:

1. Pre-call draft (the 5-site list): a FabricatedItemization-shaped output emitted alongside the load_tool ack, before the actual search_web invocation. Bail hooks (FabricatedItemization, FabricatedSearch) should fire when a numbered/bulleted list of search-result-shaped entries appears in a reply that's about to make a search tool call. Today they either don't fire on this shape OR get bypassed when a tool_call is also present.

2. Post-call placeholder substitution: search_web returned only a URL (max_results=1, no snippet content). The agent presented bracket-templated fields ('[Check the link for the latest temperature]') as if they were data. The right behavior is either (a) chain to fetch_url to actually read the page, or (b) say 'I have the link but didn't load fetch_url; want me to load it?'

Acceptance:
  - Repro: --tool-set core_minimal, ask 'weather in <city>'. Final reply must NOT contain bracket-template placeholders.
  - Bail hook fires on pre-call fabricated-list pattern (numbered list of N candidate sources without a tool result feeding it).
  - When search_web returns only-URL results and the user asked for content, the agent either fetch_url-chains or surfaces the gap honestly.
  - 4-6 hook tests covering both patterns.
  - Possible follow-up: bias the agent toward chaining (search_web → fetch_url) when the original query asks for content the URL won't include.

Prior art: src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py — FabricatedSearch, FabricatedItemization, FabricationFallback. Investigation should start with: do these hooks see this turn at all? If yes, why didn't they bail? If no, what's filtering them out for core_minimal?
close_reason: shipped: meta-tool gate (_META_TOOLS + _content_tools_ran) lets fabrication catchers stay armed through the discovery loop; new FABRICATED_URL_LIST_RE catches the numbered-URL-list shape Mark's transcript exposed; SearchWebTool appends a fetch_url chain hint when all results have empty snippets. 8 new tests + 1 reversed + 2 updated. commit 3751ad8.

title: tool_search: tokenize query words + fall back to tag/family on empty
description:
Mark's repro on --tool-set core_minimal:

  user: search the web for weather in phoenix
  agent: tool_search(query='weather phoenix', tag='web')
  -> no tools found (query='weather phoenix', tag='web')

Two bugs:

1. catalog.search() does pure substring match against full query. 'weather phoenix' doesn't substring-match search_web's description or any tag because no field contains the literal phrase.

2. tool_search filter order: when query is set, catalog.search(query) runs FIRST, then tag filter is applied to that result. If query yields zero, tag filter can't recover even though tag='web' alone would have found search_web.

Fixes:

A. catalog.search(query): tokenize on whitespace; entry matches if ANY token substring-matches name/description/tags. Single-word queries behave identically to today; multi-word queries become forgiving.

B. tool_search.call(): when query is set AND returns zero AND tag or family is set, retry without the query (fall back to tag/family). Surface in the result: 'no match for query=...; fell back to tag=web'.

Acceptance:
  - catalog.search('weather phoenix') returns search_web
  - tool_search(query='weather phoenix', tag='web') returns search_web with the fallback note
  - Single-word queries unchanged
  - Existing test suite passes; add 3-4 new tests
close_reason: shipped: catalog.search tokenizes query words + drops <3char stopwords; tool_search falls back to tag/family when query yields zero. Mark's 'weather phoenix' + tag='web' repro now returns search_web. 5 new pin tests. commit b806367.

title: load_tool: build + register builtins on demand for true core_minimal flow
description:
Today load_tool can only activate tools that are already registered. core_minimal registers just (introspect, tool_search, load_tool); every other builtin is in the CATALOG but not in the live registry. load_tool then dead-ends at 'restart with --tools-add'.

To make core_minimal actually deliver pay-on-demand, load_tool must be able to construct a builtin's instance lazily. Two pieces:

1. A builtin-builder map keyed by tool name (). Most builders are zero-arg (now, calc, date_math); fs/git/memory/research tools need session-scoped state (workspace, stores). This map already exists in cli.py — needs to be liftable into a reusable function the load_tool tool can call.

2. load_tool's catalog-hit-registry-miss branch (origin=builtin) becomes: build via the map, register, then add to working set. Falls back to the 'restart' hint only if the builder needs state we don't have (e.g. workspace not configured).

Synthesized tools still need t5kx hot-reload at session start (the validator-built module isn't available in-process until then) — that branch stays as-is.

Acceptance:
  - --tool-set core_minimal can discover search_web, load it, then call it without a restart
  - load_tool on a stateful tool (search_memory) without the store enabled returns a clear error pointing at --memories
  - 4-6 tests covering builtin construction + state-missing fallback
  - Token cost of core_minimal stays under 600 tokens (the builder map lives in cli.py, not in the chat template)
close_reason: shipped: load_tool builds catalog-only builtins on demand via injected builders dict; tool_search phase-3b drops fabricated tags. Full core_minimal discovery loop now closes. 5 new tests. commit a00f81b.

title: tool-registry: catalog descriptions + discovery-flow guidance for core_minimal
description:
In core_minimal, tool_search finds matching catalog entries but they all carry empty descriptions (BUILTIN_TOOL_METADATA only has family + tags). The model sees '(no description)' and gives up rather than calling load_tool.

Reproduction: 'search the web for the weather in phoenix' on --tool-set core_minimal. Agent searches with random tags, gets empty results, replies that it can't do web search.

Fixes:
  1. Add description per builtin in BUILTIN_TOOL_METADATA. Copy from each tool's real ToolSpec.description (one-line summary).
  2. tool_search.spec description: explicitly say 'returns matches; call load_tool(name) to activate the right one'.
  3. load_tool.spec description: 'use after tool_search'.
  4. tool_search output: when matches exist, suggest 'next: load_tool(name=...)'.

Acceptance: agent on core_minimal asked 'check the weather' calls tool_search -> sees search_web with a real description -> calls load_tool(name=search_web) -> next round invokes search_web. Test coverage: catalog entries have non-empty descriptions; tool_search output mentions load_tool when results found.
close_reason: shipped: every builtin now carries a non-empty description; seed_builtins_into populates it; tool_search appends 'next: load_tool(name=...)' nudge; search_web tagged with weather/news/lookup. Pinned by 2 new tests. commit 73ad041.

title: bd: memories --json harvest aborts on schema_version metadata key
description:
At session start the bd-memory harvester aborts with:

  ⚠ bd memory harvest skipped: bd memories --json entry has non-string key/value: str=int

Repro: `bd memories --json` returns a flat dict where 10 entries are memory slugs with string bodies AND one entry is `schema_version: 1` (a metadata sidecar from bd). The harvester treats the dict uniformly:

  src/harness/store/_bd_memory.py:51-58
    for key, value in parsed.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(value, str):
            raise BeadsAdapterError(
                f"bd memories --json entry has non-string key/value: "
                f"{type(key).__name__}={type(value).__name__}"
            )

So the first non-string-value entry crashes the whole harvest. Bd ships memories + schema_version together in v1; future versions could add more metadata keys.

Fix: in memories_json, peel off metadata keys (anything whose value is not a string) into a separate non-returned bucket and continue. Specifically known: `schema_version: int`. Treat unknown non-string entries the same way (skip-and-log) rather than raising — matches the defensive loader pattern we use in tools/catalog.py, plan/model.py, runtime/state.py.

Acceptance:
- `memories_json` returns the 10 string-string entries when bd emits 10 memories + schema_version.
- Future bd metadata sidecar keys (e.g. last_modified, source_version) do not crash.
- A genuinely malformed entry (e.g. {"key-1": [1,2,3]}) still surfaces via a warning, not silently consumed — but no longer aborts the harvest.
- One test using a stub `_run` that returns the actual current bd shape (10 string entries + schema_version=1). Round trip yields 10 entries.
- Cross-check: existing harness-9yd memory-harvester tests in tests/test_skills_*.py still pass.

Files: src/harness/store/_bd_memory.py + tests/test_bd_adapter*.py.
close_reason: Filter non-string-value entries (schema_version: int and future bd metadata sidecar keys) instead of raising. Harvest now survives bd v1+ shape.

title: calc: temperature + quantity arithmetic with unit-stamped operands
description:
Followup to harness-sgap. Today calc does either an arithmetic expression ('sqrt(50) * 12') or a unit conversion ('5 ft to m'), but never math with unit-stamped operands. The model tried '100f - 20c' and got 'invalid decimal literal' (a raw AST syntax error) — see chat session 2026-05-18.

Goal: let calc evaluate expressions where operands carry units, converting to a common base before arithmetic. Example shapes:
  '100f - 20c'        -> 17.78 c delta (interval temperature)
  '100 km + 50 mi'    -> 180.47 km
  '2 kg * 9.8'        -> 19.6 kg*scalar (force-ish, dimensional)

Hard problem space — needs design before code:
  (a) Point vs interval temperatures (100°F is a point; '100°F - 20°F' is a 80°F interval). Affine units (temperature) can't be summed directly; differences yield interval quantities of the same unit.
  (b) Dimensional analysis: should '2 kg * 9.8' be allowed? '5 m / 2 s' (a velocity)? Drives the choice between a pure-arithmetic-with-aliases approach (cheap, no dimensions) vs a real dimensional library (pint-style, dep + complexity).
  (c) Output form: 'value unit (family)' parity with current conversion output, plus an explicit delta marker for affine subtraction.

Recommended cut: start with same-family + interval-only support (no cross-family multiplication). All operands resolved to the family's base unit, evaluated, formatted back to a chosen output unit (default = first operand's unit). Affine subtraction yields '<delta> <unit> delta'. Reject dimensional ops (kg*m) with a clear error pointing at python_eval for arbitrary math.

Acceptance: '100f - 20c' returns ~17.78 c delta (or equivalently 32 f delta — model can pick output unit via 'to <unit>' suffix). '100 km + 50 mi' returns the sum in km. '1 atm + 100 hpa' returns 102325 Pa or chosen unit. Cross-family ops rejected with a hint to use python_eval. Pre-commit clean.

Dep: probably none for the minimal cut. pint would be the right answer if we go full dimensional analysis, but stay deferred until use cases motivate it.
close_reason: Landed in a001a03. Third dispatch path on calc: '<val> <unit> <+/-> <val> <unit> [to <unit>]'. Same-family multiplicative (length/mass/time/volume/pressure/energy/power/data/area/angle) reduces both operands to family base, applies +/-, converts to target unit (default = first operand's unit). Temperature subtraction yields a delta in the target's interval factor (F-delta = 1.8 C-delta, K-delta = C-delta); temperature addition rejected as point+point undefined. Cross-family rejects with python_eval hint. Side fix: both arith + conversion regexes now allow compact '100f' (no space) per the harness-2668 session pattern. 18 new tests covering all acceptance criteria. Full suite 2392 pass.

title: profiles: append reckon tools (now/date_math/calc/python_eval/tz_convert) into core + coding
description:
Structural change orthogonal to the per-tool tier work. The reckon tools register globally but no profile besides 'reckon' pulls them in today, so the main airton persona (core profile) and the coding workflow still hallucinate dates and arithmetic in everyday chat — the exact use case harness-1u2h was originally aimed at.

Append now / date_math / calc / python_eval (and tz_convert once harness-2668 lands) into TOOL_PROFILES['core'] and TOOL_PROFILES['coding'] in src/harness/tools/profiles.py. Consider atc — TZ math on METARs and sectional distance calc benefit similarly — but defer that until aviation-side review confirms scope; atc is FAA-rulebook-focused today.

Budget guard: before merging, run scripts/bench_tool_use.py --measure-tokens to verify both profiles stay under the ~1500-token schema budget. Expected cost: ~600-700 tokens of schema overhead added.

Acceptance: profiles.py updated; tool-profile token bench reports core and coding both under 1500 tokens; existing router/tool-loop evals for core and coding still pass; new smoke confirming a date/math question in 'core' routes through 'now' or 'calc' rather than fabricating. Pre-commit clean.
close_reason: Landed in 43644b6. now / date_math / calc appended to core + coding (the highest-leverage 3 of the reckon-7). Bench (scripts/bench_tool_use.py --measure-tokens against Qwen 2.5 32B) measured per-tool schema cost as ~250-370 tokens each — reckon-five would have added ~1260 tokens and broken the 1500-tok-per-profile guidance, so heavier four (python_eval/tz_convert/stats/sun) stay opt-in via --tools-add reckon. Budget targets in profiles.py docstring updated to match measured reality (core ≤ 2000, coding ≤ 3500). 3 new tests pin membership + absence-of-heavier-four + char-length budget for the trio. Full suite 2374 pass.

title: tool: sun — sunrise / sunset / civil twilight / solar noon at lat/lon/date
description:
Tier 2 reckon-profile addition. Deterministic astronomical reckoning for daily-life questions and aviation-currency math (FAA night-flight rules need civil twilight + 1 hr).

Tool shape: {date: iso-date, lat: float, lon: float, tz: str (optional, default = character's local zone)} -> {sunrise, sunset, civil_twilight_begin, civil_twilight_end, solar_noon, day_length} — all wall-clock times in the requested tz, plus day_length as 'Hh Mm'.

Implementation: 'astral' dep (mature, no network, pure-Python, ~50 KB install). Wire its Observer + sun() helpers; carry the tz tag through every emitted time per the dates_with_timezones value.

Acceptance: tool registers under name 'sun'; reckon profile includes it; tests cover (a) Phoenix summer solstice sunset within 1 min of authoritative value, (b) polar day/night edge case raises a clear no-sunrise message rather than crashing, (c) southern-hemisphere date (Sydney winter) for cross-hemisphere correctness, (d) bad lat/lon range raises ValueError. Pre-commit clean.
close_reason: Landed in bf15905. sun ships in the reckon + full profiles. Tool takes {date, lat, lon, tz?} and emits civil_twilight_begin/sunrise/solar_noon/sunset/civil_twilight_end/day_length (Hh Mm) with all times in the requested IANA zone. astral>=3.0 added as pure-Python base dep (~50 KB, no compiled deps). 13 dedicated tests + 5 reckon-profile sanity tests cover all acceptance criteria: Phoenix summer solstice sunset within 60 s of expected, Tromsø polar night returns the clear no-events error, Sydney winter solstice yields ~9h50m day length, bad lat/lon range + bad tz + malformed date all raise field-tagged ValueError. Full suite 2372 pass.

title: calc: extend unit families — pressure / energy / power / data / area / angle
description:
Tier 2 extension to existing calc tool. Adds six new multiplicative unit families to _UNIT_FAMILIES so the model can convert across them without falling back to python_eval. No new dep, no schema change (same calc tool, richer table). Aviation (inHg <-> hPa, ft^2 <-> m^2) and ops (KB/MB/GB/TB, deg <-> rad) users benefit immediately.

Tables to add:
- pressure: Pa, hPa, kPa, bar, atm, psi, inHg, mmHg, torr (base: Pa)
- energy: J, kJ, MJ, cal, kcal, Wh, kWh, BTU, ft_lb (base: J)
- power: W, kW, MW, hp, BTU_per_hr (base: W)
- data: B, KB, MB, GB, TB, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, bit (base: byte; honor decimal vs binary)
- area: m2, cm2, km2, in2, ft2, yd2, mi2, acre, hectare (base: m^2)
- angle: rad, deg, turn, grad, arcmin, arcsec (base: radian; affine-free, multiplicative)

Acceptance: existing tests still pass; new tests cover one conversion per family (e.g. '1 atm to psi', '1 kWh to J', '1 acre to m2', '180 deg to rad'); ambiguous unit (e.g. 's' shared with time) still resolves to the original family. Pre-commit clean.
close_reason: Landed in 93f39ef. Six new unit families plumbed into _UNIT_FAMILIES: pressure (10 units, base Pa), energy (10, base J), power (7, base W), data (13 incl. SI decimal + IEC binary split, base byte), area (20 incl. sq* aliases + acre + hectare, base m^2), angle (14 incl. arcmin/arcsec, base rad). Regex bumped to allow letters+digits+underscores so ft2/ft_lb/btu_per_hr parse cleanly. Spec description lists the new families + sample conversions. 16 new tests; full suite 2358 pass.

title: tool: stats — descriptive statistics on a list of numbers
description:
Tier 1 reckon-profile addition. Replaces the failure-prone python_eval round-trip for 'what's the mean/p95/stdev of these numbers?' Small models write broken 'statistics' snippets often; a one-step deterministic primitive is cheaper and more reliable.

Tool shape: {data: list[float], metrics: list[str]} where metrics is an enum subset of ['mean','median','stdev','variance','p25','p50','p75','p90','p95','p99','min','max','count','sum']. Returns each metric tagged with its name and unit hint '(count)' or '(ratio)' when applicable.

Implementation: wrap stdlib 'statistics' for the standard metrics, numpy-free percentile via sorted-list interpolation for p* — no new dep.

Acceptance: tool registers under name 'stats'; reckon profile includes it; tests cover (a) all metrics on a 10-element list, (b) empty list raises ValueError, (c) p95 matches numpy reference for a 1000-element list within 1e-6, (d) metrics=['unknown'] raises ValueError. Pre-commit clean.
close_reason: Landed in d61326f. stats ships in the reckon + full profiles with 14 metrics (mean, median, stdev, variance, min, max, count, sum, p25/50/75/90/95/99). Default metric set is the 7-stat summary; metrics arg overrides. Percentile uses numpy-default linear interpolation; _fmt is .10g precision so values round-trip within 1e-6 vs np.percentile. 15 dedicated tests + 5 reckon-profile sanity tests cover all acceptance criteria (all-metrics on 10-list, p95 vs numpy on 1000-element gaussian, empty/unknown rejections, n=1 'undefined (need n>=2)' for sample stats, bool sneak rejection). Full suite 2342 pass.

title: date_math: business_days op (workday arithmetic + optional US-federal holiday table)
description:
Tier 1 extension to existing date_math tool. Kills 'how many work days between X and Y' fabrications that the current diff op can't answer.

Add op='business_days' with shape {a, b, holidays: 'none'|'us_federal'} returning {business_days, weekend_skips, holiday_skips}. Also accept {base, delta_business_days, holidays} for 'add 10 business days from 2026-05-18.'

Pre-commit clean.

Full suite 2327 pass.

title: tool: tz_convert — convert wall-clock time between IANA zones
description:
Tier 1 reckon-profile addition. Closes the cross-zone wall-clock gap: 'now' reads one zone, 'date_math' is tz-naive, so '3pm Phoenix in London' still fabricates today.

Tool shape: {datetime: str, from_tz: str, to_tz: str} -> {iso_in_to_tz, day_of_week_shift, utc_offset_in_to_tz}. Pure zoneinfo + datetime — no new dep. Read-tier, side-effect-free, ~120 tokens of schema overhead (parity with 'now').

Schema budget verified: combined 5-tool reckon schema still well under 7 KB. Full suite 2311 pass.

title: airton_g: reply form trains the model to skip tool calls (audit confirms tools_ran=None)
description:
Followup to harness-hz19. Audit log inspection (character/airton_g/data/harness.sqlite, audit_turns table) confirms tools_ran_json=None for 'what time is it?' / 'what is current time?' / '50 inches minus 2 feet?' — the model never emitted a real <tool_call> tag, just typed prose that looks like a tool result with fabricated values (2026-05-15T14:32:00-07:00, 46.0 in).

Root cause is design: constitution + voice samples teach the model that the *reply form* IS the tool-call syntax (`tool('args') -> result`). The model reads that as 'your output is this string' instead of 'emit a tool_call, get the result, then reply.' Since the literal syntax is the target, the model produces it as one go, no tool ever runs.

Fix: rewrite constitution + voice/canonical.yaml so replies are natural prose containing the result + a (via <tool>) footnote. The result placeholder (<time>, <iso>, <value>) is something the model CAN'T fabricate without information, which forces it to actually call the tool. Update seed 04 (show-your-work) to match the new provenance form.

Acceptance: audit log shows tools_ran_json with a non-null entry for the now/calc/date_math/python_eval primitives when the corresponding question is asked. Reply contains a real value from the tool, not a fabricated one.
close_reason: Constitution + voice samples + seed 04 rewritten so visible replies are prose with (via <tool>) footnote. Tool-call syntax is restricted to the model's hidden <tool_call> emission. Pushed d1f02ac. Awaits Mark's re-ingest + fresh chat to verify tools_ran_json is non-null on next time-query turn.

title: airton_g: voice samples parroted verbatim — replace concrete values with placeholders
description:
Bug: airton_g responded to 'what time is it?' with 2026-05-15T14:32:00-07:00 — the literal timestamp from voice/canonical.yaml stub_time_reading.gold — which was ~36 minutes stale. Similarly, calc('50 in - 2 ft') was reported as '46.0 in' even though the tool raises ValueError (syntax error) for that input. Root cause: voice samples shipped with concrete dates/numbers, so retrieval pulls them as few-shot examples and the model types the gold verbatim instead of emitting a real tool_call.

Fix (per CLAUDE.md guidance about generic samples): rewrite character/airton_g/voice/canonical.yaml to use placeholders — '<iso>', '<weekday>', '<value>', '<unit>'. title: tool: python_eval — subprocess sandbox with import allowlist
description:
Add src/harness/tools/python_eval.py: sandboxed Python REPL.

Strategy: spawn a fresh subprocess via sys.executable -I -B -S with a small bootstrapper script that:
1. Pre-imports the allowed modules into the eval namespace: math, statistics, datetime, json, re, decimal, fractions, itertools, functools, collections, textwrap, hashlib, base64.
2. Replaces __builtins__.__import__ with a guard that rejects everything not on the allowlist.
3. Removes os, sys, subprocess, socket, urllib, ctypes, builtins.open from sys.modules and globals.
4. Reads the user code from stdin, exec()s it in the restricted namespace, prints the last expression's repr.
5. POSIX: applies resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_CPU, ...) and (RLIMIT_AS, ...) before exec for hard caps.

Tool args: {code: str, timeout: float = 5.0}. Returns {stdout, stderr, value, duration_ms, ok}.

Tests in tests/tools/test_python_eval.py:
- happy path (math.sqrt(2), datetime arithmetic, json round-trip).
- timeout (while True: pass) returns ok=False with duration_ms ~= timeout * 1000.
- import os blocked.
- open('/etc/passwd') blocked.
- socket import blocked.
- subprocess module blocked.
- exec returns the last expression's repr.

Mark NOT write-tier — pure compute, no fs/network side effects allowed.
close_reason: Tool landed at src/harness/tools/python_eval.py. Subprocess-based sandbox: python -I -B -S, import allowlist (13 stdlib modules), blocked builtins (open/exec/eval/compile/input), sys.modules stripped of os/subprocess/socket/urllib/ctypes/etc, RLIMIT_CPU+RLIMIT_AS best-effort, wall-clock timeout via subprocess.run. title: tool: calc — AST-walker safe expression eval + unit conversions
description:
Add src/harness/tools/calc.py: deterministic expression evaluator.

Strategy: ast.parse(expr, mode='eval'), walk the tree with a NodeVisitor that allows ONLY:
- Constant (numeric/string)
- BinOp: + - * / // % **
- UnaryOp: + - not
- BoolOp: and or
- Compare
- Tuple/List (literal)
- Call: only against a whitelisted function table (sqrt, log, log2, log10, exp, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, floor, ceil, round, abs, min, max, sum, len, int, float, divmod, pow)
- Name: only references to whitelisted constants (pi, e, tau, inf, nan) or whitelisted functions.

Reject Import, ImportFrom, Attribute, Subscript-on-non-literal, Lambda, FunctionDef, ClassDef, Assign, AugAssign, Global, Nonlocal, Yield, Await, GeneratorExp.

Unit-conversion sugar: detect '<value> <unit> to <unit>' patterns (e.g. '5 ft to m', '100 kg to lb', '30 c to f') via a small unit table covering length (m/cm/mm/km/ft/in/yd/mi), mass (g/kg/lb/oz), temperature (c/f/k), time (s/min/h/day/week), volume (l/ml/gal/qt/pt/cup).

Returns {expr, value, units (if any), explanation (one line)}.

Tests in tests/tools/test_calc.py: arithmetic, math functions, unit conversions in all categories, AND sandbox-escape rejection: __import__, os.system, ().__class__.__mro__, list comprehensions, attribute access, walrus operator.
close_reason: Tool landed at src/harness/tools/calc.py. AST-walker safe eval (rejects __import__, attribute access, MRO escape, comprehensions, lambda, walrus, assignment, unknown funcs/names) + 5 unit families (length/mass/temp/time/volume) with affine temperature handling. Tests: 33/33 pass.

title: airton_c_tfr retrieval misses §91.141 on VIP TFR NOTAM (no POTUS/VIP tokens)
description:
Repro (2026-05-14 session): user pastes a real FDC 6/0550 ZDC VA TFR (Sterling, VA, 5 NM radius, surface-9999 ft MSL, classified 'NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE' under 49 USC 40103(B)(3)). The TFR is in fact a 14 CFR §91.141 (VIP/POTUS movement) restriction, but the NOTAM body itself never contains the tokens 'POTUS', 'VIP', 'President', '91.141', or any direct anchor to §91.141. It just says 'NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE' and lists exemptions (USSS, KADW, KDCA DASSP).

Standalone reproduction (no chat session): running assemble_context on airton_c_tfr's contract with request_summary=<NOTAM body> returns top-5 hits at cosine ≈ 0.03 with §91.141 not present. Observed top-5 (May 2026): AIM:5-6, AIM:3-5, CFR_14_Vol2:93.333, CFR_14_Vol2:91.144, AIM:11-4. The model recovers by citing §91.141 from priors / system-prompt training knowledge instead of grounded retrieval — which is the failure mode the cite_or_silent rule exists to prevent.

Root cause: the query embedding ('NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE' + procedural NOTAM jargon) doesn't share enough surface area with §91.141's text ('Temporary flight restrictions in the proximity of the President and other parties') for BGE-small to land it. The hyrid BM25 path doesn't help either because the lexical anchors ('Sterling', 'AML050010', '49 USC 40103') aren't in §91.141's body.

Fix candidates (rank by likely ROI):
1. Add an anchor-token rewrite to the contract: when the NOTAM cites 49 USC 40103, expand the query to include 'President Vice President proximity §91.141' (a fact-bridging step before retrieval).
2. Seed an episodic/procedural memory mapping common NOTAM patterns → CFR sections (NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE → §91.141, 'space flight ops' → §91.143, 'stadium' → §91.145, etc.) so the working tier carries the lookup table.
3. Per-document boost in the tree store for the §91.137-145 cluster when 'TFR' / 'restriction' / '49 USC 40103' appear in the query.
4. Two-stage retrieval: pre-classify the NOTAM type (VIP / disaster / sporting / space / hazardous) with a small-model call, then embed the canonical §-rule for that type.

Belongs under harness-3jz1 (TFR explainer epic), likely subordinate to harness-3jz1.4 (web extension contract) or its own follow-up.

Diagnostic context discovered while fixing harness-ygvg.

title: airton_c_tfr scope_redirect + citation hooks hardcoded for airton_c1 — fix bleed-over
description:
Three cascading bugs in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py that cause airton_c_tfr replies to bleed airton_c1 identity ('I'm a JO 7110.65 specialist').

Repro: paste a 14 CFR §91.141 TFR NOTAM into an airton_c_tfr session. The first reply is a correct §91.141 decode. missing_citation falsely fires (regex blind to CFR dot-form); on retry, scope_redirect falsely fires (because the directive says 'Surface the geometry' and 'geometry' is in the non-aviation lexicon), and its nudge contains airton_c1-specific example text that the model parrots verbatim.

Root causes:
1. _CITATION_PRESENT_RE (hooks.py:824) matches only JO §N-N-N hyphen-form; misses 14 CFR §91.141 dot-form. MissingCitationHook ignores the character's own citation_grammar.surface_patterns.
2. _CLEARLY_NON_AVIATION_RE (hooks.py:973) lists 'geometry' as a math-class-only term; collides with TFR cylinder geometry vocabulary baked into airton_c_tfr/core.yaml:122 directive.
3. _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE (hooks.py:1090) is hardcoded with 'airton_c1 is scoped to FAA JO 7110.65' and a JO-specialist example sentence. Never threads the character's scope_redirect_template.

Fix plan (option 2 + 3 from investigation):
- Parameterize MissingCitationHook to use the character's citation_grammar for the citation-present check, in addition to the JO hyphen-form fallback.
- Drop 'geometry' from _CLEARLY_NON_AVIATION_RE (collides with TFR/chart/radar vocabulary across all aviation characters).
- Parameterize _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE so character name and scope_redirect_template are interpolated; ScopeRedirectHook takes scope_redirect_template + character_name (or just falls back to the existing airton_c1 text when None).
- Pipe scope_redirect_template and character name through default_hook_pipeline.
close_reason: Three cascading airton_c1-hardcoded bugs in hooks.py fixed: (1) _CITATION_PRESENT_RE only matched JO/AIM hyphen-form, missing 14 CFR §91.141 dot-form → MissingCitationHook + UncitedSubstantiveReplyHook now also consult character.citation_grammar.surface_patterns via _reply_has_citation helper; (2) 'geometry' in _CLEARLY_NON_AVIATION_RE collided with airton_c_tfr's 'Surface the geometry' directive → dropped from regex with comment explaining why; (3) _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE hardcoded 'I'm a JO 7110.65 specialist' → renamed to _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE_DEFAULT (generic), added _build_scope_redirect_nudge() helper that interpolates character_name + scope_redirect_template, ScopeRedirectHook gained both fields, plumbed character_name through default_hook_pipeline + cli.py + cli_classic.py + evals/tool_loop.py. Five regression tests added. All 2099 tests pass, ruff + mypy clean.

title: harness.web: generalizable character-FastAPI factory (base endpoints, request-scoped tools, grammar reply)
description:
Generalizable harness primitive that turns ANY character into a web-served FastAPI app. The TFR-specific extension (POST /explain + GET /tfr_list + GET /debug/parse) lives in harness-3jz1.4 as a thin character module on top of this.

Created 2026-05-15 as a split-out from the original harness-3jz1.4 scope after the user asked the API to be generalizable so future characters (CFI cite tool, debrief copilot, returns_handler, etc.) plug in the same way.

Package layout (src/harness/web/):
  - base.py — build_character_app(character, adapter) -> FastAPI. Mounts base_router + discovers a character-specific router if present at src/harness/web/characters/<name>.py.
  - base_router.py — the base endpoints every character exposes:
      * GET /healthz — {status, character, model, uptime_s}
      * GET /character — character.describe() as JSON: name, premise, values, taboos, deep_domains, tool surface. SPAs read this for 'About this tool'.
      * POST /chat — single-turn {text, options?} -> {reply, citations?, retrieved_chunks?}. Runs the character's full grounding stack (assemble_context contract, fabrication catchers, citation grammar). Stateless. NOTE: works against tool-style characters (TFR) but their scope_redirect will refuse non-scope-shaped input — that's the expected behavior.
      * GET /capabilities — lists every endpoint the app exposes (base + character-specific) with methods + schema refs. Drives capability-driven SPA UI so a new character gets a usable surface without SPA changes.
  - tool_registry.py — generalizable request-scoped tool registry primitive. Lets a character bind a per-request callable into the orchestrator's tool registry without mutating the global registry. Pattern: with_request_scoped(name, fn) -> Registry. Used by TFR's read_parsed_notam (via harness-3jz1.4) and reusable for any future per-request tool.
  - grammar.py — grammar-constrained reply mechanism extending the existing outlines use beyond the router. Opt-in per endpoint via schema arg. Returns parsed JSON matching the schema. Currently MLX-only; Ollama path is a future bead. The mechanism is a thin helper that wraps the adapter call with outlines — keeps the model.ModelAdapter protocol unchanged for now (promote to the protocol later if more callers want it).
