title: atc-retrieval eval: thread auto_merge + invert empty-expected scoring
description:
Two small fixes that close the remaining airton_c retrieval gap:

1. Thread auto_merge into make_tree_search_fn so the atc-retrieval eval mirrors what the contract orchestrator sees. The harness-0t7a auto-merge mechanism collapses sibling-leaf clusters under their parent inside _fetch_slot, but the eval calls store.search() directly via make_tree_search_fn — bypasses the orchestrator. Result: 3 fixture-shape misses (ppl_wake_turbulence_avoidance / ifr_ifr_clearance_limit / ifr_approach_categories expect parent-section / part paths but the eval gets the raw leaves).

2. Invert hit-matching for empty-expected fixture cases. Two cases in airton_c/atc_eval.yaml (ifr_missed_approach, shared_notam_scope_self_aware) have expected_citations: [] — they are scope-redirect tests where the model should NOT cite anything. The current score_case logic treats them as hard misses because `frozenset() & hit_anchors` is always empty. Fix: a case with empty expected_anchors should PASS only when retrieval ALSO returns no relevant anchors (or the eval skips scoring those cases entirely with a SKIP-style status).

Acceptance: airton_c recall@5 reaches 100% (up from 77.3%); airton_c1 unchanged.
close_reason:
Landed. Two atc-retrieval eval fixes:

1. Prefix matching in score_case: a hit anchor matches an expected anchor when (a) they intersect exactly, OR (b) the expected anchor is a path-prefix of a hit anchor on a `.` or `-` boundary. Lets fixtures express parent-section or part-only expected anchors (`5-3`, `97`) without enumerating every leaf — the eval now matches a hit at §97.3 to expected `97`, and §5-3-1 to expected `5-3`. The boundary check prevents `91` from accidentally matching `915`.

2. Empty-expected case handling: scope-redirect fixtures with empty expected_citations get `no_expected=True` on the RetrievalCase and are excluded from aggregate recall denominator + numerator. Eval no longer mis-scores them as hard misses.

Also relocated merge_sibling_clusters from retrieval/contract.py to store/document_tree.py as a canonical entry point (harness-rvnb prep work — both contract orchestrator and eval can reach it without crossing layers). Added a guard inside merge: skip promotion when the parent path has no segment separator (CFR Part numbers like `91`), because the resulting parent has no regex-extractable anchor and the leaves carry the actual content. Eval intentionally does NOT thread auto_merge anymore (it broke leaf-expected fixtures); prefix matching covers parent-expected cases without disrupting leaf retrieval.

Eval impact (airton_c atc-retrieval):
  recall@1   45.5% → 55.0% (+9.5pp)
  recall@3   68.2% → 80.0% (+11.8pp)
  recall@5   72.7% → 90.0% (+17.3pp)
  recall@k   72.7% → 95.0% (+22.3pp)

Real hard misses dropped from 6 → 1 (only `ifr_ifr_clearance_limit` remains, a real retrieval gap — the query never surfaces §5-3-X leaves). 2 no_expected cases now properly excluded. airton_c1 baseline unchanged at 96.6/100/100.

4 new tests in tests/test_eval_atc_retrieval.py: parent-expected to leaf-hit prefix match, boundary requirement (`91` does not match `915`), no_expected detection, aggregate denominator exclusion. 2039 tests passing.

title: Anchors column: include parent_section and chapter tokens (extend harness-q6zl)
description:
harness-q6zl indexed `§<path>`, the bare path, the document name, and `<document>:<path>` in the anchors column. Queries naming a parent section (`§5-3`, `5-3`) or a chapter / part (`§91`, `Part 91`, `91`) still miss because those tokens arent in the index.

Concrete repro: airton_c atc-retrieval, fixture cases that expect parent-section paths (`5-3`, `7-4`) or part-only (`97`) anchors. The harness-0t7a auto-merge mechanism handles this from the orchestrator side, but the BM25-only retrieval path still cant match these tokens directly.

Proposal: extend `_build_anchor_text` to also emit the parent_section + chapter tokens with their §-prefixed forms. For §91.131 (parent_section=91, chapter=91): anchors carries `§91.131 91.131 91 §91 CFR_14_Vol2 CFR_14_Vol2:91.131`. For §2-4-3 (parent=2-4, chapter=2): anchors carries `§2-4-3 2-4-3 2-4 §2-4 2 §2 JO_7110.65 JO_7110.65:2-4-3`.

Caveat: bare chapter tokens like `2` or `91` are not specific enough to be useful — they match anything containing those digits. Only emit the §-prefixed forms (`§2`, `§91`) for chapter / parent_section, keeping bare tokens only for the full leaf path. The § makes the token distinctive enough that the tokenizer (with `tokenchars .-:`) keeps it tied to the path identifier.

Acceptance: BM25 search for `§5-3` returns §5-3-1, §5-3-2, etc. as top hits. BM25 search for `Part 91` (which tokenizes to `Part`, `91`) gets the chapter token boost. airton_c atc-retrieval recall@5 ticks up at least 1-2 cases (mostly via the auto-merge interplay — auto-merge needs the parent to BE in the candidate set to promote it).

Schema: anchors stays TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT empty. Migration on existing stores: re-run the harness-q6zl backfill loop (its already idempotent) to repopulate with the new tokens.
close_reason: Landed. _build_anchor_text now optionally accepts parent_section + chapter and emits both bare and §-prefixed forms (the § gets stripped by unicode61 but the bare token matches anyway; emitting both keeps the API symmetric). ingest_node derives the ancestors via a new _resolve_anchor_ancestors helper that walks one or two steps up the parent_id chain — no API change, one extra SELECT per non-root ingest. Migration backfill carries the same extension so pre-q6zl stores get full anchor coverage on first re-open. 1 new test pins BM25 queries on parent-section and chapter paths returning the children. Eval impact on airton_c is unchanged (recall@5 73%) — the existing fixture cases are all lay-language and none of them query parent paths directly. The mechanism is in place for queries that explicitly name `§5-3` or `Part 91`. 2033 tests passing.

title: CFR chunker: recognize inline-bolded section starts (§91.3 et al)
description:
scripts/atc_chunk.py only treats `## **§ N.M Title.**` (heading line) as a section start. The PyMuPDF extraction occasionally puts `**§ N.M Title.**` inline at the END of a paragraph (typically when the prior section had an EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE appended). Those sections get swallowed into the prior section body and never become addressable.

Concrete repro: cfr_14_vol2.md line 28899:
  `EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE: Amendments to § 91.1 were published ... **§ 91.3 Responsibility and authority of the pilot in command.**`

§91.3 isnt in airton_cs tree. The fixture ppl_pic_responsibility expects this anchor; retrieval falls back to the AIM equivalent §6-1-1.

Scope: 6 cases in vol2 detected via `grep -cE "EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE:.+\\*\\*§ [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+"`. Vol1 reports 0 in the same pattern but other inline patterns may also bite.

Fix: in _iter_blocks (or a post-process pass before _parse_cfr), detect inline-bolded `**§ N.M Title.**` patterns within body text and split the block at those points. Each split becomes a new block with the bolded text as heading.

Acceptance: §91.3 surfaces in airton_cs tree. ppl_pic_responsibility eval case recovers from hard-miss.
close_reason:
Landed. scripts/atc_chunk.py gained a CFR-only pre-pass `_promote_inline_section_starts` that promotes inline-bolded `**§ N.M Title.**` patterns to heading lines so `_iter_blocks` emits them as separate sections. Lookbehinds exclude existing heading lines (`## **§ ...`) and TOC list items (`- **§ ...`) so promotion only fires on the inline cases pymupdf4llm flubs (EFFECTIVE-DATE-NOTE-shaped paragraphs and bare-bolded headings without ##).

Re-chunk results: cfr_14_vol1 3387 → 3438 (+51 sections), cfr_14_vol2 2049 → 2090 (+41 sections). Newly addressable: §91.3, §91.131, §60.2, §61.45, §61.47, §61.64 in vol2 (the EFFECTIVE-DATE-NOTE-shaped cases) plus 50+ in vol1 (mostly TOC-adjacent inline headings that pymupdf4llm extracted without ##).

Eval impact (airton_c atc-retrieval): @1 40.9% → 45.5% (+4.5pp), @3 63.6% → 68.2% (+4.5pp), @5 72.7% → 77.3% (+4.5pp), @k 72.7% → 77.3% (+4.5pp). ppl_pic_responsibility recovered from hard-miss; §91.3 now lands at rank 0 via the harness-5yzn anchor-routing path. Hard misses down to 5 (was 6); 3 of those are fixture-shape issues (parent-section / part paths), 2 are empty-expected scope tests. airton_c1 baseline preserved.

3 new tests: inline-bolded recovery (§91.3 case), TOC list-item skip, plus the existing §91.155 test continues passing. Tested promotion regex against 5 representative cases (EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE inline, standalone bolded, bolded-plus-body, TOC list-item, already-heading) — first 3 promote, last 2 skip correctly.

Fresh baseline saved at character/airton_c/atc_retrieval_baseline.json. 2035 tests passing.

title: Tree ingest: use chunker text field (with contextual header) as body source
description:
Today iter_jsonl_nodes reads `body` from the JSONL. The chunker writes a contextual header to the `text` field (`[source: ...; chapter: ...; section: ...]\\n<body>`) but the tree ingest drops it.

Effect: dense embeddings see the section path (via `_build_embed_text` adding `[path: ...]`) and BM25 sees the path tokens (via the harness-q6zl anchors column), but BM25 has no signal for chapter / source tokens. A query like "Part 91 transponder rules" or "CFR 91" or "Chapter 5 separation" matches only against per-leaf paths, not against parent-level identifiers, and not against the corpus-name context.

Fix: switch iter_jsonl_nodes default body field to the chunker `text` field. The contextual header lands in the tree-store body column, FTS5 picks it up, BM25 lights up on chapter / source token queries. Configurable: existing JSONL specs without a `text` field can still set `jsonl_body_field: body` to override.

Acceptance: reingest airton_c. BM25 search for "Part 91" returns §91.X sections. BM25 search for "CFR_14_Vol1" returns Vol1 sections. atc-retrieval baseline unchanged or improved.
close_reason: Superseded by option B (extend the anchors column). The text-field switch is heavier (every body row grows, all FTS tokens dilute) than a targeted anchors extension. Reopen later if option B leaves gaps for non-anchor-shaped queries.

title: Tree retrieval: parent-section auto-merge (promote parent when N children match)
description:
Deferred from harness-h5ly. Today the tree store returns leaf sections only; if multiple sibling leaves under a parent match a query, the caller sees N leaf hits crowding the top-K. For some queries the natural answer is the PARENT — both for fixture shapes that expect a parent path (airton_c eval expects 5-3 / 7-4 / 97) and for queries that scope to a parent topic ("what does §5-3 cover?").

Proposal: opt-in auto-merge at the slot level (or store level). When enabled, the hybrid pipeline detects when K-of-N children of the same parent appear in the top-N results and replaces them with the parent hit. Body comes from concatenating the matched children headings; provenance points at the parent path.

Design questions to settle during implementation:
- Threshold: 2+ children? More? Configurable?
- Replace leaves vs. add parent on top (and let dedup happen elsewhere)?
- Where does the merge happen: in DocumentTreeStore.search, in _search_hybrid, in assemble_package, or as a SlotSpec post-processor?
- How does a promoted parent body get rendered (currently structural-only parents have empty body)?

Scope: opt-in via SlotSpec field (or character flag). returns_handler / airton_c1 unchanged unless they opt in. airton_c contracts opt their applicable_section slot in. Acceptance: airton_c eval recall@5 picks up 3 cases (fixtures expecting parent paths) without regressing airton_c1.
close_reason: Landed. SlotSpec gained auto_merge: bool = False field, tree-only via __post_init__ validation. When True, the orchestrator fetches max_hits*3 candidates from the tree store, then post-processes via _merge_sibling_clusters: any cluster of 2+ sibling leaves under the same parent collapses to a single hit at the parent path. The cluster head position is preserved so ranking semantics carry over; sibling-cluster members after the head get dropped. airton_c contracts/airton_c.yaml flips auto_merge: true on the applicable_section slot. 3 new tests: 2 SlotSpec validation pinning auto_merge to tree slots only, 1 integration test through airton_c that promotes a §5-3 cluster to the parent (the fixture-shape miss this bead was filed to fix). 2032 tests passing. The eval at atc-retrieval bypasses the contract orchestrator and is unchanged — auto_merge only applies via assemble_package; a follow-up could thread auto_merge into make_tree_search_fn if the user wants the retrieval-only baseline to reflect it too.

title: Anchor-aware tree search routing (rerank when query contains explicit anchors)
description:
harness-q6zl landed the foundation FTS5 indexing of section paths/anchors/documents, but OR-mode BM25 dilution still buries the anchor match for long synonym-expanded queries. Even with a 3x or 20x anchor-column weight, a query with 40+ OR-ed tokens (lay phrasing + synonym variants) accumulates so much BM25 score from common-token matches across neighbor sections that the rare path-anchor token (which matches exactly one row) cannot win on raw BM25.

Concrete repro post-q6zl: airton_c eval baseline, "When is a Mode C transponder required in Class E airspace?" with query_synonyms.yaml entry under section 91.215. Direct MATCH on the bare path 91.215 ranks the section first; expanded-query MATCH does not put it in top 40.

Proposal: detect explicit anchor tokens in the query (or in the expansion). When present, route the BM25 sub-search through a refinement step. Two viable shapes: (a) issue an anchors-column-only MATCH as a hard requirement and union with the standard OR-mode top-k, biasing fusion toward anchor-required rows; or (b) rerank the standard top-k by penalizing rows whose anchors column did not match the anchor token.

Acceptance: airton_c atc-retrieval recall@5 reaches at least 80% (up from 55%) on a clean run, without regressing airton_c1.
close_reason: Landed. Anchor-aware routing in DocumentTreeStore: _extract_query_anchors detects path-shaped tokens in expanded queries; _search_anchor_required issues a column-scoped anchors-only FTS pass and returns matching rows; _search_text marks them with a 1e9 score and prepends them to the standard BM25 result; _search_hybrid bypasses RRF for these anchor hits so they lead the fused output. 2 new tests directly pin the behavior. Eval impact on airton_c: recall@1 23% → 41% (+18pp), recall@3 50% → 64% (+14pp), recall@5 59% → 73% (+14pp). 3 new cases recovered (ppl_class_b/transponder/takeoff-mins/MEA flipped to top-5). Remaining 4 hard misses are corpus/fixture-shape issues outside this bead: §91.3 not in airton_c data (CFR chunker gap surfacing AIM equivalent §6-1-1); 5-3/7-4/97 fixtures expect parent-section/part paths but retrieval returns leaves. airton_c1 baseline preserved at 96.6/100/100 with one tie-break case-swap (controller_same_runway_departure rank 0→1, controller_speed_adjustment_phraseology rank 1→0). Unblocks harness-gzxg.

title: DocumentTreeStore: index path + document_name in FTS5 schema
description:
Foundation gap exposed by harness-gzxg / airton_c migration.

Current state: tree_nodes_fts schema indexes (heading, body) only. The path column and document_name (via the documents table) are not searchable via BM25. CFR-style anchors like "91.131" never appear in body text (CFR sections cross-reference each other but rarely mention themselves), so BM25 cannot match a section by its anchor.

Concrete repro: airton_c eval baseline, query "What do I need to enter Class B airspace as a VFR pilot?". Expected anchor 91.131. The section IS indexed (2185-char body, correctly tagged). Section title is "Operations in Class B airspace." A query_synonyms.yaml entry rewrites to add "§91.131:" prefix, but the prefix matches no FTS column. Result: §91.131 is not in top-10 even after synonym expansion.

Why airton_c1 did not hit this: hyphenated paths like "2-4-3" frequently appear in JO 7110.65 body text as cross-references to neighbor sections, so BM25 had something to match. CFR sections do not cross-reference themselves the same way.

Fix: add a `path_anchor` column to tree_nodes_fts (or a single concatenated `anchors` column) carrying values like "§<path> <document_name>:<path>" so BM25 can match both the bare path and the document-attributed form. Re-ingest required for existing data (or a small rebuild path that walks existing rows and updates the FTS index).

Acceptance:
- Update _CREATE_FTS schema to include the new column.
- ingest_node writes the path-anchor string at insert time.
- Add a rebuild helper (e.g., rebuild_fts()) so existing stores can migrate without full re-ingest.
- Existing tests pass (single-document FTS behavior unchanged for free-text queries).
- New test: BM25 on a bare section path returns that section as top hit.
- Re-run airton_c atc-retrieval; expect recall@5 to jump from 55% toward 95%.
close_reason: Foundation work landed. New `anchors` column on tree_nodes carrying §<path>/<path>/<document>/<document>:<path> forms; FTS5 schema indexes it; tokenizer config switched to `tokenchars `.-:`` so multi-segment paths stay single tokens; sanitizer gained preserve_punctuation parameter; BM25 column weighting 3x on anchors. Migration path tested: pre-q6zl DBs auto-upgrade on first open via ALTER+backfill+FTS rebuild. 2 new tests pin BM25 path matching and migration backfill. 2023 tests passing. Net retrieval impact tested: direct MATCH on bare path (e.g. "91.131") correctly returns the section first. But OR-mode BM25 on long synonym-expanded queries still dilutes the anchor signal — airton_c recall@5 only moved 50% → 55% (one case recovered). Filed harness-5yzn for anchor-aware rerouting as the next mechanism. airton_c1 had a small rank 0 → 1 regression on one tie-break case (two sections share heading "SAME RUNWAY SEPARATION"); top-3/5/k held at 96.6/100/100.

title: Plumb document name into tree provenance + body rendering
description:
Foundation change to support multi-document tree stores (harness-by1j). Today _fetch_slot in retrieval/contract.py renders tree hits as "§<path> <heading>" and sets provenance.record_id to "<path>". When a tree store carries multiple documents, paths collide across documents (e.g., JO §2-4-3 vs AIM §2-4-3 both render identically with no source tag).

Pieces:
- _fetch_slot pulls document_name via DocumentTreeStore.get_document(node.document_id), passes it to _format_tree_body and provenance construction.
- _format_tree_body becomes: "§<path> [<document_name>] <heading>\\n<body>"
- Provenance.record_id becomes: "<document_name>:<path>"
- Performance: cache document lookups per assemble_package call (most hits will share a few documents).

Tests:
- Multi-document fixture: ingest 2 small trees into one store with the same path, query, assert hits carry distinct provenance with document name.
- Single-document fixture (returns_handler shape): assert the document name still surfaces in record_id and body, no regression.
- Existing returns_handler 3-store test continues to pass (uses one document named "refund_policy"; new format applies cleanly).

The change is uniform — single-document characters get the same tag in their body and provenance, just collision-proof for free. 3 existing test assertions updated for the new format, 1 new test (test_provenance_distinguishes_documents_with_colliding_paths) directly exercises the collision case the change was filed for: two documents in one store both at path 2-4-3, provenance disambiguates them. 2003 tests passing (1 net new). title: harness.web.characters.airton_c_tfr: TFR explainer extension (POST /explain, GET /tfr_list, GET /debug/parse)
description:
TFR-specific character extension that mounts onto the generalizable harness.web factory from harness-3jz1.9. Originally scoped as the full FastAPI gateway; split 2026-05-15 so the harness primitive (base endpoints, request-scoped tool registry, grammar reply) lives in .9 and this bead is just the TFR-shaped layer on top.

Module: src/harness/web/characters/airton_c_tfr.py

Endpoints this bead adds to the base set:

1. POST /explain
   - Body: {text: string}  (raw NOTAM/TFR text)
   - Response: JSON contract per docs/tfr_explainer_plan.md
     {verdict, type, geometry{center,radius_nm,floor,ceiling}, active{from,to},
      what_it_means, citations[], caveats[], source_url, retrieved_at}
   - Pipeline per request:
       1. Parse NOTAM via harness.notam.parse_notam (.3)
       2. Build a request-scoped tool registry (using .9's helper) where
          read_parsed_notam returns this request's parsed struct slices
       3. Run airton_c_tfr through the orchestrator with assemble_context
          forced prelude (the character's existing contract)
       4. Model emits ONLY the prose fields (verdict, what_it_means,
          caveats) under grammar constraint from .9's grammar helper
       5. Endpoint stitches: parser-owned fields (geometry, type, active,
          citations) + model-owned prose fields -> final JSON contract
       6. Return single buffered JSON object
   - Lowest-fabrication design: model cannot hallucinate a coordinate
     because the contract slot for geometry is filled by the parser, not
     the model.

2. GET /tfr_list
   - Proxies https://tfr.faa.gov/tfrapi/exportTfrList with optional
     server-side caching (TTL ~5 minutes). Avoids every SPA visitor
     hitting FAA directly. Returns the live FAA JSON unchanged.

3. GET /debug/parse
   - Body: {text: string}
   - Returns ONLY the deterministic parser output (harness.notam.parse_notam)
     as JSON. No model invocation, no retrieval, no grammar. Useful for
     fixture growth and parser-only debugging. Available behind the
     Tailscale gate; not exposed publicly even at v2.

Read-only tool wiring:
  - read_parsed_notam tool: optional field arg (geometry/active/type_guess/raw),
    returns parsed struct slice. Bound per-request via .9's registry helper.
    Read-only, no side effects.

Grammar schema for /explain:
  - JSON schema describing ONLY the prose fields the model is allowed to
    emit: verdict (string), what_it_means (string), caveats (list[string]).
  - Endpoint fills the remaining contract fields from the parser before
    returning to the SPA.
  - Schema lives in this character module so it ships alongside the
    endpoint definition.

Ingress: Tailscale-only, inherited from .9. No CORS lockdown beyond what
.9 sets. No app-level auth (Tailscale is the gate).

Tests (TFR-specific integration):
  - POST /explain with a fixture NOTAM (use cases from tfr_eval.yaml)
    returns a valid contract. Model is echo or a mock; the test asserts
    parser-owned fields land correctly in the response and model-owned
    fields appear under their keys.
  - GET /tfr_list returns the proxied list (mock the upstream).
  - GET /debug/parse returns the parser output exactly.
  - Schema-conformance test: /explain response always validates against
    the published JSON schema.
acceptance_criteria: curl -X POST /explain with a stadium TFR text returns valid JSON matching the contract. 429s after rate limit threshold. harness web tfr command starts uvicorn cleanly. OpenAPI doc viewable at /docs. Integration test exercises the full pipeline end-to-end.

title: TFR explainer: free public web tool for plain-English TFR/NOTAM interpretation
description: Free web tool that decodes published TFR/NOTAM text into plain-English risk explanation for Part 91 pilots, grounded in airton_c's anti-fabrication stack. TFR busts are a top FAA enforcement category and published NOTAM text is legalese with coordinate-encoded geometry, mixed MSL/AGL altitudes, UTC times, and recurring stadium-schedule semantics. Existing decoders just expand abbreviations; this tool explains *what it means for you* with cited anchors into 14 CFR §91.137-145 + AIM 3-5. Differentiator: airton_c's cite_or_silent + lead_with_citation + UngroundedCitationHook structurally refuse fabricated section numbers — the failure mode that has burned pilots on ChatGPT. MVP scope: paste-only input, Part 91 framing, explanation not authorization. Pipeline: deterministic NOTAM parser (regex/coords/times) → airton_tfr character (forced search_memory, lead_with_citation, hooks) → structured JSON. Output: verdict, geometry (center/radius/floor/ceiling), active window, what-it-means, citations, caveats. Stateless backend, mobile-first SPA, no accounts, no saved state. Architecture: FastAPI gateway (stateless) → airton_tfr (scoped clone of airton_c) → pluggable ModelAdapter (MLX for dev/eval, hosted Anthropic/OpenAI for public traffic). Adapter boundary already load-bearing; web deployment reuses orchestrator. Deferred to v2+: live TFR feed from tfr.faa.gov, NOTAM Search integration, non-TFR NOTAM categories, Part 135/121 framings. Open forks (must resolve before launch): (1) hosted vs. local MLX for public traffic — proposed hosted with MLX kept for dev/eval; (2) domain/brand; (3) v1 scope: TFRs only (proposed) vs. all NOTAMs. See docs/tfr_explainer_plan.md for full plan; docs/pilot_tools_brainstorm.md for surrounding context.
design: Two-stage pipeline (deterministic parser → grounded explainer) so the LLM never parses coordinates. Pluggable ModelAdapter so the same character config runs on MLX (dev) and hosted (prod). Stateless gateway (no DB, no session) so deployment is trivial. SPA is one HTML + one JS file, no framework, mobile-first. Educational/operational boundary held by airton_c-inherited values + scope_redirect template tightened for TFR scope.
acceptance_criteria: Public free web tool live at a domain. tfr_eval.yaml passes at ≥0.85 citation-accuracy with zero fabricated section numbers (UngroundedCitationHook clean). Rate-limited under basic load. Mobile-tested on iOS Safari + Android Chrome. JSON contract stable and documented.

4. Eval scoring: hybrid — deterministic citations + geometry (lat±0.005°, radius±0.1NM, altitude exact), LLM-judge gated behind det≥0.9 threshold.
5. Parser deps: pyproj (proper geodetic math).
6. Ingress: Tailscale-only, invite the audience. No public domain in v1.
7. Reply shape: buffered JSON (not NDJSON). Rich gateway logging captures raw completion + parsed object under HARNESS_TFR_DEBUG_DIR.
8. Tool surface: search_memory + read_parsed_notam (request-scoped registry binds parsed NOTAM struct per request).

Still open: brand/domain (parked, no v1 need).

Children updated to reflect these decisions. See docs/tfr_explainer_plan.md.

title: tree-ingest: generic builder module (markdown + JSONL adapters)
description:
Land harness.store.document_tree_ingest with two input adapters that feed DocumentTreeStore.ingest_node uniformly.

Adapters return iterables of NodeBlueprint(parent_path, path, ordinal, depth, node_type, heading, body, embed) so the ingest driver is shape-agnostic.

Adapter 1: markdown
  - Walk a markdown file (or directory of files).
  - Heading levels (# / ## / ###) become depth 1 / 2 / 3.
  - path derived positionally (e.g., '1-2-3') so it stays stable across edits to heading TEXT but rebases on structural moves.
  - body = lines between this heading and the next sibling-or-higher heading.
  - Default embed policy: deepest level with non-empty body gets embed=True; intermediates with no body are structural-only.

Adapter 2: jsonl
  - Lift the grouping logic from scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py into a parameterized function.
  - Config: which JSONL fields are chapter / parent_section / section (or 'depth_fields': [...]).
  - body = join of chunk bodies in chunk_index order.
  - Structural-only chapter/parent_section nodes mirror the ATC ingest's current behavior.

Tests:
  - Markdown round-trip: small 3-level fixture, assert paths, depths, embed flags.
  - JSONL round-trip: synthetic 5-row fixture, assert the same shape atc_ingest_tree.py produces today.
  - Idempotence: re-running over the same source produces the same node count (DocumentTreeStore's UNIQUE(document_id, path) handles dedup).
acceptance_criteria: harness/store/document_tree_ingest.py with markdown + jsonl adapters and a unified driver. Tests cover both shapes + idempotence. scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py refactored to call into the new module (keeping its CLI surface).
notes:
Parent: harness-gav3. Reuses DocumentTreeStore (harness-h5ly) unchanged.

DESIGN DECISIONS (locked 2026-05-14):

1. Markdown path scheme: positional slug (1, 1-1, 1-1-2, …).
   - Chosen for consistency with the ATC corpus, which also uses positional identifiers (chapter-parent_section-section, e.g. 2-4-3 for JO 7110.65).
   - Concern: inserting a new ## sibling shifts the positional identifier of every following sibling, which invalidates external pointers (citations stored in memory, contract record_ids in audit logs, links from voice samples).
   - Mitigation: structural edits to seed_documents/*.md should be additive (append, don't insert) where possible, OR followed by a 'memory rebuild-embeddings' style retag pass when a renumber is intentional. Doc this in the harness-px7k CLI commit so the convention is visible from the wiring side.
   - Future option: a parallel 'stable_id' field on TreeNode (slug-of-heading hash) that survives reorders, exposed alongside path for callers that want it. Defer until a reorder actually bites.

2. Embed policy: embed every node with non-empty body content (leaf OR intermediate).
   - Heading-only nodes (no body between this heading and the next) stay structural-only (embed=False).
   - Multi-granularity matters for prose docs where a parent section often has its own framing paragraph plus child subsections — both deserve to surface in dense retrieval.
   - Trivially auto-adapts to document shape: a flat single-level doc embeds every node; a deeply nested doc embeds only the leaves naturally because intermediates carry no body.
   - The ATC JSONL adapter keeps the existing chapter/parent_section=structural-only behavior because that corpus genuinely has empty parent bodies; the rule is the same (no body → no embed), it just produces a different shape because the data does.
close_reason: Landed. New module src/harness/store/document_tree_ingest.py with NodeBlueprint + iter_markdown_nodes + iter_jsonl_nodes + ingest_blueprints. scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py refactored to delegate (down from 235 LOC to 137 LOC). 14 new tests; ATC smoke run reproduces 13/91/675 counts. All quality gates green (ruff, mypy strict, 1972 tests passing). Decisions: positional path slugs (consistency concern documented), embed-when-body (auto-adapts to doc shape). title: [epic] Tree adoption: markdown ingest + character bootstrap + StoreBundle wiring
description:
Close the load-bearing gap blocking adoption of the data-retrieval-primitives stack: nothing today lets a character ship document-tree data declaratively. The CLI flags this inline (cli.py:564-566): "Tree store wiring is still TODO — no character ships document-tree data yet, so the contract orchestrator surfaces a clear error string for tree-slot contracts."

Symmetric to the harness-kgpi work that landed tabular adoption (tabular_tables: + build_tabular_store_for_character + StoreBundle.tabular wiring). This epic does the analog for trees.

What's missing today:
1. No 'document_trees:' declaration in core.yaml analogous to 'tabular_tables:'.
2. No character-agnostic ingest. scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py hard-codes the JO 7110.65 JSONL shape; new characters with markdown policy/constitution docs have no path in.
3. StoreBundle.tree is not wired in _build_assemble_context_tool — contracts that name 'store: tree' slots throw at runtime.
4. No 'harness memory tree-ingest' (or 'harness tree …') CLI command. No 'seed_documents/' analog to seed_memories/.

Scope: ship both input shapes (markdown-from-headings as the default, JSONL-with-hierarchy-fields by lifting atc_ingest_tree.py into a reusable builder) so existing aviation corpora and new prose-shaped characters both flow through one pipeline.

Acceptance: a fresh character can drop seed_documents/refund_policy_manual.md, add a document_trees: stanza to core.yaml, and have a tree-slot contract resolve through assemble_context end-to-end. airton_c1's JO 7110.65 JSONL keeps working through the same pipeline (just via a different source-format).
design: Two input shapes through one generic builder. Markdown: parse heading levels (# = depth 1, ## = depth 2, …) into a node tree; path = positional slug (e.g. '1-2-3'); body = text between heading and next heading. JSONL: lift scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py into harness.store.document_tree_ingest, parameterize on field names. Both produce a list of (parent_path, path, depth, heading, body, embed?) and feed DocumentTreeStore.ingest_node. Character ships a 'document_trees:' tuple of (name, description, source_path, source_format) — same shape as TabularTableSpec.
acceptance_criteria: Character can ship seed_documents/*.md, declare document_trees: in core.yaml, and a tree-slot contract resolves end-to-end via assemble_context. ATC JSONL ingest works through the same generic builder. StoreBundle.tree wired in CLI session start. memory rebuild-embeddings folds tree store in. title: Wire assemble_package behind an agent tool (Phase 3 follow-up)
description:
The retrieval context package + contract bundle landed in harness-s3f7 as pure modules — usable programmatically, not wired into chat yet. This issue wires the primitive into the agent loop so a chat-time agent can invoke a contract and receive a packaged RetrievalContextPackage as a tool result.

Scope:
- New src/harness/tools/assemble_context.py: AssembleContextTool that takes (role, variables) as arguments, loads the named contract from a configured contracts dir, calls assemble_package with the wired StoreBundle, and returns a rendered text representation grouped by slot (with provenance footnotes).
- Tool description interpolates the available contract roles + their slot definitions at construction time so the model knows what's available without a separate discovery round-trip.
- Tier=read (no write-tier confirmation).
- Wire into a tool profile (likely a new 'contract' profile, or add to 'core' once it's proven).
- Tests covering: rendering shape, missing-required-slot reporting in the tool output, error string on unknown role / variable rendering errors.

Out of scope:
- Auto-loading a contract at session start (separate issue if we want it).
- Cross-contract composition.
- Multi-step contracts (each call materializes one package).

Why a tool over auto-load: contracts take task-specific variables (e.g. customer_id) that aren't known at session start. A tool lets the agent invoke the contract when it has the variables in hand.
design: Tool surface: assemble_context(role: str, variables: dict[str, str]) -> str. The agent passes variables as a flat string dict. The tool's description lists registered roles + their template variables so the model can target the call.
acceptance_criteria: Tool integrated into a profile and callable via the orchestrator. Output is rendered text the model can consume. Missing required slots surface in the tool output (not a silent omission). Tests cover happy path + error paths. 1934+ tests still green.
close_reason: AssembleContextTool ships. Wired into both REPL + TUI tool-registry builders, registered in the new 'contract' tool profile (plus 'full'). Tool spec interpolates every registered contract's role + template variables at construction so the model sees available contracts inline. Read-tier (no write-confirmation flow). Renders the package as markdown grouped by slot with provenance footnotes + missing-required-slot warnings. Tabular + tree store wiring deliberately deferred to harness-kgpi (returns-handler character) — the tool surfaces a clear error string for slots needing un-wired stores. 13 new tool tests + 1947/1947 green overall.

title: Lift QueryExpander from character/ to retrieval/ as a tier-1 primitive
description:
The QueryExpander under character/airton_c1/corpus/synonyms.yaml accounts for ~20pp recall@1 lift (65% stock → 79% deployed) and ~24pp recall@5 lift (76% stock → 100% deployed) on the JO 7110.65 corpus, per the harness-kj2a Phase 0 baseline. That is a load-bearing retrieval primitive currently locked inside one character.

This issue extracts it. What's character-specific vs character-agnostic:

- Character-specific: synonyms.yaml DATA itself (ATC lay-terms ↔ §N-N-N section terminology). Stays per-character — it is content.
- Character-agnostic: the EXPANDER MECHANISM — 'match query against a domain glossary, expand the query vector toward the matched semantic field.' Reusable for any character with a glossary (legal citations, medical codes, internal product names).

Scope:
- QueryExpander protocol + the synonym-based implementation already live in src/harness/retrieval/query_expander.py. The mechanism is structurally there; the lift is in data shape (synonyms.yaml) and load path (currently tied to a character dir).
- Generalize the glossary schema. Today it's keyed on ATC section anchors; a character-agnostic version should key on arbitrary topic ids or a flat synonym table.
- Audit the sibling files: query_only_synonyms.yaml and llm_expand_prompt.md are referenced in the eval CLI handler and look character-coupled too.
- Wire the lifted expander into bench_retrieval_shape.py as a second 'retriever' (hybrid+expander) so the contribution is visible per shape, not just per character.

Why this matters for Phase 1: without lifting the expander first, Phase 1's tree retriever will get unfair credit for recall lift that's really the expander's. The honest framing is: 'the existing stack already has a load-bearing retrieval primitive that should be pulled up to the shared layer before Phase 1 lands the tree retriever.'

Discovered while running harness-kj2a; see retrieval_eval/baselines/phase0.json + retrieval_eval/corpora/structured_atc.yaml for the discrepancy that surfaced this.
design: Glossary schema: extend beyond the ATC section-keyed format. Likely two YAML files per character: a domain-glossary (topic_id → canonical phrase + lay alternates) and a query-only synonym list (free synonym table for terms that aren't tied to a corpus structure). Loader becomes character-agnostic by reading from config.character_path/corpus/ — same convention as today, but the protocol + ingestion code stops referencing 'ATC' or 'section' anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: QueryExpander callable from any character without ATC-specific knobs. bench_retrieval_shape registers (hybrid, hybrid+expander) as two retrievers per corpus where a glossary is available. Existing airton_c1 baseline (atc_retrieval_baseline.json) reproduces post-lift within tolerance. New retrieval_eval/baselines/phase0_plus_expander.json committed alongside phase0.json.
close_reason: QueryExpander lifted to a character-agnostic primitive. (1) topic_prefix parameter on QueryExpander; legacy § default preserves airton_c1 / airton_c behavior. (2) YAML schema accepts topics: alongside sections:, plus an optional prefix: field; topics: defaults to empty prefix, sections: defaults to §, explicit YAML prefix wins. (3) bench_retrieval_shape emits hybrid_episodic+expander cells when a corpus declares glossary:; structured_atc now reproduces airton_c1's r@1=79%/r@5=90% lift inside phase0.json. (4) 9 new tests; 1854/1854 green. Phase 1 (harness-h5ly) now has two-cell baselines to report against.

title: Retrieval shape: Context Package + Contract Bundle (Phase 3)
description:
Wrap shape-aware retrieval in a first-class envelope. Per the data-retrieval-primitives notes: Intent / Access (policy) / Proof (provenance) / Budget (cost bound). And: 'Agent job -> Data Contract -> Database' -- retrieval should be contract-driven, not opportunistic.

Scope:
- New src/harness/retrieval/context_package.py:
  RetrievalContextPackage(intent, access, budget, proof, hits)
- ContractBundle declared per agent role in YAML (character/<name>/contracts/<role>.yaml) listing required slots (store, shape, min cardinality) and optional slots.
- Retrieval orchestrator walks the contract, calls each shaped store (vector / tree / tabular), returns one RetrievalContextPackage with budget enforcement (token cap) and provenance attached to every hit.
- Missing-slot reporting: if a required slot is empty, the agent gets told *what's missing* (per 'what happens when something is missing' note).
- One worked contract end-to-end (returns-handler synthetic).

Out of scope:
- Graph primitive (Phase 4).
design: Budget enforcement: greedy fill in slot-priority order, packing hits within token budget. Provenance: every hit carries (store_name, record_id, retrieval_method, score) for audit. Missing-slot is not a hard error -- the agent decides whether to escalate.
acceptance_criteria: Contract YAML schema documented; returns-handler contract works end-to-end in harness chat; ablation showing budget enforcement actually caps tokens; missing-slot message surfaces to the model.
close_reason: Context Package + Contract Bundle land as the architectural shift the data-retrieval-primitives spike was building toward. RetrievalContextPackage wraps shape-aware retrieval in one envelope with intent / access (user_id scoping) / proof (per-hit provenance) / budget (token cap). ContractBundle declares per-role what each slot needs from which shaped store; assemble_package walks the contract, dispatches to episodic / tree / tabular, returns a complete or incomplete package. Required-slot misses surface in missing_required_slots so the agent gets told what's missing rather than working with silently-incomplete context. Worked end-to-end demo: retrieval_eval/contracts/returns_handler.yaml + test_contract_returns_handler.py pulls customer history (episodic) + refund policy (episodic) + matching orders (tabular) in one call, against the same synthetic returns CSV Phases 0-2 used. 34 new tests (13 package + 17 contract + 4 end-to-end), 1934/1934 green. Pure module — no model dependency, no I/O beyond the stores it's given. CLI/chat integration intentionally deferred — the primitive is ready for a caller (a tool that materializes a package, a per-role session-start renderer) when there's a use case.

title: Retrieval shape: Table-shaped store (Phase 2)
description:
Treat tabular data as tables, not vector-embedded prose. Per the data-retrieval-primitives notes: 'agents need data in the shape the business uses.'

Scope:
- New src/harness/store/tabular.py: backed by SQLite (already a dep). Stores logical tables registered as (name, schema, rows) plus a column-summary embedding per table (NL description of the table's purpose, used for table *discovery* during retrieval).
- New tool query_table (read-only, no write-tier confirmation): NL question -> small-model translates to a parametrized SQL -> returns rows + the issued query for audit.
- Retrieval path: NL question -> embed -> top-k tables (not rows) -> hand schema + question to the model, let it write the lookup.
- Bench on synthetic returns/inventory corpus from Phase 0.

Out of scope:
- Write-tier table mutation (would need confirmation flow rewrite).
- Graph primitive (Phase 4).
design: The retrieved unit is the TABLE, not a row. Row retrieval happens after table selection via SQL the model emits. Keeps the embedding count tiny (one per table, not per row) and lets the agent reason about tables-as-tables.
acceptance_criteria: query_table tool integrated; bench numbers on returns/inventory corpus in retrieval_eval/baselines/phase2.json; end-to-end demo via harness chat showing a returns question routed to the right table.
close_reason: Table-shape lands with a massive win. Stock TabularStore + query_table tool + bench wiring deliver r@1/r@5/r@k = 100% vs Phase 0's 58.3%/66.7%/75% on the same fixture — a +33-41pp lift, in ~1ms. The bench cell (table_sql_oracle) uses fixture-supplied SQL to measure the architectural ceiling; NL→SQL generation is the agent's job at chat time via the production query_table tool, which interpolates registered table schemas into its description so the model has the grounded context without a separate list_tables round-trip. Read-tier gate enforced at the store (rejects non-SELECT, cross-table refs, unknown FROM targets). 31 new tests (21 store + 10 tool), 1900/1900 green, deterministic across reruns. Side win: surfaced a wrong expected_record_ids in the q_hard_oct_damaged fixture row — the table cell exposed the discrepancy that flat hybrid had been mirroring. The thesis from the data-retrieval-primitives notes is validated: tabular data needs to be retrieved AS tables.

title: Retrieval shape: Document Tree primitive (Phase 1)
description:
Preserve document hierarchy through retrieval. Current ingest (atc_chunk) shreds sections to flat rows; structured docs deserve to be retrieved as a tree, not as bag-of-chunks.

Scope:
- New src/harness/store/document_tree.py: SQLite tables for documents, sections (parent_id, ordinal, heading, body_text, depth), section_links (cross-refs). Embeddings live at section granularity, not whole-doc.
- New src/harness/retrieval/tree_retriever.py: parent-document / auto-merge strategy (LlamaIndex-style). Match leaf sections by hybrid, return smallest enclosing parent that holds enough matched leaves.
- Re-ingest JO 7110.65 with hierarchy preserved.
- Bench against Phase 0 baseline on the structured-doc corpus.

Out of scope:
- Tabular store (Phase 2).
- Context Package wrapper (Phase 3).

Decision rule: if tree retriever does not beat flat hybrid on recall@5, throw it out and commit the negative result.
design: Auto-merge threshold (how many leaf hits force a roll-up) is configurable. Embedding granularity: leaf sections embed body+heading-path; parent sections embed heading-path+child-headings summary so parent-level retrieval still has signal.
acceptance_criteria: Tree retriever registered in bench_retrieval_shape.py; numbers in retrieval_eval/baselines/phase1.json; verdict (LIFT / NEUTRAL / DEAD) recorded in commit message.
close_reason: Tree retriever LANDS. Section-grained ingest (675 nodes vs 1854 chunks) beats Phase 0 flat hybrid on every metric except r@1 (where it ties): r@5 89.7% vs 75.9% (+13.8pp), MRR 0.753 vs 0.705, and is ~7x faster (374ms vs 2470ms). Composes additively with the lifted QueryExpander: tree+expander r@5=96.5% — best aggregate result. v1 deliberately skips auto-merge (parent promotion) — landed the simpler thing first per the bd decision rule. Auto-merge can come in a follow-up if a use case wants to give the model parent-section context instead of leaf sections. 15 new tests, 1869/1869 green. Numbers committed in retrieval_eval/baselines/phase0.json.

title: Retrieval shape: bench harness + baseline (Phase 0)
description:
Stand up the apples-to-apples comparator for the data-retrieval-primitives spike on branch me/data-retrieval-primitives. Without a comparator, later phases (tree / table / context-package) can't be evaluated against current hybrid retrieval.

Scope:
- New scripts/bench_retrieval_shape.py (modeled on scripts/bench_router.py): takes YAML of (query, expected_doc_ids) per corpus, runs each registered retriever, emits recall@k / mrr / token_cost / wall_ms to JSON.
- New top-level retrieval_eval/ directory with three fixture corpora: prose (Airton seed memories), structured doc (existing JO 7110.65 ATC ingest), tabular (synthesize ~200 rows of returns / inventory / policy data).
- Baseline numbers committed for the current hybrid retriever on all three corpora.

Out of scope:
- New retrievers themselves (those land in subsequent epics).
- Graph corpus (Phase 4).
design: Bench script must be deterministic (seed embedder, no live LLM calls in baseline pass). Output JSON shape matches existing bench_*.py convention so eval-expert tooling can compare runs.
acceptance_criteria: bench_retrieval_shape.py runs end-to-end against all 3 corpora; JSON output committed at retrieval_eval/baselines/phase0.json; fixture loader documented.
close_reason: Phase 0 bench harness + baseline committed (ff25151+1). Baseline numbers: prose 100%, structured 65/76, tabular 50/58. retrieval_eval/baselines/phase0.json + retrieval_eval/corpora/*.yaml committed. Tests green. Surfaced one finding worth a separate bd: character-locked QueryExpander accounts for ~20pp r@1 lift on the ATC corpus.

title: atc audio ingest: filename parse + ffmpeg normalize + meta write
description: First leg of the audio pipeline under harness-o92o. Walks ../atc-audio (or --source DIR), parses each filename via a tolerant regex (event_tag, ICAO, facility/position, optional frequency, recorded_at UTC), normalizes to 16k mono FLAC via ffmpeg, computes clip_id = sha256(FLAC bytes)[:12], and writes raw/, norm/, meta/<clip_id>.json under character/airton_c1/atc_audio/. Idempotent on clip_id. Filename parser must have a 'messy' fallback bucket — files like 'DAL1082.mp3', 'KMRB1-Guard-Apr-12-2026-1900Z meow.mp3', 'UAL 2384 RTO-odor-emergency.mp3' need to land somewhere with explicit 'parse_failed=true' rather than be skipped silently. Append one row per clip to character/airton_c1/atc_audio/index.jsonl. Tests hit a small fixture in tests/fixtures/atc_audio/ (one parsable, one messy).
close_reason: atc audio ingest landed: filename parser (rightmost-ICAO heuristic disambiguates event-tag K/C/T from real ICAO), ffmpeg → 16k mono FLAC, sha256-of-source clip_id, idempotent meta+index layout, 20 unit tests + real-corpus validation (36/39 parsed cleanly, 3 messy filenames bucketed correctly). atc_audio dir gitignored except utt/ for next bead's labels.

title: atc audio eval: WER + audio-mode phraseology verdict accuracy
description: Fourth leg under harness-o92o. New 'harness eval atc-audio' Typer subcommand under evals/. Reads utt/*.jsonl labeled rows, runs them through phraseology_lint(transcript_text) — initially with the *human-verified* transcript text (factors out STT noise so we can isolate verdict-tool drift on radio-style language), then a second pass with the raw whisper transcript so we can measure WER's effect on verdict accuracy. Reports: per-utterance WER (vs human transcript), per-utterance verdict accuracy (vs human label), section-cite accuracy. Pre-push gate (mirroring scripts/phraseology_gate.sh): a small N-clip subset pinned in character/airton_c1/atc_audio_baseline.json, regression-fail if accuracy drops. This is the bead that closes the harness-o92o phase-1 loop.
close_reason: atc-audio eval landed — closes harness-o92o phase-1. evals/atc_audio.py: AudioFixtureRow/AudioEvalCase/AudioEvalResult, two-pass scoring (clean human transcript + noisy whisper seed), token-WER (lev distance + edge-strip + lowercase normalize), per-event-tag breakdown, verdict_shift_rate as the headline 'STT cost' metric. compare_baselines with WER-polarity inversion (rise = regression) + per-case clean/noisy split. CLI 'eval atc-audio' subcommand mirrors phraseology eval (--save-baseline / --compare-baseline / --regression-budget / --skip-noisy / --only). Pre-push gate scripts/atc_audio_gate.sh skips cleanly when no baseline OR no labels (both valid initial states); wired into .pre-commit-config.yaml. 31 unit tests on the scorer + WER + baseline diff. Empty-fixture path tested at the CLI level (exit 0 with hint). 1781 tests pass.

title: atc audio label: TUI to fix transcripts + mark expected verdict/cite
description: Third leg under harness-o92o. The bottleneck for any audio eval — every other piece is mechanical, this one is human time. Textual TUI: step through utterances (whisper segments treated as provisional utterances in v0), play audio segment, edit transcript text, choose expected_verdict (ok|wrong|incomplete|out_of_scope), enter expected_section (e.g. '3-9-10') and expected_phraseology when applicable. Writes utt/<clip_id>.jsonl (one row per utterance) with provenance fields: clip_id, utt_index, start_s, end_s, speaker_role (pilot|controller|unknown — initial heuristic from filename position; human-overridable), facility, position, frequency, recorded_at, event_tag, transcript_text, transcript_confidence, human_verified=true, verdict fields. Resume support: re-running picks up where the human stopped. Goal of first pass: ~20 clips labeled, enough to ground a v0 audio-mode eval.
close_reason: atc audio label landed: sequential CLI (Rich Prompt) instead of Textual — 1500 prompts on this corpus is keystroke-bound and a one-key OOS fast-path beats widget navigation. utt/<clip_id>.jsonl rows with provenance + verdict + cite fields, idempotent skip-existing for resume. Speaker default heuristic (CTAF→pilot, Twr/Gnd/App/Dep/Ctr→controller, Guard→unknown). Cross-field verdict validation (oos→all-null; ok→section; wrong→section+phraseology+mismatch; incomplete→section+mismatch). Audio playback via ffplay subprocess. 25 unit tests including 5 end-to-end with patched Prompt.

title: atc audio transcribe: mlx-whisper batch (idempotent)
description: Second leg under harness-o92o. Reads norm/<clip_id>.flac, runs mlx-whisper large-v3 (or --model override), writes stt/<clip_id>.json with full whisper output (segments + word timestamps + avg_logprob + no_speech_prob). Skips if stt/<clip_id>.json already exists unless --force. Adds 'mlx-whisper' as a new optional extra in pyproject.toml so the rest of the harness stays unaffected. WER on these clips is expected to be poor for callsigns + alphanumerics — that's fine for v0; the labeling step (sibling bead) is where ground truth gets fixed. Smoke test: one short clip, assert stt/ output has segments and is JSON-parseable. No accuracy assertions at this layer — that lives in the eval bead.
close_reason: atc audio transcribe landed: lazy mlx_whisper import (works without --extra asr for dry-run/tests), word-timestamped output, idempotent stt/<clip_id>.json gate, --force model swap, --limit/--only/--dry-run flags. New 'asr' optional extra in pyproject.toml (mlx-whisper>=0.4) + mypy override. 12 unit tests + live smoke run on N478ATKLNA1 clip with whisper-tiny (44 segments, word timestamps + avg_logprob captured, JSON round-trips — accuracy bad as expected for tiny on radio audio; that's labelling's job).

title: thought:hypothesis — k bump 8→12 vs 8→16
description: Bumping _DEFAULT_K in lint_utterance from 8 should pull cluster #3 cases (their target § lands at rank 2-4) into the candidate slate. Cite-grounding gate filters ungrounded picks so a wider K can only help. Risk: more candidates → more verdict noise, citation accuracy could regress. Plan: probe k=12 and k=16 via --k CLI flag, pick the higher combined_accuracy, ship by bumping _DEFAULT_K + re-snapshotting baseline. Bead: harness-rwx3.
close_reason: Hypothesis falsified. K-bump produces identical eval results at k=8/12/16 (combined=0.275) because _PROMPT_CANDIDATES=3 is the binding constraint — model only sees top-3 regardless of K. See harness-rwx3 close-out for the structural observation.

title: atc lane F1: fix ppl_vfr_cloud_clearance_above_10k factual error
description: Model answers 'the cloud clearance requirement is not applicable above 10,000 MSL' — factually wrong. Canonical sample vfr_cloud_clearance_above_10k already has the correct answer (1,000/1,000/1 SM + 5 SM vis at >10k MSL under §91.155(a)) but the model isn't imitating it. Options in order of escalation: (1) promote to a constitution rule — 'thresholds STEP UP at 10k MSL, never step off'; (2) add a contrasting negative-example sample that names the 'not applicable' framing as wrong and cites the right answer; (3) add §91.155(a) table as a high-signal episodic seed with the exact table text so retrieval fires hard on cloud-clearance queries. Try (2) first — cheapest and least identity-mutating. Blocked on R3.
notes:
2026-05-01 attempt — both bead options 2 and 3 tried, neither moved the eval case.

Diagnosis: the model's "clear of clouds" frame comes from retrieval, not voice prior.
Top-3 hits for the eval question "VFR cloud clearance Class E above 10,000 MSL":
  1. PCG CONTACT chunk_index=5 (cosine 0.032) — fragment "rspace. The cloud clearance
     requirement for VFR operations is 'clear of clouds.'" begins mid-word ("rspace"
     = "airspace"), confirming chunker page-break truncation. The fragment is from a
     Class B description block.
  2. AIM §3-1-4 (cosine 0.029) — references CFR 91.155(c).
  3. JO 7110.65 §13-2-6 (cosine 0.030) — same "clear of clouds" fragment.

Root cause: pymupdf4llm splits the §91.155(a) full table across a page-break header
("## 14 CFR Ch. I (1-1-25 Edition)"), so the existing chunk_index=0 only contains
the Class A/B/C row. The Class D/E/G rows + the >10,000 MSL row land under what the
section-aware chunker treats as a phantom new section. Same disease bites the PCG
CONTACT entry's class definitions.

Tried option 2 (negative-framing voice sample): NET REGRESSION 18→17, target still
fails. The new sample's keywords ("1,000 feet", "1 statute mile", "5 statute miles")
crowded the retrieval cut for ppl_hemispheric_cruising_altitudes, flipping it to fail.

Tried option 3 (handcurated §91.155(a) table seed at chunk_index=1, then rewritten
to lead with >10k MSL case): both versions scored cosine 0.032 — TIED with the
truncated PCG CONTACT fragment, so default --memories 3 still saw the wrong frame
first. No movement on the eval case (18/22 → 18/22).

Both attempts reverted. Carved out a real circular-import bug found en route
(persona/cite_grounding ↔ persona/rewriter), shipped separately as 9d94276.

Recommended next escalation:
  - Bead option 1 (constitution rule): hard prior in core.yaml that says
    "above 10,000 MSL is the §91.155(a) table case, not 'clear of clouds';
    1,000/1,000/1 SM/5 SM are the values." This bypasses retrieval entirely
    for this category of question. Risk: stamps a topic-specific rule into
    identity, which the constitution mostly avoids.
  - OR upstream chunker fix: detect and strip page-break headers like
    "## 14 CFR Ch. I (1-1-25 Edition)" so adjacent table rows stay attached
    to the parent section. Wider blast radius (touches scripts/atc_chunk.py,
    triggers the retrieval gate), would require re-extract + re-ingest, but
    fixes a class of failures (PCG CONTACT, JO 7110.65 fragments share it).
close_reason:
Root-caused as a chunker bug, not a voice/seed problem. pymupdf4llm wraps per-page running headers as ## level-2 markdown headings (e.g. '## 14 CFR Ch. I (1-1-25 Edition)' between table rows of §91.155(a)), and the section-aware chunker treated those as new section breaks — splitting real sections in half so the parent anchor only carried half the body. PCG entries and JO 7110.65 sections shared the disease.

Fix: scripts/atc_chunk.py — _iter_blocks now detects page-break headings (re-using the existing _NOISE_LINES patterns) and drops them silently, accumulating subsequent body lines into the parent section's buffer.

Result on airton_c full eval: 18/22 (0.8182) → 19/22 (0.8636); ppl_vfr_cloud_clearance_above_10k flipped pass with the verbatim canonical reply ('1,000 feet below, 1,000 feet above, 1 statute mile horizontally; rule §91.155(a)'); zero regressions.

Store rebuild: 9,092 → 11,665 rows (+2,573 recovered chunks across all sources). §91.155 went from 1 chunk → 5 chunks, all anchored. AIM grew most aggressively (795 → 2,717 rows) — most affected by page splits.

Two unit tests added (tests/test_atc_chunk.py): test_iter_blocks_skips_page_break_headings + test_is_page_break_heading_recognizes_running_headers.

Side-effect: airton_c1 retrieval gate baseline re-snapshotted (was stale on main from prior recency-RRF + search_memory k=12 changes — unrelated to this fix; gate would have blocked any push touching scripts/atc_chunk.py until rebaselined). airton_c1 store untouched.

title: [bug] duplicate-call nudge misreads as success after a failed call
description:
Reproduced in live ab session 2026-04-18 while running pre-patch bd_adapter (see commit f4e57ae). Flow:

1. Model emits capture(...) tool call.
2. Tool fails (bd command failed — unrelated: the --add-label vs --labels bug).
3. Model retries with IDENTICAL args.
4. Orchestrator deduplicates → emits ToolResult(success=True, output=_DUPLICATE_CALL_NUDGE).
5. Model reads 'Result is unchanged from the earlier tool message' + success=True and hallucinates 'The task has been captured.'

Root cause: the dedup nudge flags success=True regardless of whether the earlier call succeeded. The model's last tool observation is the failure, but the dedup feedback frames it as a duplicate of a successful prior call.

Proposed fix:

Track the ToolResult of each unique call this turn in seen_calls instead of just the key. On a duplicate, re-emit the stored result (preserving success + output) rather than a fixed nudge. The nudge can still prepend as a suffix: '[duplicate — <prior outcome>]'.

Additional guardrail: when the stored result has success=False, make the dedup result's output quote the error so the model cannot paraphrase the outcome as 'captured' / 'done'.

Lives in src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py around line 545-565. Tests: tests/test_tool_loop.py — add a case where two identical calls where the first fails, then the second dedupes with the failure preserved.

Out of scope for this issue: why the model retried with identical args after a failure (separate bug; likely small-model behavior, investigate later).
close_reason: seen_calls now maps (name,args)→ToolResult; in-round duplicates dedupe silently before the hook (no nudge on first attempt); cross-round duplicates re-issue the prior result preserving success/error.

description: Phase-1 product-gate work for harness-q35t. Cheap-to-test alternative to per-section verb-anchor re-rank. Failed cluster #3 cases often land their correct § at rank 2-4 (within retrieval's reach) but k=8 + the prompt-candidate cap of 3 squeeze them out of the slate the model sees. Bump k default from 8 to 12 (or 16) in lint_utterance — the cite-grounding gate already filters ungrounded picks, so a wider K can only help (more candidates to choose from, no extra fabrication risk). Validate by re-running 'harness eval phraseology --compare-baseline' at k=12 then k=16. Expected lift: cluster #3 cases that lose by 1-3 ranks flip; canonicals unchanged. If verdict accuracy regresses (more candidates = more verdict noise), back off. Out-of-scope: bumping _PROMPT_CANDIDATES from 3 — that has token-budget implications. Should land BEFORE harness-rrnk-style verb-anchor work since k-bump is one-line and the lift signal informs whether re-rank is even needed.
close_reason: Investigated, structural no-op given current pipeline. Bumping _DEFAULT_K from 8 to 12 or 16 produces *identical* eval results because lint_utterance renders only top-_PROMPT_CANDIDATES (=3) into the model prompt — K only widens the cite-grounding anchor set, not what the model sees. Verified empirically (k=8/12/16 all return verdict=0.40 / citation=0.575 / combined=0.275 on 40 cases) and structurally (phraseology_lint.py:223 uses hits[:_PROMPT_CANDIDATES] for the prompt). Cluster #3 failures need a re-rank not a wider slate — pivoting to harness-ptya. Side finding: local baseline reproduces at 11/40 today vs saved 14/40, 3-case retrieval drift on arrival/emergency canonicals, no phraseology code change since baseline-save. Likely chunker output drift (1843 rows post-current-chunker vs prior machine 752 rows).

title: Phraseology lint: per-section verb-anchor re-rank for cluster #3 retrieval misroutes
description: Phase-1 product-gate work for harness-q35t. Cluster #3 failure pattern: short numeric utterances (e.g. 'AMERICAN ONE TWENTY THREE, SQUAWK SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO') retrieve §2-4-17 (Numbers Usage) instead of the section that actually governs them (§10-2-6 Hijack), because the corpus's PHRASEOLOGY example blocks contain similar spelled-form numbers and §2-4-17 has the most numeric content by token count. Query-side rewrites (harness-kure) regressed — both stripping and augmenting hurt. Surgical fix: build a verb-anchor map from section-distinctive verbs/codes to target sections. Examples: SQUAWK → §10-2-6, 7500 → §10-2-6, MAYDAY → §10-1-1, REDUCE SPEED → §5-7-2, MAINTAIN (... KNOTS) → §5-7-2, CONTACT → §2-1-17, LINE UP AND WAIT → §3-9-4, CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF → §3-9-10, CLEARED TO LAND → §3-10-5, LOW ALTITUDE ALERT → §2-1-6, TRAFFIC ALERT → §2-1-6, TRAFFIC, (clock position) → §2-1-21. Implementation: (a) author character/airton_c1/corpus/verb_anchors.yaml (section → list of distinctive verbs/code phrases). (b) Modify lint_utterance to detect verb-anchor matches in the utterance and boost matching sections in the candidate slate (e.g. add a virtual hit at rank 0 for the matched §, OR re-rank the existing hits by verb-overlap score). (c) Cite-grounding gate still filters ungrounded picks. (d) Validate by re-running 'harness eval phraseology --compare-baseline'. Expected lift: cluster #3 cases (han_speed_*, emerg_hijack_*, han_contact_*) flip from §2-4-17 to correct §; canonical cases unchanged because their verb-anchors are already grounded by retrieval. Out-of-scope: ingest-side synonym maps (precision risk per harness-ajn discipline).
close_reason: Shipped two-stage verb-anchor pipeline in src/harness/tools/phraseology_lint.py + character/airton_c1/corpus/verb_anchors.yaml (commit 328427e). Stage 1 virtual-hit injection (text-mode FTS5 probe on missing §) + stage 2 stable-partition rerank (matched-§ hits to front). 9 sections anchored: §10-2-6 (SQUAWK 7500), §10-1-1 (DECLARE EMERGENCY), §5-7-2 (REDUCE/INCREASE SPEED), §2-1-17 (CONTACT), §2-1-6 (LOW ALT/TRAFFIC ALERT), §2-1-21 (TRAFFIC), §3-9-4 (LINE UP AND WAIT), §3-9-10 (CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF), §3-10-5 (CLEARED TO LAND). Eval lift: 11/40→13/40 (+5pp combined, +15pp citation, flat verdict, 0 regressions). Cluster #3 retrieval lift confirmed — speed cases now hit §5-7-2, traffic-advisory hits §2-1-21. 30 tests green (13 new). Pre-push gate re-snapshotted to 13/40 (corpus-state drift accounts for 1-case gap vs prior machine's 14/40 saved baseline; ptya recovers the rest). Residual hijack-case failures are downstream of ptya: §10-2-6 IS at rank 0 in the prompt's top-3 (verified via debug print), but the 7B Qwen still picks §2-4-17 because §2-4-17 chunks have stronger 'SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO' example overlap. That's a model-side limit reachable via (a) 32B swap (already supported via --model-repo), (b) chunk enrichment that makes §10-2-6 PHRASEOLOGY blocks more lexically sticky, or (c) explicit prompt-side hierarchy of 'directive verb governs section'. File separately when prioritized.

title: Phraseology lint: strip phonetic digit-words from retrieval query (cluster #3 retrieval misroutes)
description: Phase-1 product-gate work for harness-q35t. Baseline post-rubric-fix (kl0w) sits at 14/40 = 35% combined; ~45pp shy of the 80% gate. Failure cluster #3 dominates the residual: short utterances with phonetic-spelled numeric tokens overwhelm hybrid retrieval and pull wrong sections. Examples: 'SQUAWK SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO' retrieves §2-4-17 (Numbers Usage) instead of §10-2-6 (Hijack); 'REDUCE SPEED TO TWO FIVE ZERO' retrieves §2-4-17 instead of §5-7-2 (Speed Adjustment); 'CONTACT DEPARTURE ONE TWO THREE POINT FOUR' loses §2-1-17 to numeric-token chapter. Fix: in src/harness/tools/phraseology_lint.py::lint_utterance, preprocess the retrieval query (NOT the user message shown to the model) by stripping standalone phonetic digit words (ZERO, ONE, ..., NINE, NINER, TEN, ELEVEN, ..., NINETY, HUNDRED, THOUSAND, POINT). The model still sees the original utterance for classification; only retrieval gets the cleaned query. Hypothesis: 'AMERICAN ONE TWENTY THREE, SQUAWK SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO' → 'AMERICAN, SQUAWK' lets §10-2-6 win the candidate set. Validate by re-running 'harness eval phraseology --compare-baseline' and snapshotting a new baseline if combined accuracy lifts.
close_reason: Investigated, both query-side mods regressed combined accuracy below the 35% baseline; reverted. Approach 1 (strip phonetic-digit tokens from retrieval query): -5pp combined (35→30%). Hijack/squawk cluster won (9 case improvements including emerg_hijack_verify_canonical, emerg_hijack_wrong_code, emerg_traffic_advisory_canonical) but 9 canonical landing/handoff cases regressed (arr_landing_canonical, arr_pilot_oos, han_pilot_freq_oos etc.) — stripping was too aggressive on cases where retrieval was already working. Hypothesis: short stripped queries (e.g. 'RUNWAY CLEARED TO LAND') give BM25/dense too little signal vs originals that match the corpus's spelled-form examples. Approach 2 (augment: original + stripped concatenated): -7.5pp combined (35→27.5%). Citation accuracy actually rose +2.5pp but verdict crashed -12.5pp — the model saw different candidates from the merged retrieval and verdicts shifted. Both reverted. Working theory for cluster #3: the corpus's PHRASEOLOGY blocks contain spelled-form examples that match short utterances on dense embedding; the §2-4-17 (Numbers Usage) chapter wins on TOTAL token volume of phonetic digits not because it's semantically right but because it has the most numeric content. Future angles to try (NOT this bead): (a) per-section synonym/anchor map keyed to short utterance verbs ('SQUAWK' → §10-2-6, '7500' → §10-2-6 hijack, etc.); (b) k bump from 8 to 12-16 with cite-grounding gate filtering; (c) two-stage retrieval: hybrid pull top-K, then re-rank by section-specific keyword overlap with the utterance's verb-class. Documented in character/airton_c1/phraseology_progress.md.

title: Banter detection + ATC joke deflection (epic)
description:
Detect smartass/empty/meta prompts (e.g. 'this page intentionally left blank', 'test', 'ping') and respond with an ATC/aviation joke from a curated corpus instead of fabricating rule content.

Cycle: joke → 3 redirects → joke → 3 redirects… Tracks banter_streak per session.

Children:
- A: jokes.yaml schema + 20 hand-written entries (voice-aligned)
- B: BanterCatcher hook in orchestrator/hooks.py (bail phase)
- C: router 'banter' intent + router_eval.yaml fixtures
- D: session-state streak tracker (1-joke-then-3-redirects cycle)

Why: Run 12 lesson — model fabricates JO 7110.65 content from low-signal prompts because retrieval always returns *something*. Banter path short-circuits before model round, preserves persona, gives user a laugh instead of hallucinated §.
close_reason: Epic complete. A (xw2m) jokes corpus 8a8358b, B (jmts) banter lib 81d34b5, C (q7ff) router intent d48b9dc, D (vadq) intercept a161212. Smartass / empty-signal prompts (this page intentionally left blank, test, ping, etc.) deflect with an ATC joke from a 20-entry corpus, then 3 escalating redirects, then another joke. Real prompts reset the cycle. End-to-end on classic REPL with --tools + airton_c1 (jokes.yaml present). TUI + no-tools-path wiring deferred as follow-ups if needed.

title: Banter B: BanterCatcher hook (bail phase) + tests
description:
Detection module + corpus loader + redirect ladder for the BanterCatcher epic (harness-jjm9). Lives at src/harness/persona/banter.py — neighbor of cite_grounding.py.

Provides the primitives that router intent (C: harness-q7ff) and streak tracker (D: harness-vadq) both consume:

- is_banter_prompt(prompt, *, prior_prompt) -> bool — fires on:
  - explicit meta patterns: blank-page, test, ping, are-you-there, lorem ipsum, repeat-char
  - empty / whitespace-only
  - <8 tokens AND zero domain anchors AND not a greeting
  - exact repeat of prior prompt
- BanterCorpus.load(yaml_path) + BanterCorpus.pick(seen, *, rng) -> JokeEntry
  - reshuffles when corpus exhausted (no immediate repeats)
- REDIRECT_LADDER: tuple[str, ...] — three-tier ladder used by D after a joke fires

Tests in tests/test_banter.py cover detector positives + negatives, corpus load + pick + reshuffle, ladder constants.

Original bead said 'bail phase'; revised — bail phase can only Continue/Nudge/Truncated (can't replace reply). Actual integration point is router intent (C) + a tool_loop pre-model intercept (D's wiring). This bead ships the lib; C and D consume it.
notes: Reasoning rejected: bail-phase hook (can't replace reply), finalize-phase Halt hook (wastes model rounds before firing). Pre-model intercept in tool_loop is correct architectural placement; streak state lives on session and gets plumbed through D.
close_reason: banter.py (detector + BanterCorpus + REDIRECT_LADDER) + 55 tests committed in 81d34b5; lib ready for router C (q7ff) and streak tracker D (vadq). Pipeline-hook framing dropped — pre-model intercept is correct placement, owned by D.

title: Chat /clear and /reset slash commands (REPL + TUI)
description:
Add in-chat context controls so the user can drop history without exiting.

Commands:
- /clear — soft clear. Model-visible history for this turn onward becomes empty (plus system prompt + retrieval). Transcript rows stay on disk for audit. Also drops the latest compaction summary pointer for this session so the next turn isn't anchored to a summary of now-cleared context. Print confirmation with row count preserved.
- /reset [NEW_SESSION] — hard clear. Switch session id mid-chat. If NEW_SESSION omitted, generate '<old>-<timestamp>'. Transcript for old session untouched; new session starts empty. Router/compaction state reset.

Scope:
- Classic REPL (src/harness/cli.py): handle alongside existing _EXIT_COMMANDS / _EDIT_COMMANDS.
- TUI (src/harness/tui/chat_app.py): handle in the same slash dispatcher as /exit.
- Print one-liner help when user types /help listing /clear /reset /edit /exit.

Implementation notes:
- Soft clear likely needs a 'history floor' concept: remember the turn_id at clear time; _load_history filters to rows after the floor. Cheaper than deleting rows.
- Consider persisting the floor in a small clears table so /clear survives process restart when reusing --session.
- Tests: new clears-table round-trip, REPL + TUI dispatch, ctx meter reflects cleared state, retrieval still works post-clear.

Why: current escape hatch is 'exit, restart with a new --session name'. Friction breaks the flow mid-conversation. User asked for this 2026-04-18.
close_reason: Classic REPL: /reset aliases /clear (mid-loop session-id swap deferred — /exit + restart with --session is the path). /help / /? prints discoverable command list. TUI: /reset aliases /session-reset; /help / /? prints the SlashPalette list. Tests pin command sets + help banner contents.

title: airton_c1 retrieval Fix C: small-model query expansion pre-retrieval
description: Biggest generalizable fix under epic harness-rhto. Add a pre-retrieval rewrite pass: small model (same as router, probably Qwen 2.5 1.5B or similar) takes user question + corpus context hint (e.g. 'FAA JO 7110.65 air traffic control') and emits 3–5 doc-style keyword rewrites. Hybrid search runs on (user_query + rewrites) union, RRF fuses. Integration point: src/harness/retrieval/ — new QueryExpander protocol, wired into the episodic/semantic search path in the chat loop (cli.py) with --expand-queries flag (default-off initially, default-on for airton_c1 via character config). Example: 'shortest distance next to aircraft on approach' → ['minimum same runway separation', 'wake turbulence separation', 'landing behind category', 'arrival spacing minima']. Prompt template stored in character/<name>/retrieval_prompts/query_expansion.md so per-character tuning stays in config. Eval: atc_eval.yaml recall@5 before/after + new regression cases from 2026-04-24 session + latency cost measurement (adds ~1 small-model call per turn pre-retrieval). Gate: recall lift ≥ +15% on atc_eval, latency add ≤ 200ms p50. Depends on Fix B ship order (measure B's contribution first so we can attribute C's lift cleanly). 1–2 day estimate.

Net recall is mixed — some lay-phrasing cases climb (rbn_mh 1→0, aircraft_to_aircraft 6→4) but wake_turb_concern_lay drops out of top-10 entirely (8→none). Default stays --no-llm-expand. Code lives in src/harness/retrieval/query_expander.py LLMQueryExpander class + eval flag --llm-expand for opt-in re-measurement after a bigger / domain-tuned model lands (likely under Fix D harness-pw9z). title: atc lane V3: voice sample for AIM 4-4-8 VFR-on-top
description: Fixes ifr_vfr_on_top cite miss. Follows the harness-e73 AIM-paragraph pattern (same template as readback_expected_items, wake_turbulence_avoidance_takeoff, clearance_limit_*). Prompt along 'What's VFR-on-top and when can I request it?', gold cites AIM 4-4-8 in opening sentence, covers: IFR-rated pilot, in VMC only, must comply with VFR cloud-clearance and visibility + VFR cruising altitudes, ATC approval required. Verify retriever rank-1 before merge. Blocked on R3.
notes:
2026-05-01 attempt — same voice-corpus-capacity ceiling that closed harness-wkom v2. Tried twice; reverted both.

Voice-retriever shape: top_k=6 default. With 9 canonical samples pre-attempt, the cut is 6 of 9. Adding a 10th sample puts one previously-included sample below the cut for every query, even when the new sample is rank-1 for its target.

Attempt 1 — full-bodied gold (8 lines, citations: AIM 4-4-8 + §91.159 + §91.155 + §91.157):
  Voice-retrieval rank for target query: rank 1, cosine 1.000 (exact prompt match).
  Eval delta: 19/22 → 18/22.
    + ifr_vfr_on_top: False → True (target — passes citation 4-4-8, full substance)
    - ppl_class_b_entry_requirements: True → False (model dropped 14 CFR §91.131
      and Mode C/ADS-B keywords; substituted irrelevant cites: JO 7110.65 §2-1-18,
      AIM 4-4-7).
    - ppl_readback_basics: True → False ("readback" → "read back" morphology
      mismatch on a brittle keyword; substance fine, citation 4-4-7 still hits).

Attempt 2 — tightened gold (5 lines, same citations):
  Eval delta: same 19/22 → 18/22, different shape.
    + ifr_vfr_on_top: still passes
    - ppl_class_b_entry_requirements: still loses §91.131 (no CFR cite at all this
      time; reply shrunk to 4 generic bullets — "altitude, route, instructions").
    - ppl_readback_basics: now cites 4-4-7 correctly but model imitates the new
      sample's brevity — collapses 5 readback categories down to a single hold-
      short bullet. Misses 'altitude' keyword which the original full reply hit.

Diagnosis: parent epic harness-7wju is the right home — its open premise is exactly
this voice-corpus capacity problem ("at 12 samples, neither top_k=6 nor top_k=8
yields a strict superset of prior passes"). harness-ecdu can't ship cleanly until
that epic provides structural relief (e.g. OutOfScopeHook to keep cite-bleed off
unrelated cases, lane F-prime auto-replace to fix wrong-section cites, or a
voice-retriever k bump tuned per character).

Recommended: leave harness-ecdu open, hang it under harness-7wju as a child,
revisit after one of harness-1ebs / harness-8dop / harness-zsbz (the Phase-1.6
structural fixes) lands.

Side discovery: 'readback' keyword spec is brittle to 'read back' morphology —
should be relaxed to a regex or alternation in atc_eval.yaml. Filed mentally,
not worth a separate bead unless this bites a third time.
