title: hybrid RRF: BM25 hits land below cosine floor → topical bleed
description: store/_hybrid.py fuses BM25 (FTS5) + dense cosine via reciprocal-rank fusion. RRF preserves rank order regardless of absolute similarity, so a BM25 lexical hit on a repeated word ('junior', 'stack') can rank an old, semantically-unrelated row into the top-K even when its dense cosine is well below the configured min_score. Result: stale memory leaks into queries that share only surface tokens. Investigate: (a) apply min_score floor on the fused score (not just dense); (b) require BM25 hits to also clear a soft cosine threshold; (c) document the trade-off and gate via --memories-threshold semantics. Reproduce: search 'junior' against the local episodic store and inspect what comes back at score >0.5 vs raw cosine.
close_reason: Added bm25_min_score gate to EpisodicStore.search + SemanticStore.search hybrid path. Default = max(min_score - 0.15, 0.0). Soft floor lets identifier queries keep working; common-word lexical bleed gets cut. 5 new tests via steerable axis-token embedder.

title: Fabrication catcher gaps: bare 'Captured.' + fake bead-id + bare 'Updated.'
description:
User saw airton_b fabricate: 'Captured. Scope: personal. Outcome: ... Bead id: harness-abc123..' and earlier 'Missed ... Updated. Rerun /plan.' — both with no tool call this turn.

Gaps:
1. _FABRICATED_AB_CAPTURE_RE anchors on '^Captured:' (colon). Fabrication used 'Captured.' (period). Miss.
2. No catcher for fake bead-ids in free text. Real ids only appear in tool-result messages; model emitting 'Bead id: harness-xxx' inline is always fabrication.
3. _FALSE_SUCCESS_RE misses bare single-word claims ('Updated.', 'Captured.', 'Created.' at line start).

Fix:
- Broaden _FABRICATED_AB_CAPTURE_RE: match 'Captured' at line start followed by period/colon/em-dash AND proximity to receipt-shape keywords (Scope/Outcome/Bead id) so we don't false-positive on wrap-ups that summarize a real capture.
- Add _FABRICATED_BEAD_ID_RE matching 'Bead id:\s*harness-[a-z0-9]+' (or similar). Triggered in fabrication bucket when no tool ran.
- Add bare-claim line variant to false-success: '^(?:Updated|Captured|Created|Deleted|Removed)\.\s*$'.

Tests: positive cases from the observed session (captured.period, fake-id, bare Updated line). Negative: real CaptureTool output ('Captured harness-xxx — [personal] task...') must NOT match.
close_reason: Shipped. Broadened capture regex, added bead-id + bare-claim catchers, 5 new tests.

title: Tool-loop failure corpus + per-catcher attribution eval
description:
## Why

tool_loop.py is 731 lines with a growing stack of hallucination catchers (fabricated tool-call success, fabricated search results, bare tool-intent, quoted-snippet numbered lists, paired meta-confirm, ab Remembered-receipts, period-Captured, fake bead-ids, bail_retry, fabrication-exhaustion fallback). Recent commits (bec4578, 162b41d, 828effc, 34f34cf) keep adding patches. No eval pins which catcher saves which class of failure, so we cannot tell pruning-safe layers from load-bearing ones, and cannot compare a rearchitect against the current stack.

Existing benches (bench_tool_use, bench_router) measure throughput, not fabrication correctness. Router eval exists (character/<name>/router_eval.yaml) and is the template to copy.

## What

1. Capture a failure corpus from real session transcripts + the known hallucination shapes each catcher was added for. Fixture file: character/airton/tool_loop_eval.yaml. Each scenario:
   - messages: input turn(s)
   - tool_set / router mode / model (small + main, both mockable via echo-adapter scripted replies)
   - expected: final reply must/must-not contain, must-not claim tool success, must-not emit fake bead-id, etc.
   - label: which catcher class it stresses (e.g. "fabricated-remembered-receipt")

2. New command: `uv run harness eval tool-loop [--json]` scoring pass/fail per scenario with the label grouping so we see per-catcher coverage.

3. Attribution harness: run the fixture with each catcher individually disabled (env flag or param) and record the pass-rate delta. Output a table: catcher → scenarios it uniquely saves → scenarios where it is redundant with another catcher.

4. Commit the baseline numbers in the eval output so any rearchitect PR has a concrete target.

## Out of scope

- Actually rewriting the orchestrator. This task produces the measurement rig only.
- Adding new catchers. Document-and-measure, do not patch.

## Done when

title: airton_c1 OutOfScopeHook: cosine-floor scope gate
description: Phase-1.6 child of harness-7wju. New hook in orchestrator/hooks.py 'bail' phase: after search_memory tool returns, if max(top_k_cosine) < scope_floor (suggest 0.10 for JO 7110.65 corpus; calibrate against retrieval baseline), emit scope-redirect template instead of letting the model draft a fabricated cite. Motivating failure (2026-04-27 chat session, mark): 'True or False: A nose-high pitch attitude is a good indicator of a steep flightpath of the lead aircraft?' Question is pilot-side wake-turbulence material (AC 90-23 / AIM 7-3) — JO 7110.65 corpus has zero 'nose' lexical matches. Retrieval returned §14-3-3 (Oceanic CPDLC ABNORMAL CONDITIONS, glossary chunk) at cosine 0.031 — corpus noise floor is ~0.016 per harness-11ha empirical data. Model latched onto §14-3-3 and fabricated a procedural answer twice (UngroundedCitationHook fired once for missing_citation but retry kept the bogus anchor). Constitution + core.yaml both prescribe scope-redirect: 'That's a pilot-side question — airton_c is the generalist. JO 7110.65 doesn't cover it.' Acceptance: (a) hook fires on the nose-high question and emits scope-redirect template; (b) does NOT fire on any of the 26 currently-passing eval atc cases (top hits there are 0.4-0.7 cosine, well above floor); (c) calibration script samples N=200 random JO 7110.65 chunks as queries to confirm in-scope cosine distribution is well-separated from the 0.016 noise floor; (d) flag --scope-gate on eval atc to A/B vs no-gate; (e) per-corpus floor configurable via core.yaml scope_cosine_floor field (airton_c1: 0.10; default off for airton/airton_b). Pairs with harness-NEW-RETRY for defense-in-depth: scope gate is the cheap preempt, retry-tier grounding is the safety net.
notes:
2026-05-01 — scaffolding shipped, classifier underperforms.

Architecture (commit forthcoming):
  - RouterIntent gets `scope: "in" | "out" | "unsure"` (default "unsure").
  - Both ModelRouter + GrammarRouter take `persona_scope_hint`; prompts get a scope-classification block when set.
  - GrammarRouter schema: `scope` enum is unconditionally required; characters without a hint return "unsure" for every turn.
  - tool_loop.run() classifies once at the top; on `scope=out` AND character.scope_redirect_template set, returns ToolLoopResult(content=template, rounds=0). Skip the model entirely.
  - Character gets `scope_hint` + `scope_redirect_template`. airton_c1's core.yaml ships both.
  - eval router scores scope_accuracy alongside tool_accuracy; new `expected_scope` field on fixture rows; 14 scope rows added to airton_c1/router_eval.yaml.
  - Tests: 11 new (parser, prompt, orchestrator short-circuit, fixture loader, scoring).

Live measurement on airton_c1 router_eval (Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit, grammar mode):
  - tool_accuracy: 0.400 (artifact: many new scope rows have expected_tool=null, but Hermes routes them anyway; tool selection is irrelevant for scope=out rows since orchestrator short-circuits).
  - scope_accuracy: 0.214 (3/14):
      IN cases  (5): 1 correct, 4 → unsure
      OUT cases (7): 0 correct, 5 → unsure, 2 → in
      UNSURE    (2): 2 correct
  - Tried two prompt iterations (full guidance vs tighter guidance with explicit "use unsure sparingly"). Same 3/14 outcome both runs.

Critical positive: ZERO false-`out` verdicts on real in-scope rows. Hermes underclassifies as `unsure` (fall-through, no harm) but never falsely blocks legitimate questions. Architecture is fail-safe by design — only confident `out` triggers the redirect, and Hermes never produces false confident-out.

Diagnosis: Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit's discriminative power is the limit, not the prompt. On this corpus where pilot/controller language overlaps heavily ("wake turbulence" appears in both controller separation and pilot avoidance contexts), a 3B-4bit model can't reliably split the two.

Possible next steps (don't pick yet):
  (1) Larger router — bench Qwen2.5-3B / Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct unquantized vs Hermes 3B.
  (2) Use the main model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit) for scope at the cost of latency.
  (3) Two-pass classifier: separate Hermes call dedicated to scope, isolated from tool routing.
  (4) Lexical fallback layered onto Hermes: cue-verb heuristic ("can I", "may I", "do I need") as an out-signal that votes alongside Hermes's verdict.
  (5) Accept the underclassification — gate is fail-safe today; revisit when a better small router lands.

Bead stays open as deferred until one of (1)-(4) is picked. Architecture work is done; this becomes a classifier-tuning problem, not an orchestrator problem.

description: Phase-1.6 child of harness-7wju. Lane F-prime detect-only shipped under harness-11ha (Run 12, 2026-04-26). Module src/harness/persona/cite_grounding.py + --cite-ground flag on eval atc. Detection works: 2/2 real wrong-cite fabs caught (controller_same_runway_arrival_lay_time §3-10-4, controller_hijack_squawk §10-2-5 → suggested §10-2-6 exact). But 3 false positives on voice-sample-anchored lay variants (wake_turb_lay §2-1-19, missed_approach_lay §5-10-11, handoff_lay §5-4-5). FP budget too high to auto-replace as a hard filter. This bead tracks the actuator design: how to auto-replace ungrounded cites without nuking the voice-sample-carried lay-variant cases. Candidate strategies: (1) voice-anchored evidence weighting — skip rank check when cited section appears in any canonical voice sample's gold AND the user query is cosine-similar to that sample's prompt (not just the gold's anchor); (2) cosine sanity check on (question, cited_section_principle) — if absolute cosine high enough, override the rank check; (3) per-section-class threshold (lay vs jargon queries get different K); (4) re-roll with nudge ('§X-Y-Z is about T — does that match the question?') instead of silent replace. Decision criterion: Phase-1.6 auto-replace must keep all 26 currently-passing cases passing AND flip ≥1 of the 2 caught fabs. Acceptance: eval atc ≥27/29 = 93.1% with --cite-ground --replace, no regressions vs detect-only run.

title: airton_c1 retrieval lay-term→doc-term gap remediation
description: Session 2026-04-24 surfaced a retrieval failure distinct from Fix A (harness-8zx6). User asked 'What is the shortest distance than an aircraft is allowed to be next to another aircraft on approach to the runway?'. Authoritative §3-10-3 chunk (id 759) contains the answer (Cat I behind Cat I/II = 3,000 ft; Cat II = 4,500 ft; Cat III = 6,000 ft) but retrieval missed it entirely: dense BGE-small cosine ~0.016 (noise floor, well below min_score=0.5), FTS5 BM25 OR-expanded didn't rank 759 in top-15 (frequent tokens 'aircraft/runway/approach' dilute), hybrid RRF of both also missed. Root cause: user's lay phrasing ('shortest', 'next to', 'on approach') has zero lexical overlap with doc phrasing ('minimum distance', 'landing behind', 'same runway separation', 'Category I'); BGE-small doesn't bridge the register gap. Proof: if BM25 query augmented with 'Same OR Separation OR Arrival', chunk 759 jumps to #1. Model fell back to parametric → fabricated 1,000 ft / 2,000 ft. Epic tracks three remediations: (A) synonym enrichment in chunk principle [cheapest probe]; (B) small-model query expansion pre-retrieval [biggest generalizable fix]; (C) domain-tuned embedder swap [biggest lift, benchmark-gated]. Ship order A → B → C; stop early if earlier fix covers the regression.
notes:
Children: harness-7ph5 (Fix B, synonym enrichment), harness-hvu1 (Fix C, query expansion), harness-pw9z (Fix D, embedder swap). Ship order B → C → D with early-stop if earlier fix closes the regression gap. Sequential deps wired: C blocked by B, D blocked by C.

title: [epic] ab (airton_b) persona — personal operations lead v1
description:
Second persona in the harness: personal operations lead. Wraps bd as data plane; ab is the experience plane.

Spec locked via interactive walkthrough 2026-04-18. See docs/persona-interview.md for the template used.

Core shape:
- Identity: pronoun 'it', first-person 'I', transparent software, operations steward (not mentor, not executor). Aliases: ayrton, A, AB, ab.
- Scope: professional + personal (social deferred). Scope as bd label (scope:professional / scope:personal).
- Custom bd types: project, event, habit (bd's built-in task retained for leaf work).
- Core deliverable: /plan — tiered daily path (Shall / Should / Shmaybe / Watching) with reason on every line.
- Capture: conversational, until-resolved. Required fields: scope, parent_project, outcome, next_action, deadline.
- Memory: fully separate silo from Airton. Per-character DB at ~/Library/Application Support/harness/airton_b/memory/. bd DB isolated too at ~/Library/Application Support/harness/airton_b/beads.db via HARNESS_AB_BD_DB.
- Voice: caveman-lite default via CavemanRewriter (prompt-based). Auto-clarity relaxes to normal prose on destructive confirms, multi-step misread risk, user asks to clarify, error/retraction.
- Learning: (a) outcome feedback + (c) policy memory ship with v1; (b) style mirroring is phase 2.
- Re-plan trigger: all (manual + auto on new Shall + auto on deadline slip), always with one-line notice.

Integration architecture: ab-as-shell-over-bd. Every item operation dispatches through src/harness/store/bd_adapter.py to isolated bd DB. ab's episodic + semantic stores hold retros and ab-specific reflections; bd holds all task/project/event data + operating-style policy memory via bd remember.

v1 build (to be decomposed into child tasks):
1. Core character files: core.yaml, constitution.md, register_map.yaml, seed_memories/ (5 files), router_eval.yaml.
2. Voice corpus: 26 canonical gold samples covering plan outputs, capture dialogues, re-plan notices, drift nudges, status rollups, ambiguous-ask clarifiers, auto-clarity cases, retractions, register stress tests. Every taboo hits ≥1 fixture.
3. CavemanRewriter class: src/harness/persona/caveman_rewriter.py. Prompt-based rewrite pass on base adapter. Config: HARNESS_AB_REGISTER (lite/full/ultra), HARNESS_AB_REWRITE_ON_TOOLS (default false). Per-surface intensity map. Auto-clarity bypass.
4. bd_adapter: src/harness/store/bd_adapter.py. All bd subprocess calls route through adapter with --db pinned to HARNESS_AB_BD_DB. Registers custom types project/event/habit on first run. Applies scope label on every create.
5. Tool set: src/harness/tools/{plan,capture,status,drift,retro,reprioritize,close,defer}.py. All dispatch through bd_adapter. /plan computes tier + reasons (derived from priority, deadline, blockers-others, policy memory); never stored. /capture drives until-resolved dialogue. /retro reads bd history, writes to ab episodic + bd memories.
6. Per-character memory DB migration: src/harness/store/ path resolution by character name. Airton stays at default path; ab gets its own DB. Tests cover both paths, no cross-contamination.
7. CLI wiring: --character airton_b path through cli.py. /register runtime override. Integration tests: capture → bd create → /plan → tier output, /retro cycle.

title: Numeric quote-or-abstain fabrication catcher for tabular tool output
description:
When retrieval surfaces a section whose body contains a numeric table (pipe-rows, `|CL|Under 25|15|` shape) but SearchMemoryTool's 400-char body cap cuts the snippet before those rows, the model reconstructs missing rows from parametric priors and confidently emits wrong numbers with a correct citation.

Reproducer (session 2026-04-24, airton_c1):
  Q: 'What is the usable distance for an MH class RBN?'
  Reply: cited §4-1-1 TBL 4-1-2 correctly, wrote CL=15, MH=50 (WRONG), H=50, HH=75.
  Truth: MH = 25 miles (the model collapsed MH into the H row's value).
  Retrieval was NOT the bug — §4-1-1 chunk_0 ranked #0 at 0.033.
  Root cause: chunk_0's 400-char body preview is consumed by prologue +
  REFERENCE block, never reaches TBL 4-1-2's CL/MH rows; chunk_1 begins
  at the H/HH tail. So no retrieved snippet ever contained the MH row,
  but the section header + partial table was enough for the model to
  fabricate a plausible-looking complete table.

Regression fixture: character/airton_c1/atc_eval.yaml case
  id=controller_rbn_mh_usable_distance keys on '25 miles' and will fail
  the full-stack eval on any reply that re-hallucinates.

Catcher design sketch (complements UngroundedCitationHook, which fires
on fabricated §N-N-N anchors; this fires on fabricated numeric values
inside a cited section):
  - phase: bail (like other fabrication catchers)
  - pre-condition: reply contains BOTH a section citation AND a numeric
    table (pipe-row regex or a line with >=2 numbers + units like
    miles/feet/NM/watts)
  - check: every numeric value in the reply's table must appear
    verbatim in at least one tool result body (SearchMemory tool output
    from this turn). Values absent from tool output = fabrication.
  - bail action: canned refusal 'I can't quote that table from memory
    without fabricating rows. Let me search for the specific row.'
    + force a re-search with a more targeted query.

Two complementary fixes worth considering alongside the catcher:
  1. SearchMemoryTool: bump the 400-char body cap, OR when a chunk
     contains a table, bias the snippet window toward the table rows
     (not the prologue).
  2. Chunker: TBL 4-1-2's CL/MH/H/HH rows were split between chunk_0
     and chunk_1 at an awkward boundary. The harness-1s4 chunker-fold
     work folded NOTE/PHRASEOLOGY into parents; extend to ensure no
     numeric table is split across chunk boundaries.

Either (1) or (2) alone would have prevented THIS incident without a
catcher. The catcher is defense-in-depth for the general class of
'citation-real, table-fabricated' failures.

Acceptance:
  - new catcher class in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py with unit
    tests covering positive (MH RBN repro) and negative (small truthful
    tables, non-tabular replies) cases
  - controller_rbn_mh_usable_distance full-stack eval passes
  - attribution eval shows the catcher as the one that fires (not a
    generic FabricationFallback)
close_reason: Landed across 3 commits (7c94de6, 79f355f, 3145126): regression fixture in atc_eval.yaml, SearchMemoryTool body cap 400->1200, TableFabricationHook (pipe-table shape), NumericFabricationHook (prose-form cross-row), and airton_c1 quote-or-abstain constitution rule. Verified fix live: MH RBN now returns 25 miles with full correct TBL 4-1-2. 1,220 tests passing; pushed to origin/main.

title: airton_c1: query-side synonym expansion from synonyms.yaml
description:
character/airton_c1/corpus/synonyms.yaml currently enriches at INGEST time (scripts/atc_ingest.py::principle_for appends '[synonyms: term1, term2]' to the principle text before embed). Ingest-side works but is asymmetric — query tokens still need to match the augmented corpus tokens literally.

Add query-side expansion: before search_memory runs (or at the store.search() boundary), detect section-anchored lay terms in the user's query and expand them with their jargon equivalents from synonyms.yaml. Concretely: query 'shortest distance next to another aircraft on approach' → expanded to include 'same runway separation arrival minima 5-5-5.' The expanded terms go into BOTH the dense embed (the query vector now covers jargon space) and the BM25 tokens (FTS5 MATCH picks up exact jargon hits).

Implementation sketch:
- Load synonyms.yaml once at store init; build an inverted index from lay-term → section-anchored jargon.
- Query expansion: tokenize query, find lay-term hits, append their jargon equivalents as a second query chunk.
- For dense: embed 'original_query || expanded_terms' (or embed both separately and average — measure).
- For BM25: append expanded terms as additional OR-matched tokens.

Guard against over-expansion: synonyms.yaml entries are section-specific, so a lay term matched in the query should only inject jargon from ONE section, not bleed across. The current file already enforces this via per-section keying.

Followup: symmetric enrichment (apply same expansion at ingest AND query) may compose well with the already-landed ingest-side work. Measure before keeping both.

Expected lift: biggest for lay-language queries where the section's key noun phrase isn't in the user's vocabulary — the exact case that motivated synonyms.yaml originally (Fix-B, harness-7ph5).
close_reason: Query-side synonym expansion shipped — src/harness/retrieval/query_expander.py + SearchMemoryTool wiring + eval CLI flag. Content-token-subset matching (rather than substring) matches real-chat paraphrases: lay term 'shortest distance on approach' now triggers on fixture query 'what is the shortest distance an aircraft is allowed to be next to another aircraft on approach to the runway.' Split synonyms.yaml into shared + query-only files to prevent the expander's lay-paraphrase entries from diluting ingest-side precision on jargon queries — measured regression on jargon 'when do wake turbulence procedures apply' (rank 0 → 9) when the new entries landed ingest-side; reverted via the split. Final retrieval deltas: recall@1 76.5% → 82.4%, recall@3 88.2% → 94.1%, recall@10 94.1% → 100% (no hard misses). 27 expander tests + baseline refresh. All gates green (1205 passed).

title: Enable FTS5 porter stemming for episodic/semantic stores
description:
FTS5 uses default unicode61 tokenizer — no stemming. Query 'declare' fails to match stored 'declared' in BM25. Concretely: §10-2-5 (EMERGENCY SITUATIONS) says 'An emergency is declared by: pilot, facility personnel, officials...' — the exact answer to 'who may declare an emergency.' Dense ranks it #2 (cosine 0.77). BM25 drops it out of top-5 because 'declare' != 'declared'. Hybrid RRF fusion (equal-weight) drags the fused rank down to #4.

Expanding the query to include both tenses ('who may declare or declared an emergency') moves §10-2-5 to rank 2 in hybrid. Stemming would do this structurally.

Fix: change FTS5 virtual-table declaration to 'tokenize = porter unicode61'. Affects both episodic + semantic FTS5 sidecars. Requires FTS5 rebuild (DROP + CREATE + re-populate) on next migration; existing rows stay, just re-indexed.

Trade-off: porter stemming can over-merge (e.g. 'operate' and 'operator' become same stem), which may hurt precision on identifier-heavy queries (the original reason RRF fusion was picked). But JO 7110.65 queries are lay-language dominated, so stemming helps far more than it hurts. Worth benchmarking on the atc_eval.yaml fixture after the change.

title: airton_c1: force search_memory tool call on every turn
description:
Retrieval for airton_c1 scores ~0.016 on lay-language queries (embedder ceiling + corpus-style mismatch). Below the 0.5 floor → no passive memory block attached → model fabricates + context-bleeds. Fix A (parent_section_title) and Fix B (lay-term synonyms) chip at cosine but haven't moved it out of the 0.0x range for generic queries.

Force a search_memory tool call on every user turn for airton_c1. Mechanism:
1. Add require_search_memory: true to character/airton_c1/core.yaml (character-level flag, default false for other characters).
2. Extend harness.character.Character to expose the flag.
3. In run_tool_loop (or CLI call site), when flag is set, inject a synthetic search_memory tool call with the latest user message as args BEFORE round 0. Execute via the normal tool registry path. Append assistant-toolcall + tool-result messages to working history.
4. Model then enters round 0 with corpus text in context, not weights-only.
5. Grounding signal registers with the UngroundedCitationHook (tools_ran=search_memory), so the new catcher correctly treats the turn as grounded.

Follows bd bead harness-oc8 (UngroundedCitationHook) and the broader airton_c1 retrieval-bias program (harness-rhto / harness-7ph5 / harness-8zx6).

title: atc eval: deterministic temperature for stable baseline
description:
Phase-1 baseline runs at temperature=0.3 show ~±4-case variance per run (18% of the 22-case fixture). This dominates any single-change delta from lanes A/B/C/D — a +1-case win is invisible inside ±4-case noise.

Impact: can't measure which lane-D changes worked. Any tuning decision is indistinguishable from resampling.

Two candidate fixes:
- Set default temperature to 0.0 (greedy decoding) in 'harness eval atc'. Makes per-run output deterministic modulo MLX kernel noise. Easy.
- Add --n-runs N flag; run each case N times, report pass-rate as median or best-of-N. Honest but 5-10x slower on MLX.

My bet: ship --temperature 0.0 as default. MLX at temp=0 on a 22-case eval should be run-to-run identical. If a case has inherent ambiguity (model sometimes says X, sometimes Y), resolve via fixture alternates rather than sampling. This is an eval harness, not a voice vibe test.

Work:
1. src/harness/cli.py — change eval_atc's temperature default from 0.3 to 0.0 (keep --temperature flag for callers who want variance).
2. Run eval twice at temp=0.0 and verify pass-rate is identical run-to-run.
3. Lock that number in as the stable Phase-1 baseline; all subsequent lane work measures against it.

Gate: two consecutive eval runs at default flags produce identical case-pass sets.
notes:
Deterministic eval shipped.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- src/harness/cli.py eval_atc — temperature default 0.3 → 0.0; added --rewriter-temperature flag (default 0.0) threaded through _resolve_adapter → PersonaAdapter.
- _resolve_adapter now accepts optional rewriter_temperature kwarg; only overrides PersonaAdapter when set, preserving chat default (0.2).

VERIFICATION:
Two consecutive MLX eval runs at default flags:
- Pass-rate: 14/22 = 63.6% on both runs.
- Reply-text diff across cases: 0 / 22 (bit-identical replies).
- Hash-identical results confirm greedy decoding is deterministic on our MLX setup.

LOCKED-IN BASELINE: 63.6% (14/22). PPL 7/11, IFR 7/11. This becomes the honest Phase-1 number; any future lane work can see +1/-1 case deltas as signal, not noise.

RE-CALIBRATION: the noisy temp=0.3 history runs (54.5 → 63.6 → 72.7 → 63.6) were 3 samples from a distribution with ~±4 case variance. Lanes A/B/C/D's true cumulative lift is +9.1 pp (54.5 → 63.6 stable), not the +18.2 I was reporting after run 4. Run 4 was the outlier.

STABLE FAILURES (8 at temp=0):
- ppl_vfr_cloud_clearance_above_10k: factual error
- ppl_preflight_action: cite miss
- ppl_pic_responsibility: kw hits
- ppl_readback_basics: rewriter drops AIM 4-4-7 (harness-cco)
- ifr_takeoff_minimums_part_91: cite miss
- ifr_vfr_on_top: kw hits
- ifr_instrument_currency: kw hits
- ifr_descent_below_mda: kw hits

Path to 80% = +4 more flips. harness-cco gives 1 certain flip. Remaining 3 need per-case triage against the now-deterministic replies.

Quality gates: ruff clean, mypy strict (166 files), pytest 1118 passed.
close_reason: Eval default temperature 0.3 → 0.0 + rewriter-temperature flag. 2x consecutive runs produce bit-identical output across all 22 cases. Stable baseline locked at 63.6% (14/22). Future per-change deltas are now measurable signal, not ±4-case resample noise.

title: atc lane C: diagnose 3 factual-error retrieval cases
description:
Phase-1 baseline (atc_baseline.md) surfaced 3 cases where retrieval brought wrong content — not a form issue, a substance issue:

1. ppl_vfr_cloud_clearance_above_10k: model said 'cloud clearance requirement is not applicable above 10,000 MSL' — factually wrong. Either 91.155(a) table row missing from atc's corpus, or retrieval didn't rank it, or model hallucinated despite retrieval.
2. ppl_preflight_action: cited §91.4(a); reply mentions 'control links' and 'TFR compliance' — UAS / drone-ops shape, not PPL preflight. §91.103 should have been top retrieval.
3. ifr_takeoff_minimums_part_91: cited §91.155 + §91.179 instead of §91.175. Topic confusion.

Work:
- For each question, pull top-5 retrieved episodic rows:
    HARNESS_CHARACTER_NAME=airton_c HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
      uv run harness memory search "<question>" --k 5
- Classify the miss: (a) row not in corpus, (b) row in corpus but ranked poorly, (c) row ranked high but model ignored it.
- Likely candidate fixes by class:
  (a) Chunker filter dropped the row — check atc-5 and atc-6 filters; maybe §91.103 body was too short after cleanup, or the table in §91.155(a) split weirdly.
  (b) UAS content in Part 107/Part 89 (CFR Title 14 vol 2) dominated the 'preflight' semantic space. Consider per-source tagging + a retrieval weight that prefers Part 61/91 for PPL queries, or drop Part 107/89 from atc's corpus (they're not in Phase-1 priority anyway).
  (c) Model ignored correct retrieval — look at whether the memory block made it into the system prompt; may need to strengthen the 'cite from memory block' instruction in atc's constitution.
- Land a fix for at least the VFR cloud clearance case (highest-value PPL fact).

Also the top-K for queries like 'preflight action' STILL don't surface §91.103 at #1 — it's buried by AIM/PHAK rows on related topics. But the model now has access to the right content and the wrong content is absent.

title: atc-7: atc_eval.yaml + 'eval atc' subcommand
description:

title: atc-5: section-aware chunker → episodic JSONL
description:
Section-aware chunker that turns extracted markdown into retrieval-ready rows. Input: character/airton_c/corpus/markdown/*.md. Output: character/airton_c/corpus/chunks/<doc_slug>.jsonl (one row per addressable section or merged-sibling block).

Row shape (ingest target for EpisodicStore tier='seed', user_id=NULL):
{
  'source': 'JO_7110.65BB' | 'AIM' | 'PCG' | 'PHAK' | 'CFR_14_61' | 'CFR_14_91',
  'chapter': '2',
  'section': '2-6-4',
  'title': 'ISSUING WEATHER AND CHAFF AREAS',
  'text': '...paragraph text with the section anchor embedded for retrieval fidelity...',
  'parent_section': '2-6',
  'principle': '<mapped to airton_c taxonomy>'
}

Parsing per source:
- JO 7110.65 / AIM: section anchors are N-N-N (e.g., 2-6-4). Parse markdown heading trail.
- PCG: term-per-entry, use term as 'section', empty 'chapter'.
- CFR Title 14: Part → Subpart → § §N.NNN. Use § number as section.
- PHAK: chapter-based; section is chapter/sub-heading.

Size target: aim for 400-1200 char chunks (retrieval sweet spot). Merge short sibling blocks under the same section; split long ones on paragraph boundaries with an 80-char overlap for continuity.

Contextual chunking header (matches existing episodic embed-text convention): '[source: JO_7110.65BB; chapter: 2; section: 2-6-4]\n<body>'.

Acceptance: sample 10 rows and verify each has a well-formed anchor, and the body contains readable text (not Unicode-escaped nonsense, no page-number noise).

Depends on atc-4. Blocks atc-6.
notes:
Chunker shipped; Phase-1 corpus chunked to JSONL. IMPLEMENTATION: - scripts/atc_chunk.py (~570 LOC) — heading-stack walker + per-source parsers + size shaper. Four parser kinds: 'numbered' (AIM/JO 7110.65), 'cfr' (CFR Title 14 §N.M), 'glossary' (PCG), 'phak'. Pure function chunk_markdown(md, cfg) → list[Chunk]. - Contextual header per row: [source: X; chapter: Y; section: Z]\n. ASCII hyphen in section anchors (normalised from U+2212 in source). - Size shaper splits > 1200 char bodies on paragraph boundaries with 80-char overlap, indexed via chunk_index. Short bodies pass through. - Page-noise filter: dates (2/20/25), solo section numbers, short doc-name footers (AIM/PCG/Pilot's Handbook/14 CFR Ch.), orphan page numbers. - Argparse CLI: --only SLUG, --force, --input, --output, --sample N, --seed S. TESTS (17 new, all green): - _iter_blocks segmentation - _strip_wrappers (markdown emphasis) - _clean_body (noise drop + blank collapse) - _parse_numbered: unicode-minus normalisation, explanation-prefix stripping, chapter tracking, empty-body skip - _parse_cfr: §N.M capture - _parse_glossary: letter-as-chapter, frontmatter skip (PURPOSE / EXPLANATION OF CHANGES) - _split_oversized: pass-through, paragraph-split with overlap - _expand_by_size: chunk_index indexing - Chunk.text contextual header (full + minimal) - write_jsonl roundtrip pyproject: ruff per-file-ignores for RUF001/002/003 on atc_chunk + test_atc_chunk — U+2212 in regex + docstring is the point. OUTPUT (character/airton_c/corpus/chunks/, gitignored): pcg.jsonl — 516 rows aim.jsonl — 802 rows jo_7110_65.jsonl — 738 rows phak.jsonl — 2,391 rows cfr_14_vol1.jsonl — 3,350 rows cfr_14_vol2.jsonl — 2,037 rows Total: 9,834 rows. ACCEPTANCE — sampled 10 random rows (--seed 42): - Anchors well-formed: CFR (25.331, 5-4-8, 45.11, 33.72, 25.1153, 23.2600, 21.41), AIM (5-4-8), JO 7110.65 sections via spot-check (1-1-1, 2-6-4, 5-4-10). - Bodies readable; no page-header / date / solo-section-number noise reached the chunks. - ASCII hyphens throughout; U+2212 successfully normalised in metadata (original bodies preserve source chars, which is fine for keyword retrieval). KNOWN PHASE-1 GAPS (not blocking; file as follow-ups when retrieval signals demand): - PCG: pymupdf4llm doesn't emit a ## heading per glossary term — some terms (AAM, ABEAM, ABORT, etc.) land in the body of a sibling term's chunk. Bodies still contain the individual definitions so keyword-BM25 hits; only the 'section' metadata is less precise. - JO 7110.65 / AIM: each doc ships with an 'Explanation of Changes' block that re-states every touched anchor's section number. Results in duplicate section IDs across chunks (change-description row + real-content row). Downstream ingest can dedup by (section, body_hash) if necessary. - PHAK: unnumbered subheadings → parser falls back to chapter-level granularity. Some
HTML artifacts leak through for list-heavy chapters. Quality gates: ruff clean, mypy strict (165 files), pytest 1074 passed / 3 env-gated skips. BLOCKS unblocked: atc-6 (ingest) and atc-7 (eval).
close_reason: Section-aware chunker shipped; 9,834 chunks across 6 docs with normalised anchors, contextual headers, and page-noise filtering. 17 new tests green (1074 total). Known PCG / change-block / PHAK gaps noted for atc-6 dedup or retrieval tuning as signals demand.

title: Self-introspection: agent can describe its own abilities, tools, commands, and limits
description:
Give the agent first-class awareness of its own capabilities so it can answer 'what can you do?', 'what tools do you have?', 'what's your context window?', 'who are you connected to?' accurately instead of hallucinating.

Scope:
- Abilities: currently-loaded tool set (resolved from profile + add/drop), per-tool name + one-line purpose + write-tier flag.
- Model surface: adapter backend (mlx/ollama/echo), model repo, LoRA path if any, context window, tokens used / remaining this session.
- Memory surface: episodic + semantic counts, last consolidation time, seeded memories count, current embedder id + dim.
- Character surface: character name, loaded personae, voice sample count (canonical + captured).
- CLI commands: the same reference that lives in CLAUDE.md / docs/usage.md, but sourced from the Typer app itself so it can't drift.
- Limits/taboos: what it will refuse, what it can't do yet (e.g. no web unless web tool loaded).

Implementation sketch:
- A read-only 'introspect' tool (or set of tools: introspect_tools, introspect_memory, introspect_model, introspect_commands) the agent can call when asked.
- Alternative/additive: a rendered capability block the orchestrator can inject into the system prompt on demand (token-cheap, but staler and always-on).
- Prefer the tool route: keeps the default system prompt lean, the agent only pulls it when the user asks.

Touches: tools/ (new tools + register in profiles), orchestrator/tool_loop.py (no changes if tools follow the existing protocol), character system prompt (maybe a single line: 'If asked what you can do, call introspect_*').

Ties in with harness-7ee (router debug) — introspection could surface router state too.

title: migrate chat CLI to Textual TUI: persistent input + scrolling output + live metrics
description:
Current chat command uses Rich + blocking console.input() as a classic REPL. User wants a chat-app layout: persistent Input widget at the bottom, scrolling output region above, Footer with reactive context meter + elapsed-time metrics.

Approach: Textual (Rich's sister project). Architectural plan:
1. New package src/harness/tui/ with chat_app.py, an  subclass:
   - Header (optional)
   - RichLog (id='output') — append-only scrolling output
   - Input (id='prompt') — persistent bottom input

2. Worker pattern: input submission kicks off a @work task that runs retrieval → persona → tool_loop → scribe. Streaming updates flow back via app.call_from_thread(log.write, …).

- Phase 3: streaming token-delta rendering
- Phase 4: confirmation modal

Classic REPL untouched; --tui is an opt-in alternative.

title: tool loop: short-circuit duplicate tool calls within a turn
description:
Repro: prompt 'review the file structure and summarize its purpose'. Model emits summary prose + list_dir({'path': '', 'recursive': true, 'include_hidden': false}) in the same reply. The orchestrator records the prose as assistant history and executes list_dir. Result unchanged. Model emits another summary + identical list_dir call. Loop continues across rounds, each emitting a duplicate summary and re-running list_dir with the same args, until max_rounds or the small model finally stops. User sees the same prose three times and three identical 🔧 list_dir lines.

Fix: track a per-turn set of (tool_name, canonical-json(args)) in run_tool_loop. When the model re-emits an identical call:
- Skip execution (no re-run).
- Emit a new tool_call_deduped event so the CLI shows it happened but didn't run again.
- Append a tool-role message: '[duplicate call — result unchanged; give the user your final answer now, no more tool calls]' so the model sees the nudge next round.

Also seed the set with the router-prelude call (if any) so a model that re-invokes the router's tool gets short-circuited too.

Tests:
- Same call across two rounds → executed once, deduped second.
- Same call twice in one ModelReply → executed once, deduped second.
- Different args to same tool → both executed.
- Router prelude + model re-invoke → model's call is deduped.

Tradeoff: treats legitimate repeated-poll patterns as redundant. Acceptable at this scale; can add a force=True escape later if a real use case shows up.
close_reason: Implemented duplicate-call short-circuit in orchestrator.tool_loop. Per-turn seen_calls set keyed on (name, json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)). When the model re-emits an identical call: skip execution, emit tool_call_deduped event, append a '[duplicate call — give the user your final answer now]' tool-role message so the next round sees 'stop calling'. Router-prelude call is seeded into the set so the main model can't re-invoke it. CLI renders the dedup as a dim '⇢ name args — duplicate call skipped' line. 6 new tests: across-rounds, same-round, different-args (negative), arg-order-insensitive, router-prelude-seed, CLI render.

title: main model fabricates web-sourced prose after weak router-prelude result
description: Repro (see harness-cx2): 'tell me about origin of Jehovah's Witnesses religion' routes to search_facts (weak hits [~0.36]), then the main model emits prose that reads like web search results without ever calling search_web. The original bug frame was 'TUI hides later tool calls' — investigation showed the orchestrator + CLI renderer both emit/display every call (added 5 regression tests: tests/test_tool_loop.py::test_loop_observer_receives_events_for_{every_round,each_call_in_one_round}; tests/test_cli_helpers.py::test_render_tool_event_*). What actually happened in the repro was pure fabrication: the main model saw low-confidence facts, its 'let me search the web' preamble got eaten by _TOOL_INTENT_RE suppression, and then it continued on to invent well-shaped web-result prose that didn't trip _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE (no numbered 'here are the results', no placeholder domains). Possible mitigations: (a) tighten fabrication regex to catch narrative-style invented facts with named sources; (b) when router-prelude returns low-confidence hits, nudge the main model to explicitly call search_web; (c) raise the router's search_facts min_confidence so weak hits don't anchor a hallucination. Suggest trying (b) first — least invasive.

title: Dim transient agent thoughts/drafts, highlight final reply, show thinking state
description:
Visually separate the agent's in-progress output from its final reply so the user can tell at a glance what's ephemeral vs load-bearing.

Requirements:
- Dim (low-contrast / grey) styling for transient content: tool-call chatter, intermediate drafts, pass-1 substance before rewrite, scratch reasoning.
- Highlight/normal-contrast styling for the final reply (post-rewrite, post-tool-loop).
- Clear 'thinking…' indicator (spinner, pulsing dot, or similar) while the agent is generating but hasn't produced the final reply yet. Should clearly differentiate 'waiting on model' vs 'running a tool' vs 'rewriting voice'.
- Works with streaming: dim while streaming draft tokens, then re-render or restyle on final reply. Decide: restyle in place vs. replace dim block with bright final.

Touches the chat CLI rendering layer (Rich / prompt_toolkit). Coordinate with harness-c93 (always-on prompt) so the styling + thinking indicator don't fight the persistent prompt line.

title: Always-on 'you >' prompt with interrupt + prompt queue + persistent elapsed timer
description:
Keep the 'you >' prompt and cursor visible at all times, including while the agent is generating/working. Two capabilities:

1. Interruptible input while busy:
   - User can type at any time; Enter either interrupts the current turn or enqueues the input as the next prompt (decide UX: maybe Ctrl-C interrupts, Enter queues).
   - Prompt queue: multiple queued items run in order once the agent is free.
   - Visible queue indicator (count of pending prompts).

2. Persistent elapsed-time counter in the context/status line:
   - While working: live-updating elapsed time for the current job.
   - When idle: keeps showing the elapsed time of the most recently completed job (don't blank to zero).
   - Should sit in the existing context/status line alongside token meter.

Requires moving the REPL off blocking input (prompt_toolkit or similar) so stdin + render loop coexist with streaming tokens. Coordinate with compaction/streaming so redraw doesn't clobber the prompt line.

title: grammar extra missing datasets dep (outlines 0.2.3)
description: Running `uv run harness eval router --router-mode grammar` triggers `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'datasets'`. Stack terminates in `outlines/models/transformers.py:117 TransformerTokenizer.__hash__` which does `from datasets.fingerprint import Hasher`. outlines 0.2.3 no longer lists `datasets` transitively, so the `grammar` extra needs to pin it. Every grammar-router classify() hits this because outlines' FSM cache lru_cache's on the tokenizer hash.
close_reason: Added datasets to grammar extra (outlines 0.2.3 TransformerTokenizer.__hash__ imports datasets.fingerprint.Hasher). Also fixed outlines 0.1→0.2 API drift: temperature moved from generate() kwarg to sampler-at-construction. Router grammar eval now runs end-to-end, 80% accuracy, no warning.

title: Pin outlines<1.0 broke the 1.2.12 install; classify silently returned None
description:
uv sync --extra grammar pulled outlines==1.2.12 since the constraint was >=0.1. The v1 rewrite moved outlines.generate.json and outlines.models.mlxlm.MLXLM. MLXAdapter.complete_grammar() raised ImportError -> RuntimeError, GrammarRouter.classify() swallowed it (advisory contract), every call returned Python None, eval scored 40% (every null-expected prompt coincidentally matched).

Fix shipped:
1. Pinned outlines>=0.1,<1.0 in pyproject.toml.
2. GrammarRouter.classify now emits a RuntimeWarning once when the adapter raises, so silent degradation doesn't repeat.

User needs to resync: uv sync --extra dev --extra mlx --extra retrieval --extra grammar
close_reason: Pinned outlines>=0.1,<1.0 in pyproject.toml so the 1.x API drift doesn't land silently. GrammarRouter.classify now warns once via warnings.warn(RuntimeWarning) when the adapter raises, so a totally-broken grammar path surfaces instead of reading as 'every prompt is null-intent'. Test updated to assert warn-once behavior (2 calls -> 1 warning). User needs to: uv sync --extra dev --extra mlx --extra retrieval --extra grammar to pick up 0.x. Follow-on: harness-22f to migrate to outlines 1.x.

title: Grammar-constrained router via outlines + MLX
description:
Add a GrammarRouter that uses outlines + mlx-lm to constrain the router model's output to a JSON schema where tool_name is an enum over the registered tools + null. Guarantees valid JSON and valid tool selection by construction.

Scope:
- Optional dep: grammar extra = outlines>=0.1
- Adapter: MLXAdapter.complete_grammar(messages, schema) — lazy-imports outlines, shares the already-loaded mlx model + tokenizer.
- Protocol: GrammarCapableAdapter structural type.
- Router: src/harness/router/grammar_router.py::GrammarRouter.
- CLI: --router-mode free|grammar on chat + eval router.
- Schema built from ToolSpecs — tool is enum of names + null; arguments is free-form object (post-validated).
- Tests: schema builder unit tests. Real-model integration gated behind HARNESS_TEST_ROUTER_GRAMMAR.

Explicit non-goal: improve router accuracy on the eval fixture. The 4 remaining failures are wrong-choice errors, not validity errors. This adds robustness + future-proofing for args-schema enforcement.
close_reason: GrammarRouter landed. Adds optional 'grammar' extra (outlines>=0.1), MLXAdapter.complete_grammar() that shares the pre-loaded model+tokenizer with outlines, GrammarCapableAdapter Protocol in harness.model.adapter, and src/harness/router/grammar_router.py with build_router_schema() that enums tool names + null. CLI: --router-mode free|grammar on both chat and eval router (default free). 12 new tests for schema building + router wiring via a scripted grammar-capable adapter. Won't improve the 80% eval number (remaining failures are logic errors, not validity errors) — lands as robustness + future-proofing for args-schema enforcement.

title: Router parser: treat string 'null' as Python None
description: Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B sometimes emits {"tool": "null", ...} (literal string) when it means no tool. The parser coerces empty strings to None but not the word 'null' / 'none'. As a result, the eval displays these as null-vs-null in the table (visually identical to a true null match) but scores them as mismatches — the RouterIntent carries tool_name='null' (string) vs expected None.\n\nFix _coerce_intent in src/harness/router/model_router.py to treat the case-folded strings 'null' and 'none' as equivalent to Python None, the same way empty strings are already treated.
close_reason: Parser now folds literal 'null' / 'none' / 'NULL' / '  None  ' strings to Python None in _coerce_intent. Hermes-3-3B sometimes emits the word instead of real JSON null; previously these scored as tool_name='null' (a string) and misfired the eval. 1 new parse test covers the variants.

title: Swap default router model to Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit
description: Router eval on Qwen 2.5 1.5B Instruct 4-bit topped out at 75% on the 20-prompt fixture. Three residual failure modes (read_file→list_dir/glob, 'tell me a joke'→search_web, 'explain a merkle tree'→search_facts) showed model-capability ceiling, not prompt-tuning gap. Swap to a function-call-tuned 3B — Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B — for likely +10-15pp accuracy. ~2GB at 4-bit (~1GB more than the 1.5B), well within RAM headroom. Different tokenizer family than the main Qwen but MLX auto-detects. Update: CLI default, bench default, help text. Re-run eval to confirm.
close_reason: Default router swapped from Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit to Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit across CLI (chat + eval router), bench script, model_router.py module docstring, and chat-header tests. ~2GB at 4-bit, function-call-tuned. All 425 tests still green.

title: Tighten router prompt: explicit null rubric + more few-shots
description:
Router eval (harness eval router) showed 65% accuracy on the 20-prompt fixture. Three failure modes:

1. File-intent collapses to glob — 'show me src/main.py' / 'list src/tests' all picked glob instead of read_file / list_dir. The 1.5B isn't distinguishing CONTENTS (read_file) vs LISTING (list_dir) vs FINDING (glob) vs SEARCHING (grep).
2. 'recall' / 'conversation' under-routed to null — search_memory isn't being picked up.
3. Creative + explanatory prompts over-routed to search_web — 'write a haiku', 'explain a merkle tree', 'tell me a joke' all triggered web search.

Fix: tighten the router system prompt in src/harness/router/model_router.py — add a two-section rubric (when to use a tool / when to return null), add tool-overlap disambiguation notes, and expand few-shots from 2 to 7 covering read_file, list_dir, search_memory, and two null-creative/explanatory variants.

Target: bring fixture accuracy from 65% to 80%+.
close_reason: Router system prompt tightened. Added explicit 'tool needed when…' vs 'return null for…' rubric calling out creative writing / explanations / greetings / opinion as null cases. Added tool-overlap disambiguation notes (CONTENTS / LISTING / FINDING / SEARCHING). Expanded few-shots from 2 to 7: search_web, read_file, list_dir, search_memory, hey, haiku, hash-table. 3 new tests guard the prompt shape. Re-run harness eval router to measure the gain.

title: CLI: --router / --router-repo flags on chat
description:
Add --router/--no-router (default off) and --router-repo (default mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit) to the chat command. When --router is on, build a ModelRouter wrapping a separate MLX adapter instance at the router-repo and pass it into run_tool_loop.

Surface in the loading header: 'router  on · Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit' when enabled, drop the line when off.

Inline: render ToolLoopEvent(kind='router_intent') as a dim label '→ routed to <tool>' just before the tool-call status line.
close_reason: CLI wiring landed. --router/--no-router + --router-repo (default mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit) on chat. Requires --tools (guarded with BadParameter). Builds a second MLXAdapter at router-repo, wraps with ModelRouter, passes into run_tool_loop. Header shows 'router on · <short-repo>' under the tools block. router_intent event rendered inline as magenta '→ routed to <tool>'. 3 new header tests. Next: harness-zgu (eval) + harness-64x (bench).

title: Orchestrator: inject synthetic tool-call when router returns intent
description:
Extend run_tool_loop to accept an optional router: Router | None. Before the first adapter call:
1. If router is None -> current behavior.
2. Else call router.classify(last_user_message, registry.specs()).
3. If intent.tool_name is set AND exists in registry AND args validate against the spec schema -> append a synthetic assistant ChatMessage carrying that ToolCall, execute the tool (via the existing confirm/observe path), append the tool result, then let the main model wrap up.
4. Else (null or validation failure) -> fall through to normal tool loop.

Emit a new ToolLoopEvent kind="router_intent" so CLI can surface 'routed to search_web' inline. Tests cover: happy-path (intent -> tool ran -> wrap-up), null passthrough, bad-schema passthrough, nonexistent-tool passthrough.
close_reason: Orchestrator integration landed. run_tool_loop accepts an optional Router; when it classifies a user turn into a known read-tier tool with all required args present, the orchestrator injects a synthetic assistant ToolCall, runs the tool, and lets the main model wrap up. router_intent event fires once before round 0. Write-tier and malformed intents fall through silently. 7 new integration tests. Ready for harness-t7t (CLI flags).

title: harness eval router — fixture-based routing accuracy eval
description:
Add 'harness eval router' subcommand + character/airton/router_eval.yaml fixture. Each fixture entry: {prompt, expected_tool: str | null, expected_args_schema (optional jsonschema subset)}. Eval runs the router against each prompt and scores:
- Correct tool selection (exact match including null).
- Args validate against schema (when expected_tool non-null).
- Aggregate accuracy + per-tool confusion matrix.

Seed fixture with ~20 prompts covering: search_web triggers ('search the web for X', 'look up Y online'), read_file triggers ('show me foo.py'), search_memory triggers ('what do you remember about Z'), and null cases ('hey, how's it going').

Goal: lock in router quality so a model swap doesn't silently regress.
close_reason: Router eval landed. Fixture at character/airton/router_eval.yaml (20 prompts: search_web, read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, search_memory, search_facts, and 8 null cases).  subcommand + --fixture / --router-repo / --tool-set / --json flags. Scoring separates tool-selection accuracy from args-completeness. 12 new tests including a canonical-fixture guard. Next: harness-64x.

title: Router protocol + ModelRouter implementation
description:
Add src/harness/router/ with:
- intent.py: RouterIntent dataclass (tool_name: str | None, arguments: dict), Router Protocol with classify(user_message, tool_specs) -> RouterIntent | None.
- model_router.py: ModelRouter wrapping a ModelAdapter. Builds a strict-JSON classification prompt: given the user message and tool schemas, emit {"tool": "name", "arguments": {...}} or {"tool": null}. Parses tolerantly (markdown fences, garbage prefix). Returns None on any parse failure — advisory, never raises.

Tests hit a ScriptedAdapter that returns fixed JSON shapes. No MLX in tests.
close_reason: Landed src/harness/router/ with Router protocol, RouterIntent dataclass, ModelRouter implementation, and 23 tests. Parse tolerance mirrors scribe/extractor.py; top-level lists and malformed output return None per the advisory contract. Ready for harness-ut3 (orchestrator integration).

title: Epic: intent router — small-model pre-pass for tool routing
description:
Add a small secondary model (Qwen 2.5 1.5B Instruct 4-bit) that runs BEFORE the main model for every turn and decides tool+args. When it returns an intent, the orchestrator injects a synthetic assistant tool-call turn, executes the tool, and hands the main model a single wrap-up round — no fabrication-and-retry rounds. When it returns null or unparseable, fall through to the normal tool loop.

Locked decisions:
- Router model: mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit (~1GB RAM; same tokenizer family as main Qwen).
- Scope: tool routing only (no persona/skip/meta decisions).
- Advisory not blocking: unparseable output -> fall through, never fail the turn.
- Opt-in via --router flag; default off so we can bench against baseline.

Why now: 7B-4bit fabricates instead of calling search_web (harness-j1d). A small router sidesteps the problem entirely and scales to multi-user gateways without paying 3 rounds of 7B inference per misfire.
close_reason: Intent router epic complete. All five child issues closed: harness-6db (Router + ModelRouter), harness-ut3 (orchestrator integration), harness-t7t (CLI --router flag), harness-zgu (eval fixture + harness eval router), harness-64x (scripts/bench_router.py). Live-tested: user confirmed --router successfully routed 'search the web for bbq' to search_web on first try, no fabrication rounds.

title: Tighten _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE to catch quoted snippet-list fabrications
description: Small models (Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct 4bit) respond to 'search the web for X' by fabricating a numbered list of prose snippets ending in ." rather than calling search_web. The current regex only catches 'here are the results' / 'search results:' / placeholder URLs, so the orchestrator's _diagnose_bail returns None and the fabrication becomes the final reply. Add a pattern for numbered list items whose content ends with a closing quote ("." or unicode equivalent) with no URL — the tell-tale DDG-style HTML-excerpt shape the model imitates when it should be calling the tool.
close_reason: Added a numbered-list-entry pattern to _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE (no URL, ends with ." / !" / ?"). Tempered greedy rules out real search_web output shape. Regression + negative test added.

title: Three UX polish items on the tool-confirm flow
description: Follow-ups to harness-edj/2tq/gni: (1) stream-level meta-confirm suppression (buffer by sentence, drop matches before display); (2) pre-validation in confirm_write_tool — shrink-clobber never reaches the approve prompt; (3) richer approve prompt showing create/overwrite/append/replace intent + byte counts instead of the raw {args} dump.
close_reason: All three landed: (1) _StreamRenderer buffers sentence-level and drops meta-confirm/false-success before display; (2) _pre_validate_write_call gates the approve prompt, shrink-clobber never shown to user; (3) _describe_call summary replaces raw {args} dump — shows create/overwrite/append/replace intent + byte counts. 17 new tests (334 total).

title: Airton hallucinated tool-call success on first attempt
description: In the same .gitignore session, Airton's first turn replied 'scratch is now included' with NO tool call shown in the transcript — pure hallucination. Only after user called the lie out did Airton actually invoke tools. Likely causes: (1) 7B model tool-use reliability, (2) system prompt not emphasizing 'you must actually invoke tools before claiming actions were done', (3) possibly tool-call-parsing quirk that swallowed a call. Investigate logs and tighten the tool-use system prompt. Consider recommending Qwen3-Coder or 32B for heavy-tool sessions.
close_reason: Landed: _FALSE_SUCCESS_RE in orchestrator catches 'has been added / is now included / I've created' claims when no tool ran this turn; tool-session system prompt now explicitly forbids claiming actions without calling a tool. 2 new tests (247 total). Follow-up considered: telemetry counter for bail events to track frequency, but deferred.

Non-goal: don't violate the adapter boundary. Every adapter implements the same complete_with_tools shape. Zero new branches in orchestrator/.

title: Soft wall-clock cap per turn (force wrap-up after N seconds)
description:
Mark's 2026-05-20 GTA2 session ran for ~4100 seconds (~68 minutes) on a single turn before the model gave up and emitted a fabricated success summary. The model never hit the hard_ceiling iteration cap because rounds at expanded budgets (truncated_retry doubling, harness-jly) can each run several minutes at MLX speeds.

There is no wall-clock budget on a turn today. Anything below max_rounds + bail-retry budget can run indefinitely as long as each individual round returns.

## Fix shape

Add a soft turn-level wall-clock cap to run_tool_loop:
- New parameter `turn_wall_clock_budget_s: float | None = None` — None preserves today's behavior.
- The orchestrator records turn_start_time at loop entry.
- Before each model round, if monotonic time since start exceeds the budget AND any tool has succeeded this turn, force a wrap-up round (same path harness-0gss already uses for max_rounds exhaustion). Tools_ran_this_turn=False means no useful work has been done — better to halt with an honest "I didn't make any progress in N minutes" message than to wrap up nothing.
- Emit a new ToolLoopEvent kind 'wall_clock_wrap_up' so the CLI/TUI renders something visible like "⋯ N minutes elapsed, forcing wrap-up…".

Default: None (off) until the value is tuned. Suggested first value: 300s (5 minutes) — long enough for legitimate multi-step coding tasks, short enough that a runaway loop tops out before the user has to interrupt.

## Acceptance

- New test: scripted adapter that sleeps via clock injection, asserts wrap-up fires when budget exceeded and at least one tool ran.
- New test: budget exceeded but no tools ran → loop continues to its normal max_rounds termination (no spurious wrap-up over an empty turn).
- New ToolLoopEvent kind covered by an event-emission test.
- Existing tests stay green; param defaults to None so behavior is unchanged for sessions that don't opt in.

## Wiring

- Add CLI flag `--turn-wall-clock-budget` (default unset).
- Plumb through ChatSession / ChatApp into the run_tool_loop call.

## Out of scope

- Per-tool wall-clock budgets (a slow tool shouldn't kill a turn if other tools are fast). Tools already have their own per-call timeouts.
- Interrupting an in-flight model call when the budget expires. Mid-generation cancellation belongs to a different feature; this cap fires at iteration boundaries only, same as max_rounds.

## Related

harness-0gss (wrap-up-forced infrastructure this reuses). harness-jly (truncated_retry budget doubling — what made 68 min possible). The new bd for post-duplicate fabrication catcher (P1) addresses the immediate failure shape this would have bounded.

title: truncated_retry marker should show budget progression
description:
When the orchestrator emits a 'truncated_retry' event, the TUI / classic REPL renders just '⋯ truncated, retrying with wider budget…' — no number. A user watching the stream sees the same preamble re-stream three times before the retry budget exhausts, with no way to tell from the log alone whether the model produced 1024 useful tokens then got clipped on a tail (healthy use of retry) or burned the whole budget on intent-restatement preamble three times (pathological — model never gets to a tool call or final answer).

Proposal: include the budget progression in the marker so the pathology is visible inline. Two shapes worth considering:

  ⋯ truncated, retrying with wider budget (1024 → 2048)…
  ⋯ truncated, retrying with wider budget (2048 → 4096)…
  ⋯ truncated, retrying with wider budget (4096; ceiling)…

Implementation sketch:
- ToolLoopEvent already has unused payload room. Add a 'budget_before' / 'budget_after' pair to the truncated_retry emit at tool_loop.py:1250, populated from _BailController state before/after on_truncated().
- _render_tool_event in chat_app.py and cli_classic.py (and the _StreamRenderer in cli.py) read the new fields and append the parenthetical.
- When the doubled budget hits _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING, render the ceiling annotation instead of the arrow.

Out of scope: changing the retry policy itself. This is diagnostic-only.

Motivating real-session example (2026-05-20, Mark): three identical 'I need to implement the full GTA2 clone according to the spec…' preambles streamed before the retry budget exhausted. With budget annotations the user would have seen 1024 → 2048 → 4096 and known immediately the model never reached useful output — none of the three streams were 'close to done', they were all wasted preamble.

Related: harness-6rl (original truncated-retry plumbing), harness-jly (the both-caps doubling fix this would now surface).
close_reason: Added budget_before/budget_after fields to ToolLoopEvent on truncated_retry. Shared format_truncated_retry_suffix helper renders '(1024 → 2048)' on normal doubling and '(N; ceiling)' when on_truncated() clamped at _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING. Both renderers (cli.py + tui/chat_app.py) use the same helper so they stay in sync. 3 new tests; 2957 total pass; ruff + mypy clean.

title: core_minimal is wrong default for doc-review/multi-file research tasks
description:
core_minimal (tool_search + load_tool + introspect) is optimized for long conversational sessions where most turns don't need a tool. For multi-file research turns ('review the docs at /docs/gta and write a plan'), it forces the agent to round-trip through tool_search → load_tool just to get list_dir + read_file loaded — wasted rounds, and small models thrash on the family-vs-tag distinction along the way.

Repro: airton session on core_minimal asked to review docs/gta/spec/*.md. Took 8+ tool calls before read_file was loaded, never actually opened the spec before context ran out.

Options to investigate (don't pick one without measurement):
  A. Router-side: when intent looks like 'open/read these files' (or workspace path mentioned), have the router pre-load read_file + list_dir before round 0. Cheaper than a profile change; respects core_minimal's purpose for non-tool turns.
  B. Profile-side: ship a new profile (e.g. 'core_lite') that's core_minimal + read_file + list_dir + grep. Adds ~400 tokens; still well under core's 1500-token target.
  C. Discovery-side: ship the tag→family auto-rescue + schema-ordering fixes first, measure whether the round-trip cost on core_minimal is acceptable. Maybe the profile is fine and the discovery primitives just need to be more forgiving.

Acceptance: measure tokens-per-task on docs/gta-style prompts under each option (bench_tool_use.py). Pick the option that hits ≥80% of core's success rate with ≤60% of core's schema tokens.

Blocked on: the three tool_search fixes (file: tag→family auto-rescue; family-over-tag schema; empty-result hint). Re-evaluate after those land.

title: tool_search: empty-result hint should name the family when tag value matches a family
description:
The empty-result recovery hint (tool_search.py:248-261) teaches capability-shaped queries in general, but it doesn't catch the specific 'you passed tag=X where X is a family' mistake.

Concrete addition: when the constraints include tag=<X> and X is in the set of registered families, prepend the recovery hint with a pointed line: 'NOTE: "X" is a FAMILY name, not a tag. Retry with family="X" (or omit the filter and rely on query=).'

This is a smaller, lower-risk version of the auto-rescue — if we don't ship auto-rescue, at least the model is told exactly how to fix its next call. If we DO ship auto-rescue, this hint never fires because the auto-rescue beats it to the punch (good).

Files: src/harness/tools/tool_search.py call() — lines 234-261.
close_reason: Closed

title: tool_search 'N of M' result count is confusing when limit < candidates
description:
Session repro 2026-05-19: model called tool_search twice in one turn:
  tool_search(query='kenya national flower', tag='search', limit=1)  -> '1 of 7'
  tool_search(query='kenya national flower', tag='search', limit=10) -> '7 of 7'

Same query / same catalog — only `limit` changed. The 'N of M' header reads like the catalog gained tools between calls, which it didn't. M is the candidates-pool size; N is how many were rendered (capped by limit). The two are unrelated to catalog mutation.

Mild but real UX nit. Two non-mutually-exclusive fixes:

(1) Rephrase the header. Instead of '{N} of {M} tool(s)' surface something less ambiguous when N < M:
    - '{N} shown of {M} matching (raise --limit to see more)'
    - '{M} matched; showing {N}'
The current line is fine when N == M. The ambiguity is the unequal case.

(2) Default a higher limit. The model passed limit=1 for the first call — that's not a useful discovery shape. Either:
    - Document in the tool description that limit defaults to 10 and lower values are usually wrong.
    - Make limit=1 require explicit opt-in by clamping below 3 to 3 (or warn).

(2) feels like over-engineering. (1) is the right ROI.

Acceptance:
- tool_search header rephrased so the N != M case isn't read as 'the catalog grew'.
- Existing test_output_caps_at_limit_with_overflow_marker assertion updated to match new header text.
- Smoke test pinning the new phrasing for the limit < candidates case AND the limit >= candidates case (so the format covers both).

title: search_web: DDG geolocates results to caller's IP, breaks non-local queries
description:
Mark in Phoenix, AZ asked 'weather at RJTA' (a Japanese airport ICAO). search_web returned weather for Chandler, AZ — DDG personalized to the caller's IP. The agent then took the Chandler result as authoritative and got confused.

This is DDG's HTML endpoint behavior: without an explicit region param, it geolocates. Fix: pass kl=wt-wt (worldwide, no localization) or similar.

Investigation:
  - Test DDG with different kl= values to confirm wt-wt avoids geolocation.
  - Consider whether characters with default_site_filter need different defaults.

Acceptance:
  - 'weather at RJTA' from a Phoenix IP returns RJTA-relevant results (not Phoenix-area weather).
  - 'mlx 32B quantization' still returns the same tech results (no regression on non-geographic queries).
  - 1-2 tests with monkeypatched DDG response to pin the URL/query params we pass.

title: tool-registry: load_tool meta-tool — agent-driven working-set expansion
description:
The missing companion to tool_search (harness-ozx1). tool_search lets the agent DISCOVER tools beyond the current working set; load_tool lets it ACTUALLY USE them by expanding the working set mid-session.

Today the working set (harness-fzvg) is frozen at session start via the CLI: --tool-set + --tools-add. The agent can call tool_search and learn that calc exists, but on the next round its chat-template tool list still doesnt include calc, so it cant emit the call. Closing this gap is what unlocks minimal-core profiles, runtime synthesized tools (yari), and the agentic discovery flow.

Tool shape:
  name: load_tool
  tier: read  (read-only catalog lookup + registry mutation; no fs/network)
  description: "Add a tool from the catalog to this sessions active working set so you can call it on subsequent rounds. Use after tool_search reveals a tool that fits your need. Returns the tools spec preview + confirmation; subsequent rounds will see the tools schema in the chat template."
  parameters:
    name: str — catalog entry name to load
  output: spec preview + "now active" confirmation, OR a clear error pointing at tool_search if the name isnt in the catalog

Critical: the orchestrator must re-render the tool schema for the round AFTER load_tool fires. Today run_tool_loop builds the schema once at round 0 and reuses it. The fix is per-round schema re-rendering when the registrys working set changed since the last round — a small flag on the registry + a check in the loop.

Acceptance:
  - load_tool successfully looks up a name in the catalog, registers the tool instance into the registry if needed, adds it to the working set
  - Next round sees the new tools schema
  - Unknown name: clear error, no mutation
  - Already-active tool: no-op + clear confirmation
  - Catalog-only synthesized tool that hasnt been hot-loaded: returns a pointer-at-rqg0.5 error
  - 6-8 unit tests + 1 orchestrator integration test (mock adapter that asserts the schema grew between rounds)
  - Pre-commit clean

Once load_tool ships, document the minimal-core profile shape:
  core_minimal: [tool_search, load_tool, introspect]
  ~500 token schema; agent does discovery -> load -> call across 2-3 rounds.

Depends on rqg0.1 (catalog), rqg0.2 (working-set), rqg0.6 (tool_search). Independent of synthesis (yari) and hot-reload (t5kx) for actively-registered tools. For synthesized tools awaiting hot-load, this slice points back at t5kx.

title: tool-registry: tool_search meta-tool — discovery primitive
description:
Slice 6 of harness-rqg0. The agents discovery primitive: "given a need, find tools that fit." Cheap, read-tier, in every profile so it is always-available without filling the schema budget.

ToolSpec:
  name: tool_search
  tier: read
  description: "Find tools by keyword query, tag, or family. Returns name + family + description + tags. Use this to discover capability before fabricating an answer; if no tool fits, say so."
  parameters:
    query: str (substring matched against name + description + tags)
    tag: str | None (additional filter)
    family: str | None (additional filter)
    limit: int = 10

Output: a compact text list, similar in feel to search_memory results:
  - name (family) — description excerpt
    tags: [a, b, c]

Implementation: queries the ToolCatalog (rqg0.1). No model call required. Cap at ~200 token equivalents per result; truncate long descriptions; cap to limit entries.

Why this is load-bearing for grouping/discoverability: today the agents only know about tools that are in the rendered schema this turn. With a large persistent library + working-set selection, the agent needs a way to learn about tools it didnt receive in the schema this turn — tool_search fills that gap.

Acceptance:
  - Returns matching entries by name / description / tag / family
  - Result compact: <250 tokens for a typical 5-result return
  - Empty result has a clear no-tools-found line
  - 6-8 tests with a fixtured catalog (mix of builtin + synthesized entries)
  - Pre-commit clean

Depends on rqg0.1 (catalog).

Output compact text list with name + family + description excerpt + tags. Registry plumbing prefers live spec descriptions over catalog seeded ones. Wired into both cli.py + cli_classic.py builder dicts with fresh per-session seeded catalogs. tool_search itself listed in BUILTIN_TOOL_METADATA (family=meta, tags=read+discovery+search+catalog) so it's discoverable via itself. 21 unit tests. title: tool-registry: synthesize_tool meta-tool (write-tier)
description:
Slice 4 of harness-rqg0. The meta-tool the AGENT calls to author + register a new tool. Write-tier (per-session confirm required). Lives in src/harness/tools/synth.py.

ToolSpec:
  name: synthesize_tool
  tier: write
  description: "Author a new tool at runtime. Provide a Python module that defines a Tool class with a ToolSpec, then a smoke-test input. The candidate is validated in a sandbox before being persisted to the catalog. Use this when an existing tool would not fit the need and the new shape would be reusable."
  parameters:
    name: str (the new tool name)
    source: str (Python module source)
    family: str
    tags: list[str]
    smoke_args: dict (test arguments for one call)

Flow:
  1. Validate via rqg0.3 (sandbox)
  2. On valid: write source to character/<name>/tools/synthesized/<name>.py
  3. Add catalog entry (rqg0.1)
  4. Return success + new tool name + smoke_output

Constraints:
  - Per-session confirm (write-tier) — first invocation prompts the user
  - Refuses if a tool with the same name already exists in the catalog (require explicit drop first)
  - Records origin=synthesized + registered_at
  - The new tool is NOT hot-loaded into the current session — rqg0.5 handles that

Acceptance:
  - Valid synth call -> catalog entry created + file written
  - Invalid source -> no catalog mutation, error returned to model
  - Name collision -> error pointing at drop_tool
  - Write-tier confirm wiring exercised by an integration test
  - 6-8 tests including the rqg0.3 validator path
  - Pre-commit clean

title: tool-registry: Tool sandbox validator (Python module compile + test-call)
description:
Slice 3 of harness-rqg0. The validator the synthesis meta-tool (rqg0.4) calls before promoting a candidate tool into the catalog. Pure-Python; same subprocess + import-allowlist pattern as python_eval.

Function:
  validate_tool_module(*, source: str, smoke_args: dict[str, Any] | None,
                        allowed_imports: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> ValidationResult

ValidationResult:
  ok: bool
  spec: ToolSpec | None  (parsed from the module if compile succeeds)
  smoke_output: str | None (the test-call result if it ran)
  error: str | None (compile / contract / smoke failure)

Validation steps:
  1. Write `source` to a tmp file
  2. Spawn subprocess (python -I -B -S like python_eval) with the import allowlist; load the module
  3. Verify module exposes a single top-level Tool subclass (or duck-typed Tool: spec property + call method)
  4. Verify spec has name + description + parameters + tier
  5. If smoke_args provided: call the tool with them, capture output
  6. Return ValidationResult

Sandbox boundaries:
  - allowed_imports is conservative: stdlib subset (json, math, re, datetime, statistics) + harness.tools.base (for ToolSpec) only
  - Subprocess RLIMIT_AS + wall-clock timeout (same as python_eval)
  - Source size cap (e.g. 8 KB)

Acceptance:
  - Valid tool with ToolSpec.name + .description + .parameters + .tier + call() -> ValidationResult.ok=True
  - Missing ToolSpec attr -> ok=False with clear error
  - Banned import -> ok=False
  - smoke call that raises -> ok=False with the exception
  - 8-10 tests including the import-allowlist enforcement
  - Pre-commit clean

Depends on no other rqg0 sub-beads (independent foundation).
close_reason: shipped: src/harness/tools/sandbox_validator.py with validate_tool_module() + ValidationResult; 11 tests covering compile + spec + smoke + import allowlist + size cap. commit 1df7445.

title: tool-registry: ToolRegistry working-set + tag-based selection
description:
Slice 2 of harness-rqg0. Today ToolRegistry only knows about tools that are registered (active by default). Extend so it knows about MORE tools than it renders schemas for per turn — the catalog is the superset, the working set is what the model sees.

API extensions:
  ToolRegistry.set_active(names: Iterable[str]) -> None
      Subset of registered tools rendered by specs() this turn.
  ToolRegistry.active_names() -> tuple[str, ...]
  ToolRegistry.specs() filters to active_names (existing call site unchanged for full-active case)
  ToolRegistry.estimate_active_schema_tokens(tokenizer) -> int
      Convenience for budget checks; uses the same heuristic as test_reckon_schema_budget_under_target.

Selection helpers (compose on top of working set):
  resolve_active(*, profile: str, names: tuple[str, ...] = (), tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> set[str]
      Combines profile lookup + explicit names + tag-filter. Replaces a piece of the existing resolve_tool_names() + complements --tools-add.

Acceptance:
  - set_active({a, b}) makes specs() return only those two
  - active subset survives further register() calls (new tools register but stay inactive)
  - active=None / full-active default keeps existing behavior unchanged
  - tag-based selection uses CatalogEntry.tags (rqg0.1)
  - Compatibility: every existing test that calls registry.specs() still passes
  - 6-8 new tests + audit of existing tool-loop tests for breakage
  - Pre-commit clean

Depends on rqg0.1 (catalog provides tag metadata).

ToolRegistry gained set_active / clear_active / active_names; specs() filters to working set when set, default all-active behavior unchanged. set_active drops unregistered names silently (catalog-level working sets can reference tools the session didn't register). Tools registered after set_active stay inactive (frozen-at-call-time semantics). call() still works on inactive tools — working set is model-visibility, not sandbox. New resolve_active(catalog, profile, names, tags, families) in profiles.py unions three selection layers; catalog typed as object to avoid import cycle. 19 unit tests covering working-set semantics + resolve_active permutations + end-to-end registry wiring.   - tags: tuple[str, ...] — keywords for discovery (math, dates, fs-read, fs-write, llm-search, ...)

ToolCatalog API:
  load(path) -> ToolCatalog | empty
  save(catalog, path) atomic write
  register(entry: CatalogEntry) -> None (in-memory mutation)
  drop(name) -> None
  by_tag(tag) -> list[CatalogEntry]
  by_family(family) -> list[CatalogEntry]
  search(query) -> list[CatalogEntry] (substring match against name + description + tags)
  all() -> list[CatalogEntry]

Acceptance:
